chapters.title: Chapter 1851: Power of Stars!
paragraphs: Two beams of light descended from above.
Orion Starfall appeared on one side of the central stage, his dark gold armor reflecting the flowing rivers of time-light that streamed above the Eternal Hourglass.

The nine star marks on his body glowed faintly, not yet fully awakened, but bright enough to make him look as though he carried a small night sky within his own flesh. His expression remained composed, and his familiar smile still rested on his face, though the easy playfulness in his eyes had noticeably thinned.

Revona appeared opposite him. She stood quietly with a relaxed posture, her eyes half open while a faint void-colored light flickered within her pupils. Compared to Orion’s radiant aura of stars, she felt almost silent, yet that very silence was what made her so dangerous. Her Void Origin Eyes had already nullified far too many attacks for anyone present to take her lightly.
For a moment, neither of them attacked.
Orion studied her with interest and asked, "Before we begin, may I ask you something?"
Revona’s expression did not shift. "Ask."
"Is there truly a way to bypass the ability of your Void Origin Eyes?"
The question made several participants lean in with sharper focus. Revona’s eyes flickered slightly, and then she nodded. "Yes."
The answer sent a ripple of surprise across the pillars.
Orion’s eyebrows rose. "There is?"
Revona turned her gaze toward one particular pillar, where Max stood in silence. Orion followed her line of sight.
Revona said calmly, "One individual managed to do so in the past."
Orion paused before asking, "Who?"
Her answer was simple. "Max."
The arena went quiet for the space of a breath, and then many gazes swung toward Max all at once. His expression remained calm, as though the matter had nothing to do with him at all.

He had defeated Revona once before, but he understood perfectly well that the Revona standing on the stage now was no longer the same woman he had fought back then. Her Void Origin Eyes had awakened further since that day, and her power to nullify attacks had grown far smoother and far more complete.
Orion stared at Max for a moment, then shook his head with a wry smile. "Of course it would be him."
A few of the participants wore complicated expressions after hearing it.
Rakan Thorne chuckled softly from his pillar. "That guy really is everywhere."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly. "At this point, I would be more surprised if Max had not done it."
Kaiden Voidmere looked toward Max with thoughtful eyes, while Damian Voss said nothing at all.
Orion turned his attention back to Revona and exhaled lightly. "Then I suppose I will have to find my own way."
Revona opened her eyes fully, and void-colored light spread through her pupils. "You can try."
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]

Orion moved first, though he did not rush forward. In truth, he showed no intention of entering close combat at all. As the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court, Orion Starfall rarely fought with fists, blades, or techniques of short range.

His strength lived among the stars. His attacks descended from above, crossed vast distances as beams of light, and overwhelmed opponents through precision, sheer numbers, and celestial pressure. He was a long-range fighter by his very nature, and nearly all of his methods were built around commanding the battlefield from afar.

One star mark on his body lit up, and a single beam of starlight dropped from above the stage. It was thin, bright, and fast enough to arrive before most people could even react. The beam shot toward Revona’s shoulder, and it was clearly intended as a probe rather than a genuine killing blow.
Revona looked at it, and the beam vanished. There was no explosion, no resistance, and no sound of any kind. It simply ceased to exist the instant it entered the range of her gaze.

Orion showed no surprise. A second star mark lit up, and this time two beams of starlight descended from different angles, one aimed at Revona’s left side while the other curved around toward her back. Their paths were clean and precise, designed to force her to either turn or defend in two directions at once.
Revona’s eyes shifted. The first beam vanished, and then the second followed it into nothing.
Orion smiled faintly. "So two is not enough."

Three star marks lit up, and then five, and then ten. The sky above the central stage darkened as ten points of starlight bloomed in the air. Each point released a beam, and the ten beams descended together like divine arrows loosed from the night sky.

Nor did they travel in straight lines alone. Some curved, some split apart, some accelerated at the halfway mark, and some delayed themselves by a fraction of a breath so they might strike after the first wave had been erased.

Revona stood without moving as her Void Origin Eyes shone brighter. Wherever her gaze swept, the star beams winked out one after another. Some vanished long before reaching her, some disappeared mere inches from her body, and some were erased in the middle of their curving flight, leaving behind nothing but faint ripples of empty space.
The ten-star attack failed.

Orion raised his hand, and a hundred stars appeared. The entire arena brightened. Many participants narrowed their eyes as one hundred points of starlight took shape above the stage and surrounded Revona from every direction.

The pressure of this attack belonged to an entirely different order than what had come before. Each star carried a compressed beam, and together they wove a vast celestial net that left almost no gap through which to escape.
"Nine Star Court. Hundred Star Descent."

The one hundred beams fell, and for a moment the stage looked as though an entire starry sky were collapsing upon it. Spectators across the Divine Realm held their breath. The attack was grand, beautiful, and terrifying all at once.
Every beam carried enough force to punch through a formidable defense, and with one hundred descending in unison, the pressure was enough to make even some of the top geniuses treat it with respect.

Revona finally moved, though she went neither backward nor forward. She simply turned slowly in place while her Void Origin Eyes glowed like two entrances into nothingness. The first twenty beams vanished, then forty, then seventy, and then all one hundred.
The entire Hundred Star Descent was erased before a single beam could touch her.

chapters.title: Chapter 1852: A Bad Match Up?
paragraphs: The arena fell silent, and Orion’s smile grew more serious.
He lifted both hands. The nine star marks across his body brightened in unison, and the space above the arena transformed into a vast night sky teeming with countless small stars.
At first there were hundreds, then a thousand, and then several thousand more. The starlight gathered so densely that it looked as though an inverted galaxy had formed above the central stage.

Even Max’s eyes sharpened slightly, for this attack was anything but weak. A thousand star beams did not simply mean greater numbers. Every beam carried Orion’s personal control, and every star possessed its own angle, speed, delay, and trajectory.

Against any ordinary opponent, an attack of this kind would be impossible to defend, because even if they somehow blocked hundreds of beams, the remainder would pierce through whatever opening appeared.
Orion’s voice rang out with calm authority.
"Nine Star Court. Thousand Star Rain."

The galaxy descended. Thousands of star beams plunged toward Revona, and the entire arena was swallowed in starlight. The barrier around the central stage flashed as the pressure of the attack rolled outward, and audiences throughout the Divine Realm erupted in shock.

The disciples of the Nine Star Court, watching from their own divine viewing platform, rose to their feet with shining eyes and faces full of pride. This was exactly the kind of grand and overwhelming assault their force was famous for. Their stars never needed to draw close, for their stars passed judgment from above.

But Revona stood beneath that falling galaxy and simply raised her head. Her Void Origin Eyes released a deeper glow. The first layer of starlight vanished, then the second, and then the third. The beams poured down without end, yet wherever her eyes traveled, they dissolved into nothingness.

The sight was almost impossible to believe. A thousand beams of starlight descended with magnificent force, and they were erased layer after layer, as though the sky itself were being emptied by nothing more than her gaze.
Some beams attempted to strike from behind her, but Revona’s eyes flickered, a faint ripple of void spread around her body, and those beams disappeared as well.

Other beams delayed their descent and dove in from blind angles, yet she turned only slightly and they vanished before arrival. Still others split into smaller beams at the final moment, and even those fragments were wiped away.

By the time the Thousand Star Rain ended, Revona remained standing exactly where she had begun, untouched and unshaken. The stage around her had not suffered so much as a scratch, because not one of the attacks had ever been permitted to land.
The silence that followed weighed heavier than any before it.
Orion regarded her for a long moment, then lowered his hands, and his smile turned wry. "You might be the worst possible matchup for me."
Revona watched him quietly.

Orion shook his head and went on. "Nearly all of my attacks are long-ranged. I fight with star beams, star rain, star spears, falling star arrays, and celestial suppression. I control the battlefield from a distance and overwhelm my opponents before they can ever approach me. But your Void Origin Eyes can nullify ranged attacks before they reach you, and against someone like me, that ability is almost unfair."
Revona’s expression stayed calm. "Almost."
Orion laughed softly. "You are right. Almost."

On the pillars, the top geniuses watched with grave expressions, and Max’s gaze remained fixed on the stage. He had expected Revona to be troublesome, but watching her erase Orion’s attacks one after another confirmed just how much stronger her eyes had grown.
A single beam, ten beams, a hundred beams, and finally a thousand beams had all dissolved beneath her gaze. Unless Orion revealed something deeper, this battle would lead nowhere.
Revona looked at Orion and spoke with quiet certainty. "Use your Pseudo Cosmic Path."

Orion’s smile slowly faded. The nine star marks on his body began to glow once more, but this time the light was different. It ran deeper, felt older, and carried a majesty far beyond anything he had shown. Revona’s Void Origin Eyes brightened as she watched him.
Orion lifted his gaze to the vast space above the arena and said softly, "I was hoping to save this for later." Then his eyes returned to Revona. "But against you, ordinary stars truly are useless."
The stage began to tremble faintly, and high above the central arena, the rivers of time-light reflected the birth of a new starry sky.
Orion raised one hand. "Then let us see whether your Void Origin Eyes can erase my path itself."

The moment Orion raised his hand, the entire atmosphere of the central stage transformed. The thousands of stars that Revona had erased did not return, yet their disappearance seemed to have roused something far deeper within him.
The nine star marks on his body no longer resembled simple symbols. They had become nine ancient star gates carved into his flesh, and each one released a different rhythm of celestial power.

One gate carried burning heat like a young sun, another carried cold silver light like a frozen moon, and another carried sharpness like a falling meteor. One bore crushing weight like a dead star, one held speed like a shooting comet, and one radiated endless pressure like a collapsing sky. The remaining three were more mysterious still, glowing with colors that shifted between gold, blue, violet, and pure white.

Revona’s expression finally changed by a fraction. She could tell that what stood before her was no longer a mere star technique. This was no longer a simple attack that fell from the sky and flew toward her body.
This was a path. It was a majestic, complete, and terrifying Pseudo Cosmic Path that had gathered the inheritance, the pride, and the very foundation of the Nine Star Court into a single body.

Orion slowly lowered his hand to his chest, and the star marks across his body blazed brighter and brighter until the space above him fell into darkness. It was not dark in the way of the abyss that surrounded Ervin, and it was not the darkness of empty nothingness.
This was the darkness of the universe in the moments before dawn, wide and silent and endless, filled with countless stars waiting for the signal to awaken.
Then the starry sky descended, and it did not fall upon Revona. It converged into Orion.

chapters.title: Chapter 1853: Nine Star Sovereign Body
paragraphs: The first star entered his left hand, and the second entered his right. The third star sank into his spine, the fourth entered his eyes, and the fifth merged with his heart. The sixth star wrapped itself around his bones, the seventh burned its way into his blood, and the eighth spread across his flesh.
Finally, the ninth star formed a brilliant crown of starlight above his head before sinking into his body like a divine seal.
Orion’s aura changed completely.

Until this moment, he had been a long-range star cultivator whose attacks descended from above and overwhelmed his enemies through their numbers, their angles, their speed, and their celestial pressure.

But now, with his Pseudo Cosmic Path fully open, the power of the stars no longer hung far away from him. It gathered into his body and transformed him from a distant commander of stars into a supreme genius of close combat.
His fingers glowed with lines of starlight, his bones released faint celestial hums, and his very steps fell into rhythm with a starry sky. The entire arena could feel the difference.
Orion Starfall was no longer using stars. He had become the vessel of his stars.
His voice rang across the stage, calm and clear.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path. Nine Star Sovereign Body."
Boom!

A wave of majestic star pressure erupted from him, and the central stage trembled. Above his head, an enormous illusory star palace took shape. It stood among galaxies, encircled by nine vast stars, and at its center rose a throne forged from condensed starlight.

The throne did not look tyrannical the way Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion did, and it did not feel suppressive like Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary. Instead, it felt grand, noble, and nearly immeasurable, as though Orion had borrowed the ancient authority of the starry heavens and set that authority directly into his own flesh.
Across the Divine Realm, countless spectators rose from their seats, and at the Nine Star Court, the disciples and elders erupted into roaring cheers.
"The Nine Star Sovereign Body!"
"Senior Brother Orion has revealed it!"
"That is one of the strongest Pseudo Cosmic Paths in the Divine Realm!"
"It is no ordinary star technique. Once he enters that state, every star he controls becomes part of his body!"
"Long range, close combat, movement, defense, and suppression all become star power!"
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, every one of the top geniuses grew serious.
Damian Voss’s gaze sharpened. "So that is his path."
Kaiden Voidmere narrowed his eyes. "The stars are no longer traveling toward Revona. They have already converged into him, and that changes the very nature of the attack."
Ervin studied Orion with a deeper gaze. "It turns a long-range star cultivator into a close combat monster."
Rakan Thorne grinned as his battle intent visibly climbed again. "Good. That guy was hiding something fun."
Morgana Starveil’s eyes flickered. "The Nine Star Court truly raised a terrifying genius."

Max watched in silence. He had always known Orion was strong, yet this Pseudo Cosmic Path still managed to surprise him. The Nine Star Sovereign Body was not flashy in any shallow sense. Its majesty came from the fact that it solved the greatest weakness of a star-based long-range fighter.

Orion’s ordinary methods could be erased by Revona’s Void Origin Eyes before they ever arrived, but once the stars entered his body, every punch, step, elbow, palm, and knee became a star attack delivered through direct physical contact.
Revona could nullify attacks that traveled toward her. But could she erase a star that had already become part of Orion’s body? That was the real question.
Revona’s Void Origin Eyes shone brighter. "You chose a good path," she said calmly.
Orion smiled faintly. "I had no choice. A person of the Nine Star Court is supposed to command the stars from above, but I never liked having only one way to fight."
Revona raised one hand. "Then come."

Orion vanished. He did not move the way a normal body cultivator moved. His movement resembled a shooting star crossing a stretch of night sky. One moment he stood at a distance, and the next he appeared directly in front of Revona with his fist wrapped in condensed starlight.

Revona’s eyes locked onto that fist, and the starlight around it dimmed, yet it did not vanish completely. Orion’s fist still arrived. Revona slid sideways, and the blow brushed past her shoulder. The star force packed inside it struck the air behind her and detonated into a brilliant ring of light that set the barrier trembling.
Orion’s eyes brightened. "So direct star force can be weakened, but it cannot be erased instantly."

Revona gave no answer. Her eyes flickered, and a ripple of void spread toward Orion’s chest. Had that ripple touched him, it would have tried to nullify the star power converged within his body, but Orion had already stepped clear.
The third star in his spine flashed, and his body cut away along a sharp diagonal, trailing a brief streak of blue and white light behind him.

He attacked again. His palm, his elbow, his knee, and his finger strike each carried a different star. The palm bore the crushing pressure of a dead star, the elbow carried the sharpness of a meteor, the knee burned with solar force, and the finger strike moved with the compressed speed of a comet.

Revona’s Void Origin Eyes worked without pause. Wherever her gaze fell, the star force weakened, distorted, or dimmed. Yet the attacks no longer disappeared as easily as they once had. Orion’s stars were not beams crossing open air anymore.
They had already fused into his body, and by the time Revona’s gaze reached them, they had become part of his movement, his flesh, and his martial rhythm.
The battle accelerated. Orion circled Revona like a living constellation, while Revona stayed composed, stepping back, turning, and raising her hands only when it became necessary.

Her Void Origin Eyes still erased a great deal of his force, but she could no longer stand motionless the way she had beneath the Thousand Star Rain. Now she had to move, she had to predict, and she had to decide which part of each attack to nullify first.

Rakan Thorne grinned as his battle intent visibly climbed again.
"Good.
That guy was hiding something fun."
Morgana Starveil’s eyes flickered.
"The Nine Star Court truly raised a terrifying genius."
Max watched in silence.
He had always known Orion was strong, yet this Pseudo Cosmic Path still managed to surprise him.
The Nine Star Sovereign Body was not flashy in any shallow sense.
Its majesty came from the fact that it solved the greatest weakness of a star-based long-range fighter.

Orion’s ordinary methods could be erased by Revona’s Void Origin Eyes before they ever arrived, but once the stars entered his body, every punch, step, elbow, palm, and knee became a star attack delivered through direct physical contact.
Revona could nullify attacks that traveled toward her.
But could she erase a star that had already become part of Orion’s body?
That was the real question.
Revona’s Void Origin Eyes shone brighter.
"You chose a good path," she said calmly.
Orion smiled faintly.
"I had no choice.
A person of the Nine Star Court is supposed to command the stars from above, but I never liked having only one way to fight."
Revona raised one hand.
"Then come."
Orion vanished.
He did not move the way a normal body cultivator moved.
His movement resembled a shooting star crossing a stretch of night sky.
One moment he stood at a distance, and the next he appeared directly in front of Revona with his fist wrapped in condensed starlight.
Revona’s eyes locked onto that fist, and the starlight around it dimmed, yet it did not vanish completely.
Orion’s fist still arrived.
Revona slid sideways, and the blow brushed past her shoulder.
The star force packed inside it struck the air behind her and detonated into a brilliant ring of light that set the barrier trembling.
Orion’s eyes brightened.
"So direct star force can be weakened, but it cannot be erased instantly."
Revona gave no answer.
Her eyes flickered, and a ripple of void spread toward Orion’s chest.
Had that ripple touched him, it would have tried to nullify the star power converged within his body, but Orion had already stepped clear.
The third star in his spine flashed, and his body cut away along a sharp diagonal, trailing a brief streak of blue and white light behind him.
He attacked again.
His palm, his elbow, his knee, and his finger strike each carried a different star.
The palm bore the crushing pressure of a dead star, the elbow carried the sharpness of a meteor, the knee burned with solar force, and the finger strike moved with the compressed speed of a comet.
Revona’s Void Origin Eyes worked without pause.
Wherever her gaze fell, the star force weakened, distorted, or dimmed.
Yet the attacks no longer disappeared as easily as they once had.
Orion’s stars were not beams crossing open air anymore.
They had already fused into his body, and by the time Revona’s gaze reached them, they had become part of his movement, his flesh, and his martial rhythm.
The battle accelerated.
Orion circled Revona like a living constellation, while Revona stayed composed, stepping back, turning, and raising her hands only when it became necessary.
Her Void Origin Eyes still erased a great deal of his force, but she could no longer stand motionless the way she had beneath the Thousand Star Rain.
Now she had to move, she had to predict, and she had to decide which part of each attack to nullify first.

chapters.title: Chapter 1854: Bypassing Her Ability!
paragraphs: The shift stunned many of the spectators.
"She moved!"
"Revona actually stepped back!"
"Orion’s Pseudo Cosmic Path is working!"
"His attacks are not being fully erased!"

At the Nine Star Court, the cheering swelled even louder, and at the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples watched with widening eyes. Even at the War God Palace, many body cultivators regarded Orion with newfound respect.

They rarely admired long-range fighters, but the Nine Star Sovereign Body had turned Orion into a genius of close combat without ever abandoning his star foundation, and that alone was enough to earn their attention.
On the stage, Orion’s attacks grew heavier.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body. First Star Fist."
His fist descended wrapped in blazing star heat. Revona’s eyes flashed, and half the heat vanished, but the remaining half still forced her to raise her arm.
Boom!
Revona slid back half a step, and for one breath the entire arena went silent.
Orion did not stop.
"Second Star Step."
His body shifted behind Revona like a star changing its orbit. She turned instantly with her Void Origin Eyes already seeking him, but Orion’s third star flashed before her gaze could fully settle.
"Third Star Elbow."
The elbow strike arrived from an impossible angle. Revona nullified most of it, but a small remnant of star force slipped through and struck the defensive ripple of void surrounding her body.
Bang!
A faint crack appeared in the void ripple, and Revona’s expression grew colder.
Orion smiled. "It seems there is a delay."
Revona’s eyes narrowed slightly.

Orion pressed on. "Your Void Origin Eyes are terrifying against anything that travels toward you, but when the attack is already bound to my body, you have to identify the exact star force inside each movement before you can erase it. If I change stars quickly enough, even you cannot erase everything in the same instant."
Revona did not deny it. Instead, she stepped forward for the first time as void light gathered around her fingers.
"Then I will erase you before you finish changing."

She attacked. Her movement was quiet, yet the danger inside it was terrifying. Her fingers carried the nullification of the void origin, no longer as a ranged phenomenon but as a direct close combat technique.
Orion’s eyes sharpened, the fourth star sank into his right leg, and he pivoted just clear of her fingers while sweeping his leg toward her waist.

Revona’s eyes flickered, and the star force inside his leg dimmed. But Orion changed again. The fifth star entered his left shoulder, he abandoned the kick midway, stepped inside her guard, and struck with his shoulder.
Revona’s pupils contracted slightly. The change had come too fast. Her gaze had already locked onto the leg, and by the time it shifted to the shoulder, Orion was already upon her.
Boom!
The shoulder strike landed, and Revona was driven backward. She did not lose half a step this time. She lost three full steps.
The entire arena exploded with shock.
"He hit her!"
"Orion bypassed the Void Origin Eyes!"
"That was a clean, direct strike!"
"Did Revona’s ability fail?"
"No, it did not fail. Orion changed his star force faster than she could erase it!"

Revona came to a stop after the third step, her long hair drifting around her face. Her body carried no serious injury, but the fact that Orion had landed a clean strike mattered far more than any damage.

It proved something important. Her Void Origin Eyes could be bypassed. It could not be done easily, and it could not be done with ordinary power, but with sufficient speed, transformation, timing, and a Pseudo Cosmic Path strong enough to change the very nature of its attacks, it could be done.
On the pillars, even the top geniuses reacted.
Damian Voss’s eyes turned razor sharp. "He found an opening."
Kaiden Voidmere spoke softly. "It is not an opening in the eyes themselves, but an opening in the reaction process behind them."
Ervin nodded faintly. "The eyes can erase what they recognize, and Orion keeps changing what they need to recognize."
Rakan Thorne laughed. "Now that is more like it."
Morgana Starveil looked at Orion with fresh caution. "So the smiling star prince is also a monster in close combat."
Aurelian Lareth’s expression stayed cold, though even he could not dismiss what he had just witnessed, and Selene Vaeloria stared at the stage with a complicated look in her eyes.

Max watched in silence, his gaze calm but intent. Orion had not simply overwhelmed Revona with strength. He had found a way to pressure the very mechanism behind her ability, and that made him far more dangerous than anyone who relied only on grand displays of star power.

On the stage, Orion lowered his shoulder and smiled faintly, though his breathing had grown a touch heavier. Sustaining the Nine Star Sovereign Body while constantly cycling star forces through his own flesh was clearly no effortless feat.
Revona slowly raised her hand and touched the spot where his shoulder had struck her. Then she looked at him, and for the first time a faint smile crossed her face.
"Good."
Orion shook his head lightly. "You are saying that after being hit?"
"Yes," Revona said calmly. "Because now this battle has become meaningful."
The void-colored light in her eyes deepened, and the air around her began to disappear in small, silent fragments.

As her words settled, the void surrounding her grew deeper still. The place where Orion’s shoulder had struck her still bore a faint trace of starlight, but that trace was already dissolving beneath the glow of her Void Origin Eyes.

She did not look angry, and she did not look humiliated. Instead, her expression carried a calm seriousness that dimmed Orion’s own smile a little further, because he understood what it meant. The battle had finally reached the point where Revona would stop treating him as someone whose attacks could simply be erased from a distance.

Orion rolled his shoulder once, and the Nine Star Sovereign Body within him burned brighter. Star lines spread from his chest into his arms and from his spine down into his legs, until his entire body looked as though a miniature galaxy had been carved beneath his skin.

The nine ancient stars revolving inside him began to spin faster, and every rotation lifted his close combat power to a higher level. His breathing grew heavier, yet his aura became more majestic, as if each breath drew power down from some faraway starry heaven and condensed it into his flesh.

Revona raised her hand slowly, and the air around her fingertips vanished. It was not shattered, and it was not cut apart. It simply vanished. A circle of emptiness spread out beneath her feet, silent and smooth, and wherever it passed, the light of the arena dimmed as though it had been swallowed before it could exist.
The stage did not break, the cracks did not widen, and even the dust near her feet disappeared without a sound, leaving behind a clean and hollow space that looked disturbingly calm.

chapters.title: Chapter 1855: Revona’s Pseudo Cosmic Path!
paragraphs: Orion’s eyes narrowed. "That looks dangerous."
Revona regarded him evenly. "It is."
Then she stepped forward.

For the first time in the battle, Revona attacked with clear initiative. Her figure crossed the stage in strange silence. She was not fast in the explosive way Rakan moved, she was not elegant like Kaiden with his void steps, and she was not grand like Orion in his star movement.

She moved as though distance had simply forgotten to resist her. Her right hand reached for Orion’s chest, and the void gathered around her fingers carried the power to erase the star force inside his body before it could finish circulating.
Orion reacted instantly.
"Second Star Step."

A blue and white star flashed within his spine, and his body slid away along a diagonal like a comet changing orbit. Revona’s fingers passed through the space where his chest had been, and the starlight afterimage he left behind winked out of existence at once.
Orion reappeared at her side as the fifth star entered his shoulder again, and he drove it toward her ribs.

Revona’s Void Origin Eyes turned toward him, and the fifth star dimmed. But Orion changed midway. The seventh star surged into his blood, his shoulder strike flowed into a palm thrust, and burning red star force gathered in his hand. Revona’s eyes tracked the shift, yet Orion changed once more before her nullification could finish its work.
"Ninth Star Crown Pressure."

A crown-shaped star mark flashed above his head, and his entire body descended with heavy celestial pressure, transforming the palm thrust into a suppressive downward strike. Revona finally raised her left arm to block.
Boom!

The collision drove both of them backward. A thin line of blood appeared on Revona’s wrist, but Orion’s palm trembled as well, for the void-origin power crawling up from her arm was trying to erase the star force inside his hand.
He withdrew at once and circulated the third star through his bones, forcing the invading ripple of void out of his body before it could sink any deeper.

The entire arena went quiet. This was no longer the one-sided nullification from earlier in the battle. Orion had forced Revona to block, Revona had forced Orion to retreat, and both of them had drawn blood from the other, even if only slightly.
Orion smiled faintly despite the pressure. "You really are troublesome."
Revona’s gaze stayed calm. "You are changing your star force faster."
"I have to," Orion replied. "If I slow down even a little, you will erase it."
"Then keep changing."
The void-colored light in her eyes brightened, and Revona moved again. Orion met her head-on.

The two figures collided at the center of the stage, and in an instant the entire battlefield became a storm of stars and emptiness. Orion’s fists carried blazing stellar heat, his elbows carried the sharpness of meteors, his knees bore collapsing star pressure, and his steps alternated between the speed of a comet and the weight of a dead star.
Revona’s eyes erased whatever they managed to catch, while her hands wielded void-origin nullification capable of dissolving any star power that touched her body.

Every time Orion changed stars, Revona’s pupils shifted, and every time her gaze locked onto him, Orion altered the star circulating through his flesh. It had become a battle of speed, reaction, transformation, and understanding.

Orion drove Revona back once with a First Star Fist. She erased most of it and answered by striking his shoulder with two fingers. A patch of starlight vanished from his shoulder and blood sprayed from beneath his armor, but Orion immediately twisted at the waist and countered with a Fourth Star Knee.

The knee crashed into Revona’s guard and sent her sliding backward across the stage, and before she could steady herself, his Sixth Star Pressure descended from above, making the air around her body feel as heavy as a dead star.
Revona’s eyes shone. The pressure vanished around her head and chest, but it lingered around her feet, and for a fraction of a breath her movement slowed.
Orion seized that instant.
"Eight Star Convergence Strike."

Eight of the stars within his body ignited at once and converged into his right fist. The attack was no longer some distant beam. It was a compact stellar explosion carried by living flesh. He punched toward Revona’s abdomen, and the terrifying power packed inside that fist cracked the stage beneath him before the blow had even landed.
Revona’s eyes narrowed and her Void Origin Eyes blazed. Most of the converged star force vanished, but not all of it.
Boom!
Orion’s fist struck her abdomen, and for the first time in the battle, Revona’s body was sent flying backward.
The entire Divine Realm erupted.
"She was hit again!"
"Orion struck her directly!"
"That was an Eight Star Convergence Strike!"
"He is truly forcing the Void Origin Eyes to their limit!"

At the Nine Star Court, the disciples screamed until their starry viewing platform shook. Elders who had watched calmly earlier now rose to their feet with pride burning in their eyes as Orion pushed Revona past the point where stillness and nullification alone could carry her.

Their strongest genius had transformed from a long-range star cultivator into a close combat star sovereign, and he was proving before the entire Divine Realm why the Nine Star Court deserved its place among the strongest first-rate forces.

On the stage, Revona landed lightly, though blood trickled from the corner of her mouth. She lowered her gaze to the wound, then looked back at Orion, and for the first time the air around her truly changed.
The void beneath her feet expanded. Her pupils deepened, and what dwelled within those eyes was no longer merely the power to erase attacks.

A vast hollow world began to unfold behind her. It was not a world of darkness like Ervin’s abyss, and it was not a world of space like Kaiden’s void. It was a realm of origin-level emptiness, a place with no sky, no ground, no stars, no wind, no sound, and no color. Everything that entered that realm seemed to lose its very reason to keep existing.
Orion’s smile vanished completely, and every participant on the pillars grew solemn.
Max’s eyes sharpened.
’So this is her Pseudo Cosmic Path.’
Revona’s voice drifted quietly across the stage.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."
The hollow world behind her yawned wider.
"Void Origin Realm."
Boom!

There was no deafening explosion. There was only silence, and that silence was terrifying. The central stage seemed to lose all sound for an instant. The star glow surrounding Orion dimmed, and the cracks spreading across the arena floor simply stopped, not because they had healed, but because even the force that should have extended them had been erased.
The air inside the stage turned hollow, and the sense of Revona’s existence became faint and absolute at the same time.
Her Void Origin Eyes had already been terrifying, but once the Void Origin Realm unfurled behind her, her nullification was no longer bound to what her eyes could directly observe.

The entire region around her had become a field of origin emptiness, and any power entering it would be weakened, erased, or returned to nothingness unless it carried enough authority, enough density, or enough transformation speed to withstand the realm itself.
Orion drew a slow breath. "So that is your path."
Revona looked at him. "Now use everything."
Orion stared at her for a moment, and then he laughed softly. "Fine."

chapters.title: Chapter 1856: Orion giving his all!
paragraphs: The nine stars inside his body blazed as one, and his aura surged violently upward. The illusory star palace behind him shone brighter, and the nine massive stars encircling the throne poured streams of light down into Orion’s body. His skin split in several places under the pressure, yet he did not stop.
Blood ran down his arms, and even that blood glimmered with faint starlight. His eyes became twin stars, and the crown of starlight reappeared above his head, far clearer than it had been before.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body."
His voice dropped deeper.
"Full Star Convergence."
Boom!

The entire stage shuddered beneath the clash of two Pseudo Cosmic Paths. On one side, the Void Origin Realm spread outward as a hollow world that erased existence itself. On the other, the Nine Star Sovereign Body had transformed Orion into a vessel carrying all nine stars at once.

Orion moved, and this time his speed was terrifying. He crossed the field like a star plunging through empty space. The Void Origin Realm began erasing the star force around him the instant he entered it, but the nine stars within his body kept replenishing what was lost.

Every step burned through his stamina, every punch consumed the power circulating through his organs and bones, and every shift of star force tore at his meridians, yet Orion pressed forward without a moment’s hesitation.

Revona raised both hands, and ripples of void origin spread outward like invisible waves. Orion punched through the first wave and lost half the star power in his fist, so he changed stars. He stepped through the second wave and his left leg went numb as the void devoured the force inside it, so he changed again. He pushed into the third wave and struck.
Boom!
Revona blocked with both arms, but the impact shoved her backward, and a crack split the hollow space behind her.
The spectators were stunned.
"He is fighting inside her Pseudo Cosmic Path!"
"His star power keeps being erased, but he keeps replacing it!"
"This is insane!"
"Both of them are burning through their power far too fast!"
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the top geniuses watched without blinking.
Damian Voss’s eyes were cold and sharp. "Orion is forcing his way through by overloading the gap between her erasure and his replenishment."
Kaiden Voidmere gave a slight nod. "But that method costs him too much. The Void Origin Realm is multiplying the price of every single attack."
Ervin’s gaze ran deep. "If he cannot break through soon, he will be the one to collapse first."
Rakan Thorne clenched his fists, his grin wild yet serious. "Even so, that star bastard is amazing."

Max said nothing. He could see everything the others saw, and more besides. Orion’s Pseudo Cosmic Path was among the strongest paths he had witnessed in the entire conference. It had turned a long-range star genius into a supreme close combat monster, and even inside Revona’s Void Origin Realm, Orion was still forcing her back one step at a time.

But Revona’s path was perfectly suited to bleeding him dry. Every strike Orion threw was partially erased before it could land, every movement demanded more power than it normally would, and every attempt to change stars grew harder beneath the pressure of that origin emptiness.

Yet Orion kept going. He struck Revona’s shoulder and broke through her void guard. Her palm landed on his chest and erased a great slab of his star armor, tearing open the flesh beneath it. He answered with a Third Star Elbow that cut across her side and scattered blood through the air.

She turned the Void Origin Realm on his right leg, swallowed the force within it, and very nearly brought him down. He shifted to the Sixth Star and slammed both fists downward, forcing her onto one knee for the length of a breath. She lifted her eyes, and the void around him surged upward, stripping three layers of star force from his body at once.
Orion coughed blood. Then he smiled.
"Not enough."
He stepped in again.

The battle climbed to a terrifying intensity. The stage became a place where stars were born and erased with every passing second. Star fists detonated and vanished, and waves of void spread and cracked. Orion’s body was soon covered in wounds, with his armor broken, his hair in disarray, and blood running down his forehead into one eye.
Revona had not escaped unharmed either. Blood stained her sleeves, her breathing had grown heavy, and the hollow world behind her shuddered several times under Orion’s relentless assault.

Neither of them stopped, and neither surrendered. Orion drove Revona to the brink by endlessly changing the star circulating through his body, forcing her Void Origin Eyes to chase one force after another.

Revona drove Orion to the brink by expanding the Void Origin Realm until every step he took cost him more strength than an ordinary full-power attack. Their Pseudo Cosmic Paths collided in a way that made countless spectators forget how to breathe.

Then, at last, Orion found one more opening. Revona’s gaze had locked onto the Seventh Star burning in his blood, and the Void Origin Realm had begun erasing the star force in his veins. In that moment, Orion abruptly shifted everything into the Ninth Star Crown above his head, and for a fraction of a breath, Revona’s nullification lagged behind.
Orion appeared in front of her.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body. Celestial Crown Breaker."
His fist descended with all nine stars compressed into a single crown-shaped strike. Revona’s eyes widened slightly, and for the first time, she could not fully erase it in time.
Boom!

The strike landed square against her chest. Revona was hurled backward with blood spilling from her lips, and her body slammed into the far side of the barrier. The entire arena shook, and the hollow world behind her flickered violently.

The Nine Star Court went mad with cheering, but Orion did not celebrate. He dropped to one knee, coughing blood onto the fractured stage while his right arm trembled beyond his control. That single strike had very nearly emptied him.

Across from him, Revona slowly pushed herself away from the barrier. Her face was pale, and the front of her clothes was soaked with blood. The Void Origin Realm behind her had dimmed, but it had not collapsed.
Orion lifted his head, saw it still standing, and a bitter smile crossed his face. "You endured even that?"
Revona wiped the blood from her lips. "Barely."

Orion laughed once, though the laugh quickly broke apart into another cough. He forced himself back to his feet as the nine stars within his body flickered. One of them dimmed, then another, and then a third.
Revona regarded him calmly, though her own breathing had grown unsteady. "You are exhausted."

Orion smiled, and strangely enough, that smile was brighter than it had been all battle. Blood still ran from the corner of his mouth, several wounds across his arms and chest gaped deep enough to expose the flesh beneath his broken armor, and the star lines tracing his body had dimmed to an unstable flicker, yet he looked as though none of it mattered to him in the slightest.
"Almost," he said lightly.
"Not almost," Revona replied. "You are at your limit."

chapters.title: Chapter 1857: Starfall Extinction!
paragraphs: Orion did not deny it. He only laughed softly, wiped the blood from his chin with the back of his hand, and took one more step forward. In that moment, everyone watching could feel that he genuinely had nothing left to spare.

The Nine Star Sovereign Body had already pushed him past the natural endurance of his flesh, and Full Star Convergence had burned through his meridians, his flesh, and his blood at a terrifying rate. Any ordinary genius would have collapsed long before now.

Even so, Orion remained on his feet, and the light in his eyes had not dimmed at all. If anything, it had grown sharper, as though he had finally arrived at the exact moment he had been waiting for since the battle began.

"The Nine Star Court taught me many star arts," Orion said as the starlight around him trembled weakly. "It taught me how to call down stars, how to command them, and how to wear their power as my own body. But this final move..." His smile widened. "This one is mine."

The instant those words fell, the expressions of the Nine Star Court elders and disciples watching from afar changed all at once, and even the participants on the pillars felt their attention sharpen further.

A technique created by Orion himself was no trivial matter. For a genius of his caliber to speak this way at the very end of a battle meant that whatever he was about to unleash was not simply another inherited attack. It was a move born from his own understanding, his own martial will, and his own path as the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court.
Orion slowly closed his right hand into a fist.

The nine dimming stars within his body abruptly stopped flickering and went still. For one brief instant, it seemed as though all of them were about to go out. Then, in the very next moment, all nine stars blazed at once with a brightness so intense that even the barrier around the central stage shook violently.

The broken star palace reappeared behind him, though not in its earlier majestic and stable form. It returned in a wilder and more desperate shape, as if the entire palace had been forcibly reignited by nothing but Orion’s will.

Cracks raced across the illusory structure, and the nine stars surrounding it began breaking apart into countless streams of star essence. Rather than scattering into the sky, every one of those streams rushed straight back into Orion’s body.

His injuries worsened instantly. Blood burst from several splits along his arms and shoulders, his knees shook, and the faint groan of bones straining under the pressure could actually be heard. Yet Orion did not stop.

He accepted all of that star essence into himself, compressing it, forcing it, and refining it within the span of a single breath. The pressure released by that compression was so immense that the stage caved in beneath his feet, and even Revona’s Void Origin Realm rippled heavily in answer.

Revona’s calm eyes finally shifted in a way anyone could see. She could feel it clearly. This attack was different from everything that had come before. It was not merely a stronger star punch, and it was not another variation of his close combat star arts.

This was Orion taking the Nine Star Sovereign Body, shattering the stars within himself down to their rawest essence, and gathering all of it into one final eruption. This was a move built to end battles, a move that no longer cared about preservation, or recoil, or what would become of his body once the strike was released.
Orion opened his eyes fully, and they shone like two collapsing stars.
"This technique," he said, his voice lower and heavier than before, "is called Starfall Extinction."

The moment he spoke the name, the entire arena seemed to lose all lesser light, as though every fragment of brightness in the stage, the barrier, and the surrounding pillars had been dragged toward Orion’s fist. What remained around him was a terrifyingly dense sphere of rotating star essence.

It looked small next to the grand phenomena of his earlier attacks, yet the power compressed inside it was enough to make even the top geniuses feel their hearts tighten. It stood as the exact opposite of his sprawling celestial assaults. It was all of his stars, all of his remaining strength, all of his will, and all of his understanding condensed into a single point of destruction.

Revona inhaled slowly, and the Void Origin Realm behind her began to shrink. It no longer spread outward as a hollow world. Instead, it withdrew toward her body, condensing layer upon layer until it formed a deep, translucent ring of pure origin emptiness hovering before her.

The ring was not large, standing only slightly wider than her own frame, but the moment it appeared, everyone understood that this was no ordinary defense. It was the very core of her Pseudo Cosmic Path, the deepest defensive response she could summon under pressure.

Orion smiled brightly. Even now, with blood streaking his face and his body shaking beneath the weight of his own technique, he looked genuinely happy. It was the smile of someone who had finally found an opponent worth everything he could give.
Then he disappeared.

He did not move like a meteor or a comet this time. He moved like a star collapsing at the end of its life, shrinking into nothing for one impossible instant before exploding back into existence directly in front of Revona.
The compressed star sphere around his fist roared in utter silence, and when he punched forward, it was as though an entire constellation had been buried inside that single strike.
"Starfall Extinction!"
The punch landed against the hollow ring.
For one breath, nothing happened at all. Then the world shook.

The hollow ring before Revona trembled so violently that visible cracks began spidering across its surface. The sound that emerged was not the sound of an explosion but a low and terrifying grinding, as though two concepts that should never have met were tearing directly at each other.

Orion’s fist kept pushing forward. The compressed star essence unraveled in layers, and each layer released enough force to destroy ordinary divine techniques several times over. Revona’s condensed Void Origin Realm erased one layer, then another, and then another, but the attack never stopped coming, because Orion had constructed it so that every erased layer immediately triggered the collapse of the next one waiting inside his fist.

The first layer of emptiness shattered, the second layer cracked, and the third layer bent inward. Revona’s expression became the most serious it had been in the entire battle. Blood began to seep once more from the corner of her lips, and the light of her Void Origin Eyes deepened to a frightening degree.

Even so, Orion’s fist kept advancing. It gained a palm’s width, then another inch, and then another after that. The hollow ring was being forced back toward her chest, and the star essence within his punch had grown so concentrated that even her direct nullification could no longer erase it quickly enough.
The arena erupted.
"He is breaking through!"
"That is his own technique!"
"Revona is being pushed back!"
"Her Void Origin Realm cannot stop it!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1858: Last One Standing!
paragraphs: Max’s eyes narrowed sharply, Damian’s grip tightened around his sword, Kaiden’s expression turned deeply solemn, and Ervin stared without blinking. Even Angelina Valerius, who had remained perfectly composed through every battle so far, watched the collision with a slightly keener gaze.

Revona finally understood that if she tried to withstand this attack through ordinary nullification alone, she would lose. The force of Starfall Extinction was too compressed, too layered, and too desperate.
Orion had not built a move meant to overwhelm from range. He had built a move meant to burn everything in a single instant and force a path straight through whatever stood in front of him.
At that critical moment, Revona’s eyes blazed with terrifying intensity.
"Void Origin Realm," she said softly, though the words seemed to echo from somewhere far deeper than her own voice. "Return to Nothing."

The cracked hollow ring before her collapsed inward. It did not break apart. It folded into itself. Every layer of emptiness, every trace of nullification, and every fragment of erased existence within the Void Origin Realm converged upon one single point in front of Revona’s body.

It was a point so utterly empty that even the space around it seemed to flinch away. The shattered force of Orion’s fist, the overflowing star essence, and the compressed destruction of Starfall Extinction were all drawn into that point of absolute void.

Then it vanished, though it did not vanish all at once, and it did not vanish cleanly. The star essence fought back like a dying supernova. It tore at the point of emptiness, forcing blood to spill from Revona’s lips and draining the color from the skin around her eyes.
But in the end, Return to Nothing prevailed. The point of origin emptiness swallowed the last portion of Starfall Extinction and returned it to nothing.

When the blinding light finally faded, Orion’s fist had stopped just short of Revona’s chest. The star sphere around his hand was gone. The stars inside his body darkened one after another, the crown above his head shattered, and the reignited star palace behind him broke into dim fragments that dissolved into the air.

For a moment, Orion remained standing. He looked at Revona, then at his own fist, and then he laughed softly. It was a tired laugh, yet it carried not even a trace of bitterness. He had pushed her that far. He had forced the woman with the Void Origin Eyes to reveal the true core of her defensive ability just to survive him.
"Good," he said weakly, still smiling brightly. "That really was the limit."

The moment the words left him, all the strength drained from his body at once. His knees buckled, his shoulders sagged, and his eyes slid shut as his consciousness finally gave out. He fell forward like a star that had burned through the very last of its light.

Revona caught him by the shoulder before he could strike the ground. She was breathing hard as well, her face pale, her chest rising and falling faster than before, and a faint streak of blood still marking her lips.
Return to Nothing had allowed her to survive, but it had not come without a price. Even so, she remained on her feet, while Orion had finally spent everything he had.
The entire arena fell silent.
Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand and announced the result.
"Orion Starfall is unable to continue. Winner, Revona."

The great screen above the arena changed at once. Yet even after the result appeared, the silence lingered for several more breaths, because everyone understood that what they had just witnessed was no ordinary exchange of victory and defeat. It had been two peak geniuses driving each other to the absolute edge.
Orion had forced Revona to reveal the deepest ability of her Void Origin Realm, while Revona had withstood the strongest self-created technique Orion could release at the very end of his strength.
One of them remained standing and the other had fallen unconscious, but together they had raised the standard of the final round to an even more terrifying height.

Watching the unconscious Orion in Revona’s grasp, many of the Nine Star Court disciples felt their blood boil with pride rather than shame. Their strongest genius had lost, but he had lost while displaying a brilliance that carved his name into the memory of the entire Divine Realm more deeply than ever before.

Revona gazed quietly at the fainted Orion for a moment before the transfer light descended to carry him away. Then she too returned to her pillar, and for the first time since the battles had begun, even the top geniuses exchanged looks weighted with something far heavier than before.
After watching Orion and Revona push each other so far, all of them understood one thing with perfect clarity.
The final round had only grown more dangerous from this point onward.
[Winner: Revona.]
[Orion Starfall Defeated.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 4]
[Total Wins: 4]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Orion Starfall]
[Total Battles Fought: 4]
[Total Wins: 3]
The result appeared clearly on the screen, yet no one spoke for several breaths.

Orion had lost, but no one could bring themselves to look down on him. He had forced Revona to move, he had forced her to fight with real initiative, and he had forced her to reveal the Void Origin Realm itself.

He had wounded her again and again, and at the very end he had come within a hair of breaking through her Pseudo Cosmic Path entirely. Had his strength lasted even a few breaths longer, the result might well have been different.

Revona remained on the stage for a moment, still holding Orion upright. Her face was pale, her aura wavered unsteadily, and blood still stained her lips. She looked down at Orion, who had fainted with a faint smile lingering on his face, and then she spoke softly enough that only those closest could hear.
"You were strong."

A transfer light descended and carried Orion back to his pillar, where the laws of the Eternal Hourglass began stabilizing his injuries. Revona returned to her own pillar as well, but she sat down the moment she arrived.

The Void Origin Realm had vanished, and the light in her Void Origin Eyes had dimmed noticeably. This victory had not come easily. She had won, but the battle had driven her to the very edge of exhaustion.

Across the Divine Realm, the disciples of the Nine Star Court were silent at first. Then, one by one, they began to cheer. They cheered not because Orion had won, but because he had fought a battle worthy of their strongest genius.

He had displayed the majesty of the Nine Star Sovereign Body before the entire Divine Realm, and even in defeat he had made countless forces understand exactly why the Nine Star Court stood among the greatest first-rate powers.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Max watched Revona quietly.
’Her Void Origin Realm is dangerous,’ he thought. ’Even Orion’s Pseudo Cosmic Path could not break through before his strength ran out.’
Damian Voss’s gaze was sharp, and Kaiden Voidmere looked deep in thought. Ervin’s eyes remained calm, though his grip on his spear tightened by a fraction.
Rakan Thorne laughed softly from his pillar. "That was a good fight."
Morgana Starveil nodded faintly. "Too good. Now everyone has more problems to worry about."
Aurelian Lareth’s expression stayed cold, though even he could not deny the level of the battle that had just unfolded.
Angelina Valerius waited until Orion’s injuries had stabilized and Revona’s aura had settled enough for her to remain conscious. Then she turned back toward the screen of light above the arena.
"The next battle will now begin."

sentences.text: Max’s eyes narrowed sharply, Damian’s grip tightened around his sword, Kaiden’s expression turned deeply solemn, and Ervin stared without blinking.
Even Angelina Valerius, who had remained perfectly composed through every battle so far, watched the collision with a slightly keener gaze.
Revona finally understood that if she tried to withstand this attack through ordinary nullification alone, she would lose.
The force of Starfall Extinction was too compressed, too layered, and too desperate.
Orion had not built a move meant to overwhelm from range.
He had built a move meant to burn everything in a single instant and force a path straight through whatever stood in front of him.
At that critical moment, Revona’s eyes blazed with terrifying intensity.
"Void Origin Realm," she said softly, though the words seemed to echo from somewhere far deeper than her own voice.
"Return to Nothing."
The cracked hollow ring before her collapsed inward.
It did not break apart.
It folded into itself.
Every layer of emptiness, every trace of nullification, and every fragment of erased existence within the Void Origin Realm converged upon one single point in front of Revona’s body.
It was a point so utterly empty that even the space around it seemed to flinch away.
The shattered force of Orion’s fist, the overflowing star essence, and the compressed destruction of Starfall Extinction were all drawn into that point of absolute void.
Then it vanished, though it did not vanish all at once, and it did not vanish cleanly.
The star essence fought back like a dying supernova.
It tore at the point of emptiness, forcing blood to spill from Revona’s lips and draining the color from the skin around her eyes.
But in the end, Return to Nothing prevailed.
The point of origin emptiness swallowed the last portion of Starfall Extinction and returned it to nothing.
When the blinding light finally faded, Orion’s fist had stopped just short of Revona’s chest.
The star sphere around his hand was gone.
The stars inside his body darkened one after another, the crown above his head shattered, and the reignited star palace behind him broke into dim fragments that dissolved into the air.
For a moment, Orion remained standing.
He looked at Revona, then at his own fist, and then he laughed softly.
It was a tired laugh, yet it carried not even a trace of bitterness.
He had pushed her that far.
He had forced the woman with the Void Origin Eyes to reveal the true core of her defensive ability just to survive him.
"Good," he said weakly, still smiling brightly.
"That really was the limit."
The moment the words left him, all the strength drained from his body at once.
His knees buckled, his shoulders sagged, and his eyes slid shut as his consciousness finally gave out.
He fell forward like a star that had burned through the very last of its light.
Revona caught him by the shoulder before he could strike the ground.
She was breathing hard as well, her face pale, her chest rising and falling faster than before, and a faint streak of blood still marking her lips.
Return to Nothing had allowed her to survive, but it had not come without a price.
Even so, she remained on her feet, while Orion had finally spent everything he had.
The entire arena fell silent.
Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand and announced the result.
"Orion Starfall is unable to continue.
Winner, Revona."
The great screen above the arena changed at once.
Yet even after the result appeared, the silence lingered for several more breaths, because everyone understood that what they had just witnessed was no ordinary exchange of victory and defeat.
It had been two peak geniuses driving each other to the absolute edge.
Orion had forced Revona to reveal the deepest ability of her Void Origin Realm, while Revona had withstood the strongest self-created technique Orion could release at the very end of his strength.
One of them remained standing and the other had fallen unconscious, but together they had raised the standard of the final round to an even more terrifying height.
Watching the unconscious Orion in Revona’s grasp, many of the Nine Star Court disciples felt their blood boil with pride rather than shame.
Their strongest genius had lost, but he had lost while displaying a brilliance that carved his name into the memory of the entire Divine Realm more deeply than ever before.
Revona gazed quietly at the fainted Orion for a moment before the transfer light descended to carry him away.
Then she too returned to her pillar, and for the first time since the battles had begun, even the top geniuses exchanged looks weighted with something far heavier than before.
After watching Orion and Revona push each other so far, all of them understood one thing with perfect clarity.
The final round had only grown more dangerous from this point onward.

Orion had lost, but no one could bring themselves to look down on him.
He had forced Revona to move, he had forced her to fight with real initiative, and he had forced her to reveal the Void Origin Realm itself.
He had wounded her again and again, and at the very end he had come within a hair of breaking through her Pseudo Cosmic Path entirely.
Had his strength lasted even a few breaths longer, the result might well have been different.
Revona remained on the stage for a moment, still holding Orion upright.
Her face was pale, her aura wavered unsteadily, and blood still stained her lips.
She looked down at Orion, who had fainted with a faint smile lingering on his face, and then she spoke softly enough that only those closest could hear.
"You were strong."

This victory had not come easily.
She had won, but the battle had driven her to the very edge of exhaustion.

Then, one by one, they began to cheer.
They cheered not because Orion had won, but because he had fought a battle worthy of their strongest genius.

chapters.title: Chapter 1859: Damian vs Divine Son!
paragraphs: The silence that followed Orion’s defeat did not fade quickly.

Even after the transfer light carried him back to his pillar and the healing laws of the Eternal Hourglass began stabilizing his body, many spectators across the Divine Realm continued staring at the screen without a word.

Orion Starfall had lost, yet his loss carried more weight than many victories. He had forced Revona to reveal the Void Origin Realm, pushed her into using Return to Nothing, and burned through every last trace of his strength with his self-created technique, Starfall Extinction.
In the end he had fainted before he could break through that final layer of nothingness, but no one could claim that the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court had been weak.

Revona sat quietly on her pillar after returning, her face still pale and her breathing still uneven. The void-colored glow in her eyes had dimmed considerably, and for the first time since the final competitive stage began, she no longer looked untouchable.

Her victory was real, but so was the price she had paid for it. The Void Origin Realm had defended her and Return to Nothing had saved her, yet Orion’s final attack had pushed her to the very edge of what she could endure.
On the surrounding pillars, the top geniuses kept their silence.
Max looked toward Orion’s pillar for a moment before shifting his gaze to Revona. His expression barely changed, but his eyes had grown deeper, because the battle had handed him valuable information.

Revona’s Void Origin Eyes could erase incoming attacks, yet sufficient transformation speed could carve out openings. Her Void Origin Realm could expand that ability into an entire field, but even that field could be pressured by an attack carrying enough density and layered power.

The true problem was Return to Nothing. It was no simple defense. It gathered everything that had been erased and folded it back into a single point of origin emptiness, and it had caused even Orion’s strongest self-created technique to fail within the final stretch of distance.
Damian Voss watched quietly as well. His hand rested near his sword hilt, and the sharpness in his eyes had not faded since the moment Orion unleashed Starfall Extinction.

Others may have seen only the brilliance of that final attack, but Damian had seen the will behind it, and for a swordsman, will mattered every bit as much as technique. A person capable of creating a move like that at the brink of collapse deserved respect.

Aurelian Lareth stood on his own pillar with a cold and dignified expression. Unlike many of the others, he displayed no open admiration. His golden-white light flowed faintly around him while his eyes swept occasionally across Max, Revona, Damian, and the remaining peak geniuses.
The Divine Son of the second elven faction still carried his proud composure, but after the battles that had already taken place, even he could no longer pretend that the road ahead would be easy.
Angelina Valerius gave Revona a few moments to steady herself, and then she raised her hand.
"The previous battle has concluded," she said calmly, her voice carrying across the Eternal Hourglass arena. "The final competitive stage will continue."
The giant screen of light above the arena brightened once more, and names began to rotate. The randomizer spun faster and faster while every remaining participant looked upward.

After the battle between Orion and Revona, no one dared to relax, for the final competitive stage had already proven that the randomizer cared nothing for timing, reputation, recovery, or fear. It could match monster against monster at any moment it pleased.

The names flashed rapidly past, among them Max Morgan, Rakan Thorne, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Rosaline Lunara, Morgana Starveil, Selene Vaeloria, Fin Arclight, Revona, Damian Voss, and Aurelian Lareth.
The light slowed, and a strange pressure spread through the arena. Many spectators leaned forward without meaning to.
The first name stopped.
[Damian Voss]
The moment Damian’s name appeared, the atmosphere of the arena sharpened. The strongest genius of the Sword God Palace had finally been called into another major battle.

Until now, Damian had won every match cleanly and calmly, never revealing more than the bare minimum. His sword had looked simple, yet every victory had displayed terrifying control. He had never been pushed, he had never used his Pseudo Cosmic Path, and he had never shown the full depth of the Sword God Palace inheritance.
The second name continued spinning while the participants watched closely. Max’s gaze sharpened slightly, and Aurelian’s golden eyes narrowed.
The light stopped.
[Aurelian Lareth]
For one brief moment, the entire Eternal Hourglass arena went silent. Then the screen enlarged both names at once.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Forty]
[Damian Voss vs Aurelian Lareth]

The silence shattered, and a wave of shock swept through the arena and across the Divine Realm. Damian Voss was the strongest genius of the Sword God Palace, and Aurelian Lareth was the Divine Son of the second elven faction.
One was the blade raised by one of the greatest sword forces in the Divine Realm, a genius whose swordsmanship had remained calm, precise, and unfathomable from the very start of the conference.

The other was the Divine Son of a royal elven faction, the vessel of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline stolen from Max, and the wielder of the domineering Pseudo Cosmic Path known as Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion.
This was no ordinary matchup. This was another true collision between peak geniuses.

The Divine Realm erupted once again. In the Sword God Palace, countless disciples gathered before massive screens with their eyes burning. Damian Voss had been too calm for too long, and many of them had waited eagerly for an opponent strong enough to force out his true sword.
"Senior Brother Damian!"
"Show the Divine Son the sword of our Sword God Palace!"
"Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion is strong, but no dominion can suppress the true sword!"
"Senior Brother Damian has not even used his real strength yet!"

At the same time, within the territories controlled by the second elven faction, countless elves watched with cold pride. To them, Aurelian Lareth was far more than a mere participant. He was their Divine Son, their symbol, and their living proof that their faction still stood above countless forces in both talent and bloodline.

His battle against Morgana had already put the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion on display, but now he faced Damian Voss, and many elders understood that this fight would determine how the Divine Realm judged his true standing among the peak.

chapters.title: Chapter 1860: A Quick Battle!
paragraphs: Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Max stood on his pillar and stared at the screen. His expression did not shift, but the air around him grew slightly colder. Aurelian, the Divine Son of the second faction, was the one who carried the stolen Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.
Max had already witnessed the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion during Aurelian’s battle against Morgana, but he knew perfectly well that Aurelian had not shown everything.
Someone raised as the Divine Son of the second faction could not possibly possess only that much, and this battle against Damian might finally drag more of it into the open.
Aurelian turned his head slightly and looked toward Max. For one brief moment their gazes met, and a faint smile touched Aurelian’s face. It was calm, arrogant, and cold.
Max did not smile back.
Then Damian Voss opened his eyes fully. He looked at Aurelian, and the sword intent around him grew faintly sharper. He did not raise his voice, and he showed neither anger nor excitement.
He simply stood there like a sword still resting in its sheath, quiet enough for fools to overlook and sharp enough to make true experts sense danger before the blade was ever drawn.
Aurelian looked away from Max and turned his gaze toward Damian. "So my opponent is you," he said calmly.
Damian’s expression did not change. "Yes."
Aurelian smiled faintly. "The Sword God Palace has been very quiet in this final stage."
Damian replied, "A sword does not need to make noise before cutting."
The words were spoken calmly, yet the arena tensed in an instant.
Rakan Thorne grinned from his pillar. "Good. This one should be fun too."

Orion Starfall, still recovering under the laws of the Eternal Hourglass, forced his eyes partway open and smiled weakly when he saw the pairing. "Of course. I faint for one moment, and another good battle starts."
Morgana Starveil looked between Damian and Aurelian with shining eyes. "This will be dangerous."
Kaiden Voidmere said softly, "Sword authority against divine light authority."
Ervin’s gaze deepened. "No, it is more than that. Damian has not revealed his path yet."
Revona, still pale from her fight with Orion, opened her eyes and regarded the stage with rare seriousness. Even after her exhausting battle, this match was important enough to hold her attention.
Angelina Valerius looked down at the two named participants.
"Damian Voss."
Her gaze shifted.
"Aurelian Lareth."
The transfer lights began gathering above their pillars.
"Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended, one carrying a silent sword sharpness and the other carrying a golden-white divine radiance. The next great battle of the final competitive stage was about to begin.

The two beams faded from the central stage. Damian Voss stood on one side with his sword still sheathed, his posture calm and his eyes deep. He released no violent aura and made no attempt to smother the stage with sword intent the moment he landed, yet the space around him felt unnaturally keen, as though the air itself were being quietly divided into invisible lines.
Aurelian Lareth stood opposite him with golden-white radiance flowing around his body like a sacred cloak. Compared to Damian’s silence, Aurelian’s presence was far more majestic.

His pale golden hair drifted behind him, his eyes shone with divine light, and every breath he drew carried the oppressive dignity of the second elven faction’s Divine Son. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline within him had already begun to stir, and to Max, that light still felt unpleasantly familiar.
Angelina Valerius looked down at the two of them.
[Battle Begins.]

The moment those words appeared, Damian moved. He announced no technique and made no show of raising his sword slowly. His hand simply brushed the hilt, and a thin sword light flashed into being between him and Aurelian.
Aurelian’s eyes narrowed.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Mirror Guard."
A golden-white mirror of light formed before his body, and the sword light struck it.
Crack!

The mirror split apart instantly, but before its broken fragments could scatter, Aurelian had already raised his hand. Thousands of golden spears materialized above him and shot toward Damian like divine punishment descending from the heavens.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Spear Rain."
Damian stepped forward, and his sword left its sheath.
"Silent Sword Art, First Cut, Parting Wind."

A single horizontal slash swept across the stage. It did not look grand at first glance, but the moment it met the descending spears, all the golden-white light in front of Damian was cleaved into two clean halves. The sword light passed through the spear rain without slowing, splitting hundreds of radiant spears before fading near Aurelian’s position.
Aurelian raised one finger.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sunwheel Descent."

A golden sunwheel appeared above his head and descended with burning divine pressure. Its edges spun like a sacred blade, and the light pouring from it carried a purifying heat intense enough to set the arena barrier glowing.
Damian’s expression did not waver. He stepped sideways with a movement so small that many spectators barely registered it, and then his sword rose.
"Sword God Palace, Falling Peak Sword."
The slash descended from above like a mountain forged from sword intent, and the Falling Peak Sword collided with the Sunwheel Descent.
Boom!
The central stage shook violently as golden light and sword force detonated together. Aurelian was the first to move through the explosion, his body wrapped in a layer of radiant armor.
"Heavenly Luminance Battle Form, Divine Step."
His speed spiked sharply. In an instant he appeared before Damian and struck with a palm brimming with golden-white power.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Palm Seal."

Damian turned his sword and blocked with the flat of the blade. The palm struck the steel, and a dull explosion rolled outward. Damian slid back half a step while Aurelian’s radiant palm seared a burning mark into the air, and before Damian could fully counter, Aurelian’s other hand had already shaped a spear of light and thrust it toward his chest.
"Heavenly Luminance, Piercing Dawn Spear."
Damian shifted his body and let the spear slide past his ribs by a hair’s width, and in the same motion his sword swept upward toward Aurelian’s wrist.
"Silent Sword Art, Second Cut, Returning Thread."
Aurelian snatched his hand back instantly, but the sword light still grazed his sleeve and sliced through the golden-white defensive layer covering his arm.
The spectators burst into excitement at once.
"So fast!"
"They are opening directly with high-level moves!"
"Damian’s sword is too precise!"
"Aurelian is keeping up in close combat too!"
