He stepped sideways with a movement so small that many spectators barely registered it, and then his sword rose.
"Sword God Palace, Falling Peak Sword."
The slash descended from above like a mountain forged from sword intent, and the Falling Peak Sword collided with the Sunwheel Descent.
Boom!
The central stage shook violently as golden light and sword force detonated together.
Aurelian was the first to move through the explosion, his body wrapped in a layer of radiant armor.
"Heavenly Luminance Battle Form, Divine Step."
His speed spiked sharply.
In an instant he appeared before Damian and struck with a palm brimming with golden-white power.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Palm Seal."
Damian turned his sword and blocked with the flat of the blade.
The palm struck the steel, and a dull explosion rolled outward.

Damian slid back half a step while Aurelian’s radiant palm seared a burning mark into the air, and before Damian could fully counter, Aurelian’s other hand had already shaped a spear of light and thrust it toward his chest.
"Heavenly Luminance, Piercing Dawn Spear."
Damian shifted his body and let the spear slide past his ribs by a hair’s width, and in the same motion his sword swept upward toward Aurelian’s wrist.
"Silent Sword Art, Second Cut, Returning Thread."
Aurelian snatched his hand back instantly, but the sword light still grazed his sleeve and sliced through the golden-white defensive layer covering his arm.
The spectators burst into excitement at once.
"So fast!"
"They are opening directly with high-level moves!"
"Damian’s sword is too precise!"
"Aurelian is keeping up in close combat too!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1861: Damian’s Pseudo Cosmic Path!
paragraphs: Aurelian’s expression cooled further. He stepped back, and the radiance around him erupted outward.
"Heavenly Luminance, Twelve Sacred Wings."

Twelve wings woven from golden-white light unfurled behind him. Each wing shed countless feathers of light, and every feather carried sharpness, purification, and explosive force all at once. The twelve wings beat a single time, and the entire stage filled with golden feathers streaking toward Damian from every direction.
Damian finally raised his sword with both hands, and his sword intent expanded.
"Sword God Palace, Ten Thousand Line Sword Formation."

Thin lines of sword light bloomed around Damian, numbering dozens at first, then hundreds, and then thousands. They crisscrossed the air like invisible threads made visible for a single breath. The golden feathers struck those lines and were sliced apart one after another, until the stage became a storm of broken light and fragmented sword intent with neither side giving ground.
Aurelian moved again. He passed through the collapsing golden feathers and appeared above Damian with one hand raised high.
"Heavenly Luminance, Crowned Sun Judgment."

A vast crown of light materialized above his palm, and from within that crown descended a pillar of golden-white power. The attack was not as complete as his full Pseudo Cosmic Path, yet it already carried a trace of divine judgment authority. The pillar plunged straight toward Damian, seeking to crush his sword intent from above.
Damian looked up, and for the first time his eyes grew colder.
"Sword God Palace, Heaven-Cutting Ascension."

His sword rose, and a straight lance of sword light shot upward. It bit into the descending pillar and split it from the center, forcing the golden-white radiance to part around him like a river divided by a cliff. The sword light continued its climb and struck the crown above Aurelian’s hand.
Crack!
The crown shattered. Aurelian’s eyes sharpened, and he descended immediately with both hands aglow.
"Heavenly Luminance, Twin Divine Seals."
Two golden-white seals formed in his palms and pressed in toward Damian from the left and the right. Damian turned his body as his sword traced a narrow arc.
"Silent Sword Art, Third Cut, Moonless Return."

The blade vanished for an instant, and then two sword lights appeared at the same moment. One struck the left seal while the other struck the right, and both seals shattered together, though the impact drove Damian and Aurelian apart in opposite directions.

For a breath, the two stood at a distance once more, and neither had claimed a clear advantage. The opening exchange had been brief, yet it had already shaken the arena. They had flowed from close combat to long-range suppression, from sword formations to divine seals, and from palm strikes to crown judgment, and every single collision had carried enough power to crush an ordinary participant of the final stage. Yet between Damian and Aurelian, those attacks had been nothing more than probes.
Aurelian glanced at the cut on his sleeve and then at Damian’s sword. "You are worthy of the Sword God Palace," he said calmly.
Damian lowered his blade slightly. "And you are worthy of being called Divine Son."
Aurelian smiled faintly. "Then ordinary moves are meaningless."
Damian did not deny it, and the air around the stage changed yet again.
On the pillars, the top geniuses sharpened their focus.
Rakan Thorne grinned. "Now they are finally starting."
Orion Starfall, still pale with exhaustion, forced himself to keep watching with bright eyes. "Good. Do not disappoint me after making me miss the beginning."
Revona sat in silence, but her gaze never strayed from the stage.
Kaiden Voidmere said softly, "Aurelian has already shown his path once. Damian has not."
Ervin’s eyes deepened. "This will be Damian’s first reveal."

Max watched Damian carefully. He had always known the man was dangerous. The Sword God Palace would never raise an ordinary genius as its strongest participant, and Damian’s sword had never once felt shallow. Yet until this moment, Damian had never truly opened the depths of his path.

Aurelian raised his hand first. Golden-white light erupted behind him, taking the shape of sacred halls, radiant pillars, and a divine throne resting beneath an endless sun. The same domineering kingdom of light from his battle against Morgana began to manifest again, but this time it felt more complete.
The Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion descended with far greater pressure than before, and the golden-white crown above Aurelian’s head shone with new clarity.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path," Aurelian said calmly.
The divine kingdom spread wide behind him.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."
Boom!

The entire stage was swallowed in golden-white authority. Aurelian’s aura surged, and within the dominion his light was no longer a mere weapon. It was command, it was judgment, and it was purification. It was the authority of a divine king forcing the battlefield itself to bow before his will.

But Damian did not retreat. He stood beneath the crushing pressure of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion with his sword lowered at his side, and for a moment his figure looked almost small against the vast divine kingdom looming behind Aurelian.
Then Damian closed his eyes. The sword in his hand released a soft sound, and it was not the ring of metal. It was like the first note of a blade being born at the very beginning of heaven and earth.
The stage grew quiet. The golden-white light pressing toward Damian suddenly slowed, and Aurelian’s eyes narrowed.
Damian opened his eyes, and the sharpness within them was no longer ordinary sword intent. It was older, purer, and far more terrifying.
Behind Damian, an illusory sword world began to take form. At first there was only a single sword standing upright in a boundless void, ancient, simple, and silent.

Then the emptiness around it opened outward, revealing mountains built from sword edges, rivers flowing with sword light, skies etched with sword marks, and countless broken weapons buried beneath an endless sword altar. Above that altar floated a vast palace, formed neither of stone nor of light but woven entirely from condensed sword law.
At the highest point of the palace stood a throne, and that throne was empty. Before the empty throne, a single sword hung point-downward, as though waiting for someone worthy to claim it.
Damian’s voice rang across the stage.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."
The sword world expanded.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven."

chapters.title: Chapter 1862: Sword Sovereign Heaven!
paragraphs: The moment the name was spoken, every sword in the arena trembled. Damian’s own blade trembled, the swords of the participants trembled, and even the weapons carried by spectators far beyond the Eternal Hourglass shivered in their sheaths.
Even Dragonheart at Max’s waist released a faint vibration, not out of fear, but in acknowledgment that a mighty sword path had arrived.
Across the Divine Realm, countless swordsmen shot to their feet in shock. Inside the Sword God Palace, the disciples fell silent for the space of one breath, and then the entire palace erupted.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven!"
"Senior Brother Damian revealed it!"
"That is his Pseudo Cosmic Path!"
"It is one of the supreme sword paths of the younger generation!"
"No wonder the elders said he was born to inherit the Sword God’s battlefield!"

Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven felt nothing like a normal sword technique, nor did it resemble a simple domain. It was a world in which the sword stood above all other weapons, a place where every mountain, river, cloud, and shadow existed as an extension of sword authority. Within it, Damian’s sword intent did not merely grow sharper.

It became sovereign. It judged other powers through the purity of the blade, and it could cut force, cut light, cut laws, cut rhythm, and even cut the command hidden behind an enemy’s technique, provided Damian’s understanding ran deep enough.
Max’s eyes sharpened slightly.
’Sword Sovereign Heaven,’ he thought. ’So this is Damian’s path.’

Dragonheart grew still again at his waist, but Max could feel that the sword had responded. Damian’s path was not as forbidden as the Emotion Severing Path, not as primal as the Divine King Punishment, and not as mysterious as the Abyssal Origin Descent, yet in terms of pure sword authority it stood among the strongest Pseudo Cosmic Paths Max had witnessed anywhere in the Divine Realm.

For the first time, Aurelian’s expression turned truly serious. His Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion blazed brighter, pressing its golden-white authority against Damian’s sword world. Damian raised his blade, and the Sword Sovereign Heaven behind him answered.

Countless sword lights rose from the mountains, the rivers, the altar, and the palace. Aurelian’s divine throne glowed beneath its endless sun, and golden-white light collided with pure sword authority at the center of the stage before either man had even moved.
Boom!

The barrier shook, and spectators across the Divine Realm held their breath. Two majestic Pseudo Cosmic Paths had finally met. Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion stood against Sword Sovereign Heaven, and the true battle between Damian Voss and Aurelian Lareth had begun.

The collision between the two paths set the entire central stage trembling. Golden-white divine authority pressed forward from Aurelian’s side like an endless sacred kingdom descending from the sun. Radiant halls, divine pillars, sacred crowns, and a golden throne beneath an eternally blazing sky poured out waves of judgment, purification, and domination.
Every ray of light seemed to carry an edict, and every edict sought to force Damian’s sword world to lower itself before the authority of the Divine Son.

Opposite him, Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven refused to retreat. The ancient sword world expanded in silence. The mountains of sword edges climbed higher, the rivers of sword light flowed faster, and the endless sword altar gleamed with cold brilliance while the countless broken weapons buried beneath it trembled, as though acknowledging the arrival of a true sovereign of the blade.
Above the sword palace, the empty throne kept its silence, but the single sword hanging before it slowly turned until its tip pointed toward Aurelian’s divine kingdom.
The pressure between the two Pseudo Cosmic Paths grew terrifying. One side demanded that all things be judged beneath divine light, and the other demanded that all things be cut beneath the sword.
Aurelian raised his hand first.
"Divine Dominion, Luminance Decree."
A golden-white decree unfurled above the stage like a sacred scroll written in light, and the moment it opened, countless words of radiance rained down toward Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven.

Each word carried the power to suppress sword intent, purify hostile energy, and bind the movement of the blade. The decree did not merely target Damian himself. It attempted to command the sword world behind him to dim.
Damian’s eyes stayed calm as he lifted his sword slightly.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, First Edict, All Blades Refuse Submission."

The sword altar behind him released a piercing hum, and countless sword lights rose from the ground to meet the descending words of radiance. Every sword light was thin, yet every one of them carried a pure and absolute refusal to submit. When they collided with the golden-white decree, the sound resembled thousands of blades striking against divine chains.
Crack!

The Luminance Decree shuddered. Aurelian narrowed his eyes and pressed his palm downward, and the decree flared brighter while the sacred halls behind him poured out still more light. The pressure of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion multiplied several times over, bearing down on Damian’s sword world until the rivers of sword light began to churn violently.
Damian stepped forward, and his sword moved.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Second Edict, One Sword Divides Heaven."

A single sword light rose from his blade. It looked nowhere near as grand as Aurelian’s divine kingdom, nor as vast as the golden decree overhead, yet the instant it appeared, a chill ran through the heart of everyone watching.

The sword light traveled upward in a perfectly straight line and cut through the middle of the Luminance Decree. The decree split apart, and its sacred words of light shattered into countless fragments.

Aurelian’s expression grew colder, though he did not panic. His golden-white crown blazed, the divine throne behind him radiated majestic pressure, and twelve radiant pillars rose around the stage, each one covered in divine runes and all of them locking onto Damian at once.
"Divine Dominion, Twelve Pillars of Sacred Judgment."
The twelve pillars fired beams of golden-white light in the same instant.
Damian turned his sword.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Sword River Encircles The Throne."

The river of sword light behind him surged forward and coiled around Damian like a flowing silver dragon forged from blades. The twelve beams crashed down into the sword river and birthed a storm of shattered light and broken sword sparks. The stage cracked beneath Damian under the strain, but he did not yield a single step.
Then Aurelian vanished from where he stood.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Step."
He reappeared above Damian with a spear of divine light in his hand.
"Divine Dominion, Sacred Sun Spear."

The spear plunged toward Damian’s head with terrifying speed. This was no long-range beam. It was a close combat strike empowered by the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, carrying the full weight of Aurelian’s bloodline and his Pseudo Cosmic Path together, and it burned so brightly that it looked capable of piercing a star.

"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Third Edict, Blade Meets The Sun."
Sword and spear collided.
Boom!

The impact rocked the entire arena. Golden-white light exploded downward while pure sword force erupted upward. Damian’s feet sank into the stage, and Aurelian’s arm shook faintly from the force traveling back through his spear. The two remained locked together for a breath, their eyes meeting through the blaze of light.
Aurelian’s voice was cold. "Your sword is sharp."
Damian replied calmly, "Your light is heavy."

Then both of them attacked at once. Aurelian’s spear fell like a descending sun while Damian’s sword moved like a silent line drawn through the world, and they clashed at the center of the stage again and again. Divine light scorched the air, and sword light carved through that radiance in turn.

Aurelian’s attacks were majestic, forceful, and domineering, while Damian’s sword remained clean, precise, and terrifyingly decisive. Every time Aurelian sought to suppress him with divine authority, Damian’s sword severed the command hidden within the light, and every time Damian tried to pierce Aurelian’s defense, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion wove another layer of sacred protection around its master.

It held power, it held majesty, and it held oppressive divine authority, yet beneath all of it, Max could still sense the unnatural mismatch between Aurelian and the bloodline dwelling inside him. That bloodline had not been born with him. It had been taken.
On the stage, Aurelian’s eyes grew colder as he realized Damian was not being overwhelmed. He raised one hand toward the divine throne behind him.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Royal Mandate of the Endless Sun."

The endless sun above the divine kingdom released a vast pillar of golden-white power, and that pillar did not fall toward Damian. It descended upon Aurelian himself, sending his aura surging upward. His crown grew more solid, his spear burned brighter, and his entire body seemed to take on the judgment of a divine ruler.
Aurelian stepped forward, and the stage beneath him melted into radiant lines.
"Divine Dominion, Sun King’s Execution."

The spear in his hand swelled into a massive blade of golden-white light, and he swung it toward Damian with the full authority of the endless sun at his back. The attack blanketed half the stage and left almost nowhere to evade.

Damian finally drew a deeper breath, and the Sword Sovereign Heaven behind him changed. The empty throne within the sword palace released a faint glow, and the single sword hanging before that throne descended by a fraction.
Damian raised his sword with both hands.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Fourth Edict, Palace Sword Descends."

The sword before the throne cast out a projection, and that projection sank into Damian’s blade. In an instant, his aura turned terrifyingly sharp. His entire body seemed to merge with the sword world at his back, and the blade in his grip no longer looked like a weapon held by a man. It looked like the judgment of the Sword Sovereign Heaven made manifest.
He slashed. The sword met the Sun King’s Execution, and for one moment the entire stage split into halves, one of golden-white light and one of pure silver sword radiance.
Then the golden-white blade broke apart.

Aurelian’s pupils contracted. The sword light did not stop after cleaving through the Sun King’s Execution. It swept onward, struck Aurelian’s sacred armor, and drove him backward for the first time since both Pseudo Cosmic Paths had fully opened. A thin line opened across his chest, and golden-white blood seeped from the wound.
The arena erupted.
"Aurelian was injured!"
"Damian cut through the Sun King’s Execution!"
"That Sword Sovereign Heaven is too strong!"
"The Divine Son is being pushed!"

Inside the viewing halls of the second elven faction, the atmosphere turned frigid. Many elders stared at the screen with dark faces. Aurelian’s injury was not severe, but the meaning behind it could not be ignored. His Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion had been cut open by Damian’s sword.
At the Sword God Palace, countless disciples roared.
"Senior Brother Damian!"
"Sword Sovereign Heaven!"
"Cut down the divine light!"
Aurelian looked down at the wound across his chest, and his face emptied of expression. Then the golden-white light around him began to change. It grew purer, hotter, and far more dangerous.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
’He is drawing deeper from the stolen bloodline.’
Aurelian slowly raised his head. "You are strong enough to make me use this," he said.
Damian’s expression remained calm. "Then use it."

Aurelian’s crown flared, and the golden-white throne behind him shattered. The divine kingdom did not collapse. Instead, the fragments of the throne streamed into Aurelian’s body, fusing with his bloodline and driving his aura up to a level that was less stable but far more terrifying. Sacred runes surfaced across his skin, and the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion condensed around him into a smaller and denser form.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Crownless Divine King."
Boom!

The pressure of Aurelian’s path transformed completely. If his earlier dominion had been the authority of a ruler seated upon a divine throne, then this state was the ruler abandoning that throne and turning himself into the instrument of judgment.

The sacred halls vanished, the radiant pillars vanished, and even the endless sun dimmed, for all the authority of the dominion had gathered into Aurelian’s body and spear. His speed increased, his strength increased, and his divine light condensed to a far greater density.
Aurelian moved and appeared in front of Damian in an instant.
"Crownless Divine King, Light That Judges All Blades."

His spear thrust forward, and the golden-white light around it wove countless judgment runes aimed directly at Damian’s sword. The attack did not target Damian’s body first. It targeted his blade, his sword intent, and the very connection between him and the Sword Sovereign Heaven.
Damian’s eyes sharpened.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Fifth Edict, Sword Heart Cannot Be Judged."

His sword met the spear. The judgment runes coiled around the blade and strained to suppress it, but Damian’s sword heart released a single pure vibration, and the runes cracked apart one by one. Aurelian, however, had already flowed into his next attack.
"Crownless Divine King, Radiant Execution Step."

Aurelian’s body flickered around Damian, trailing several golden-white afterimages, and each afterimage stabbed out with a spear of light carrying divine judgment authority. Damian’s sword answered with terrifying precision, blocking, cutting, and redirecting each strike in turn, but this time Aurelian’s speed and pressure clearly outstripped everything that had come before.

Damian was forced back one step, then a second, and then a third. At last Aurelian’s spear broke through Damian’s net of sword light and pierced his shoulder. Blood splashed across the stage, and for one breath the disciples of the Sword God Palace fell silent.
Aurelian’s eyes were cold. "Even the sword bleeds."

chapters.title: Chapter 1864: Damian Wins!
paragraphs: Damian looked at the spear buried in his shoulder, and then he looked at Aurelian.
"Yes," he said calmly. "But it does not stop cutting."
His left hand closed around the spear’s shaft. Aurelian’s eyes narrowed, and Damian stepped forward instead of retreating, allowing the spear to sink a little deeper as his sword rose from below.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Sixth Edict, Bleeding Sword Severance."

Aurelian tried at once to withdraw, but Damian’s hand pinned the spear in place for that single fraction of a breath, and that fraction was enough. The sword light flashed, Aurelian’s radiant spear was sheared in half, and in the same instant a deep sword wound opened across Aurelian’s right arm.

Aurelian retreated sharply, and his expression finally broke. Damian pulled the severed spear tip from his shoulder and let it clatter onto the stage. Blood ran freely down his arm, yet his sword remained perfectly steady.
The arena went silent once more.
Rakan Thorne laughed under his breath. "That guy is ruthless."
Orion’s eyes shone weakly. "That is a swordsman."
Kaiden Voidmere said softly, "He accepted the wound to create a cutting chance."
Ervin’s gaze stayed deep. "Damian’s calmness is more dangerous."

On the stage, Aurelian’s face grew colder and colder. His golden-white blood dripped from his arm, but the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion still burned around him. The Crownless Divine King state had granted him greater power, and Damian had cut through it at close range regardless.

Aurelian raised both hands, and the broken spear of light dissolved. Behind him, the dimmed endless sun suddenly compressed into a single golden-white point, and the pressure radiating from that point was terrifying. Damian looked up, and the Sword Sovereign Heaven behind him grew quieter in answer.
Aurelian’s voice rang out like a divine decree.
"Crownless Divine King, Final Luminance Judgment."

The golden-white point expanded into a colossal divine sword of light. It was no longer a spear at all. It was a blade of judgment forged from Aurelian’s dominion, his bloodline, and his crownless state combined, and it carried enough power to burn straight through the sword world standing before Damian.
The Divine Realm held its breath. Aurelian swung his hand down, and the massive divine sword descended.

Damian stood beneath it with his shoulder bleeding, his clothes torn, and his aura drained far beyond anything the battle had cost him before. Yet his eyes remained calm, and he raised his sword one final time.

The Sword Sovereign Heaven behind him changed once more. The empty throne within the sword palace began to shine, the countless swords buried in the altar rose as one, the sword mountains bowed their peaks, and the sword rivers ceased to flow. Everything in the sword world turned toward Damian’s blade.
Damian spoke quietly.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven."
His voice was not loud, yet every swordsman across the Divine Realm heard it echo in their hearts.
"Final Edict."
The sword hanging before the empty throne dissolved into light and poured completely into his blade.
"Throne Of The Only Sword."
Boom!

For one instant, every other sword light in existence vanished, and only Damian’s sword remained. There was no river, no mountain, no palace, no altar, and no host of countless blades. There was only one sword, and because only one sword remained, that sword became absolute.
Damian slashed upward, and the single sword light met Aurelian’s Final Luminance Judgment.
The collision was silent at first. Then the colossal divine sword of light cracked.
Aurelian’s expression changed drastically. "No."

The crack spread from the tip into the body, and from the body into the core, and then the entire Final Luminance Judgment split apart. Damian’s sword light passed through it, crossed the stage, cut through the remaining authority of the Crownless Divine King, and sliced through Aurelian’s sacred armor before stopping just short of his throat.

A thin line of blood appeared on Aurelian’s neck. The divine light around him shattered, and the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion collapsed behind him, its sacred halls breaking apart, its radiant pillars toppling, and its endless sun dimming into scattered motes of gold.
Aurelian stood frozen in place. Damian stood opposite him with his sword still raised and blood flowing from his wounded shoulder. For several breaths, no one spoke at all.
Then Angelina Valerius’s voice rang across the arena.
"Aurelian Lareth is unable to continue."
The screen above the stage changed.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Aurelian Lareth Defeated.]

The entire Divine Realm plunged into shocked silence, and then the Sword God Palace erupted. Their disciples screamed Damian’s name until the skies above their palace shook. Elders who had watched with perfect composure until now finally allowed themselves to smile, and countless swords rose from their sheaths as though saluting the Sword Sovereign Heaven.
Damian had defeated the Divine Son of the second elven faction and had revealed one of the strongest Pseudo Cosmic Paths in the Divine Realm before the eyes of everyone.

At that same moment, the territories of the second elven faction fell deathly quiet. Aurelian Lareth had lost. Their Divine Son, the bearer of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline and the one expected to display absolute dominance over his generation, had been cut down by Damian Voss in front of the entire Divine Realm.

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Max watched the defeated Aurelian without blinking. There was no joy on his face. There was only cold clarity. Aurelian was strong, and in truth he was very strong, for both his Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion and his Crownless Divine King state were terrifying.
But he was not invincible. His stolen light could bleed, his dominion could be cut, and his pride could be broken.

Damian slowly lowered his sword. Aurelian’s face had gone pale, and his golden eyes churned with disbelief, humiliation, and cold fury. His body trembled as though he wished to keep fighting, but the sword light that had rested before his throat made the result impossible to deny.
Damian regarded him calmly. "You are strong," Damian said.
Aurelian’s jaw tightened.
Damian continued, "I always felt your light attacks were strong but not stable. Either way, the result wouldn’t have changed."

The words struck Aurelian harder than the sword wound had. Max’s eyes sharpened. Aurelian stared at Damian with a cold and dangerous gaze, but before he could speak, the transfer light descended and returned him to his pillar.
Damian returned to his own pillar a moment later. The laws of the Eternal Hourglass began mending his shoulder, yet the sword aura around him remained sharp and steady.
The screen above the arena updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Damian Voss]
[Total Battles Fought: 5]
[Total Wins: 5]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Aurelian Lareth]
[Total Battles Fought: 4]
[Total Wins: 3]
The result shone above everyone. Damian Voss had won, and Aurelian Lareth had lost, and with that victory, the final competitive stage became even more unpredictable than before.

chapters.title: Chapter 1865: Max vs Selene!
paragraphs: After Damian Voss defeated Aurelian Lareth, the final competitive stage entered a long and relentless rhythm.

The shock of the Divine Son’s defeat had not fully faded, but Angelina Valerius did not allow the arena to remain frozen in that moment. The laws of the Eternal Hourglass continued rotating the names above the central stage, and battles fell one after another like rain.
Some were fierce enough to make the spectators focus, while others ended so quickly that the result appeared before the crowd could even finish discussing the previous match.
Damian Voss continued to advance with terrifying steadiness.
After defeating Aurelian, he met several participants below the top monster level and won without revealing Sword Sovereign Heaven again.
Against a flame halberd genius, he used "Silent Sword Art, Fourth Cut, Withered Flame" and severed the heart of the flame technique before the halberd could descend.
Against a storm-winged woman, he used "Falling Peak Sword" to cut through her speed route and stopped his blade at her throat.
Against a defensive earth cultivator, he used only one vertical slash and split all nine layers of stone armor apart. His battle count climbed quickly, and his win count remained perfect.

Aurelian also continued fighting, but after losing to Damian, the air around him had changed. His victories were still clean. His Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion still suppressed most opponents before they could resist properly.
He defeated Hadeon Granite with "Luminance Decree," defeated Yelric Flamehorn with "Sacred Sun Judgment," and defeated a hidden spear genius with "Crownless Divine King, Radiant Execution Step."
Yet every time he returned to his pillar, his face remained cold and unpleasant. No matter how many weaker opponents he defeated, the wound Damian left behind could not be erased from his pride.

Orion Starfall recovered slowly under the laws of the Eternal Hourglass and returned to battle with a smile on his face, though his aura was clearly not as full as before. Even so, anyone below the true peak could not withstand him.

He defeated a thunder-winged woman with "Hundred Star Descent," defeated a beast-blooded warrior with "Second Star Step" and "Fourth Star Knee," and forced a soul-path participant to surrender with "Nine Star Court, Celestial Pressure Field."
Every victory reminded the Divine Realm that although Orion had lost to Revona, he had only lost after pushing her to the edge.

Revona, on the other hand, fought less aggressively after her exhausting battle with Orion, but that did not make her any easier to face. Her Void Origin Eyes remained terrifying. She defeated two opponents without using Void Origin Realm, simply erasing their strongest attacks until they understood the gap and surrendered.
Against a poison mist cultivator, she only opened her eyes once, and the entire poison field vanished as if it had never existed. Her battle count climbed steadily, and her record remained spotless.
Rakan Thorne also recovered his momentum. After his loss to Max, the War God Palace disciples had been quiet for a while, but Rakan quickly reminded everyone why he was the first Warlord.

He crushed one opponent with the First Limit of the War God Body, defeated another with the Second Limit, and did not need the Third Limit again unless the opponent truly had enough strength to withstand a few exchanges.
His loss to Max remained shocking, but no one dared to use that loss to underestimate him, because every participant who faced him afterward was beaten down with overwhelming physical force.
Kaiden Voidmere continued to win with quiet efficiency. He folded space, erased movement paths, and made techniques collapse before their full power could erupt.
Morgana Starveil also gathered several wins with her curse arts, though she sometimes took longer because her opponents had begun defending against her curses more carefully.
Fin Arclight remained dangerous with Pale Eclipse Burial, while Seren Frostveil recovered from her early loss and won several battles using Frozen World Stillness.
The records above the arena changed constantly.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Damian Voss]
[Total Battles Fought: 12]
[Total Wins: 12]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 11]
[Total Wins: 11]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 10]
[Total Wins: 10]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rakan Thorne]
[Total Battles Fought: 13]
[Total Wins: 12]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Aurelian Lareth]
[Total Battles Fought: 12]
[Total Wins: 11]
The battles kept moving.
Max also received several easier opponents during this stretch.

One of them was a blood-armor cultivator who tried to trap Max with a crimson prison. Max walked through it and shattered the prison with one punch. Another was a wind-attribute swordsman who relied on speed, but Max caught the blade between two fingers and forced him to surrender before the second exchange.
A third was a soul-path participant who tried to attack Max’s consciousness, only for the attack to vanish into the Dimension of Soul without causing even the slightest ripple.

Against those opponents, Max did not use Dragonheart, did not reveal Emotion Severing Path, did not open the Seven Divine Veins, and did not use Draconic Essences. His base strength alone was already enough.
Slowly, everyone’s battle count passed ten.
Then twelve.
Then fourteen.
Finally, the records of almost every remaining participant crossed fifteen battles.
At this point, the final competitive stage became even heavier. The weak had already collected many losses. The mid-level geniuses were struggling to preserve decent records.
The top monsters were beginning to look toward one another more often, because most of the easier matches had already passed. Every remaining major pairing would affect the final rankings.
Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand once again.
The giant screen spun.
The names rotated through the air in bright lines.
Max Morgan.
Selene Vaeloria.
Aurelian Lareth.
Kaiden Voidmere.
Ervin.
Rosaline Lunara.
Morgana Starveil.
Rakan Thorne.
Damian Voss.
Revona.
The light slowed.
The first name appeared.
[Max Morgan]
The arena immediately became alert.
Then the second name stopped.
[Selene Vaeloria]
The screen enlarged both names.
[Max Morgan vs Selene Vaeloria]
A strange silence fell over the arena.
This pairing carried a different meaning.

Max and Selene had already fought near the Witch God Tree. Everyone who had watched the earlier events remembered that battle. Selene had used her Heavenly Luminance Genesis and Spear of First Dawn, yet Max had still defeated her.

Since then, Max had revealed even more terrifying strength. He had defeated Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, crushed Rakan in a pure body battle, and continued winning without exposing his full power.

The shock of the Divine Son’s defeat had not fully faded, but Angelina Valerius did not allow the arena to remain frozen in that moment.
The laws of the Eternal Hourglass continued rotating the names above the central stage, and battles fell one after another like rain.
Some were fierce enough to make the spectators focus, while others ended so quickly that the result appeared before the crowd could even finish discussing the previous match.
Damian Voss continued to advance with terrifying steadiness.
After defeating Aurelian, he met several participants below the top monster level and won without revealing Sword Sovereign Heaven again.
Against a flame halberd genius, he used "Silent Sword Art, Fourth Cut, Withered Flame" and severed the heart of the flame technique before the halberd could descend.
Against a storm-winged woman, he used "Falling Peak Sword" to cut through her speed route and stopped his blade at her throat.
Against a defensive earth cultivator, he used only one vertical slash and split all nine layers of stone armor apart.
His battle count climbed quickly, and his win count remained perfect.
Aurelian also continued fighting, but after losing to Damian, the air around him had changed.
His victories were still clean.
His Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion still suppressed most opponents before they could resist properly.
He defeated Hadeon Granite with "Luminance Decree," defeated Yelric Flamehorn with "Sacred Sun Judgment," and defeated a hidden spear genius with "Crownless Divine King, Radiant Execution Step."
Yet every time he returned to his pillar, his face remained cold and unpleasant.
No matter how many weaker opponents he defeated, the wound Damian left behind could not be erased from his pride.
Orion Starfall recovered slowly under the laws of the Eternal Hourglass and returned to battle with a smile on his face, though his aura was clearly not as full as before.
Even so, anyone below the true peak could not withstand him.

He defeated a thunder-winged woman with "Hundred Star Descent," defeated a beast-blooded warrior with "Second Star Step" and "Fourth Star Knee," and forced a soul-path participant to surrender with "Nine Star Court, Celestial Pressure Field."
Every victory reminded the Divine Realm that although Orion had lost to Revona, he had only lost after pushing her to the edge.
Revona, on the other hand, fought less aggressively after her exhausting battle with Orion, but that did not make her any easier to face.
Her Void Origin Eyes remained terrifying.
She defeated two opponents without using Void Origin Realm, simply erasing their strongest attacks until they understood the gap and surrendered.
Against a poison mist cultivator, she only opened her eyes once, and the entire poison field vanished as if it had never existed.
Her battle count climbed steadily, and her record remained spotless.
Rakan Thorne also recovered his momentum.
After his loss to Max, the War God Palace disciples had been quiet for a while, but Rakan quickly reminded everyone why he was the first Warlord.

He crushed one opponent with the First Limit of the War God Body, defeated another with the Second Limit, and did not need the Third Limit again unless the opponent truly had enough strength to withstand a few exchanges.
His loss to Max remained shocking, but no one dared to use that loss to underestimate him, because every participant who faced him afterward was beaten down with overwhelming physical force.
Kaiden Voidmere continued to win with quiet efficiency.
He folded space, erased movement paths, and made techniques collapse before their full power could erupt.
Morgana Starveil also gathered several wins with her curse arts, though she sometimes took longer because her opponents had begun defending against her curses more carefully.
Fin Arclight remained dangerous with Pale Eclipse Burial, while Seren Frostveil recovered from her early loss and won several battles using Frozen World Stillness.
The records above the arena changed constantly.

The battles kept moving.
Max also received several easier opponents during this stretch.
One of them was a blood-armor cultivator who tried to trap Max with a crimson prison.
Max walked through it and shattered the prison with one punch.
Another was a wind-attribute swordsman who relied on speed, but Max caught the blade between two fingers and forced him to surrender before the second exchange.
A third was a soul-path participant who tried to attack Max’s consciousness, only for the attack to vanish into the Dimension of Soul without causing even the slightest ripple.
Against those opponents, Max did not use Dragonheart, did not reveal Emotion Severing Path, did not open the Seven Divine Veins, and did not use Draconic Essences.
His base strength alone was already enough.
Slowly, everyone’s battle count passed ten.
Then twelve.
Then fourteen.
Finally, the records of almost every remaining participant crossed fifteen battles.
At this point, the final competitive stage became even heavier.
The weak had already collected many losses.
The mid-level geniuses were struggling to preserve decent records.
The top monsters were beginning to look toward one another more often, because most of the easier matches had already passed.
Every remaining major pairing would affect the final rankings.
Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand once again.
The giant screen spun.
The names rotated through the air in bright lines.
Max Morgan.
Selene Vaeloria.
Aurelian Lareth.
Kaiden Voidmere.
Ervin.
Rosaline Lunara.
Morgana Starveil.
Rakan Thorne.
Damian Voss.
Revona.
The light slowed.
The first name appeared.
[Max Morgan]
The arena immediately became alert.
Then the second name stopped.
[Selene Vaeloria]
The screen enlarged both names.
[Max Morgan vs Selene Vaeloria]
A strange silence fell over the arena.
This pairing carried a different meaning.
Max and Selene had already fought near the Witch God Tree.
Everyone who had watched the earlier events remembered that battle.
Selene had used her Heavenly Luminance Genesis and Spear of First Dawn, yet Max had still defeated her.
Since then, Max had revealed even more terrifying strength.
He had defeated Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, crushed Rakan in a pure body battle, and continued winning without exposing his full power.

chapters.title: Chapter 1866: Ervin vs Rosaline!
paragraphs: Selene stood on her pillar with a cold expression.
For a few breaths, she did not move.
Angelina looked toward them calmly.
"Max Morgan. Selene Vaeloria. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.
Max appeared on one side of the central stage.

Selene appeared opposite him, her white-gold hair moving gently behind her, her face pale but composed. She looked at Max silently. The Heavenly Luminance power inside her body stirred faintly, but it did not rise. No avatar appeared behind her. No Genesis light opened. No spear formed above the stage.
Max looked at her.
Selene clenched her hands for a moment.
Then she spoke coldly.
"I surrender."
The entire arena froze.
Even Max raised an eyebrow slightly.
Angelina Valerius looked at Selene for a breath, then announced calmly, "Selene Vaeloria has surrendered."
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Selene Vaeloria Defeated.]
The screen updated immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 16]
[Total Wins: 16]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Selene Vaeloria]
[Total Battles Fought: 16]
[Total Wins: 11]
The silence lasted for several breaths before whispers spread across the arena.
"She surrendered?"
"She did not even fight?"
"She already lost to Max before."
"After seeing what Max did to Rakan, perhaps she knew fighting was meaningless."
"But she is the Divine Daughter of the second faction."
On his pillar, Aurelian Lareth’s expression became ugly.
Disgust flashed in his eyes for a brief instant.

Selene had surrendered without fighting. To others, it might be a practical choice. To Aurelian, it was humiliation. The second faction’s Divine Daughter had stepped onto the stage before Max Morgan and given up without even raising her spear. It was not only her personal surrender. It felt like another stain on the prestige of their faction.
But Aurelian did not speak.
He only looked away coldly.

Selene noticed his expression, but she did not respond. Her hands remained clenched at her sides, yet her face stayed calm. She had fought Max before. She knew better than most what kind of pressure he carried.

After watching him defeat Rakan with one finger while using only one Divine Vein and a portion of his Draconic Essences, she understood that forcing a battle here would only result in a deeper humiliation.
Max watched her quietly.
He did not mock her.
The transfer light returned Selene to her pillar, and Max returned to his own.
The battles continued again.
Some matchups were quickly resolved.
[Kaiden Voidmere vs Hadeon Granite]
Kaiden Voidmere won after folding the ground beneath Hadeon’s defenses and making all his stone barriers collapse inward.
[Winner: Kaiden Voidmere.]
[Hadeon Granite Defeated.]
[Morgana Starveil vs Yelric Flamehorn]
Morgana Starveil won by placing a curse on Yelric’s flame core, making each burst of fire burn backward into his own armor until he surrendered.
[Winner: Morgana Starveil.]
[Yelric Flamehorn Defeated.]
[Rakan Thorne vs Corvin Nightsteel]
Rakan Thorne won with one punch after opening the First Limit of the War God Body.
[Winner: Rakan Thorne.]
[Corvin Nightsteel Defeated.]
[Damian Voss vs Seren Frostveil]

Seren Frostveil tried to freeze his sword rhythm with Frozen World Stillness, but Damian cut through the stillness with "Sword Sovereign Heaven, First Edict, All Blades Refuse Submission" and forced her to surrender after three exchanges.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Seren Frostveil Defeated.]
[Aurelian Lareth vs Fin Arclight]

Fin tried to trap Aurelian inside Pale Eclipse Burial, but Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion purified the eclipse field and shattered the Moonless Descent before it could fully form. Fin surrendered with an unwilling expression.
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Fin Arclight Defeated.]
[Orion Starfall vs Vaela Sunspire]
Orion won with "Nine Star Court, Hundred Star Descent," never needing to use Nine Star Sovereign Body.
[Winner: Orion Starfall.]
[Vaela Sunspire Defeated.]
[Revona vs Darius Stoneveil]
Darius Stoneveil surrendered after Revona erased three layers of his strongest defensive formation with one look.
[Winner: Revona.]
[Darius Stoneveil Defeated.]
The final competitive stage kept tightening.
Names appeared.
Battles ended.
Records updated.

Some participants had already lost any chance of reaching the top rankings, while others fought desperately to preserve their pride. The truly important names continued meeting one another, and every time two strong participants were called, the Divine Realm leaned closer to the screens.
Then the randomizer spun again.
The light slowed.
Two names appeared.
[Ervin vs Rosaline Lunara]
The arena grew quieter.

This was not a battle between the absolute highest-ranked monsters, but it was still important. Ervin had revealed the terrifying Abyssal Origin Descent against Selene and won, while Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary had already shown itself to be a powerful sealing and suppression Pseudo Cosmic Path.
Both of them had strong records. Both had already lost or struggled against the peak monsters. This battle would decide who could remain closer to the upper ranks.
Angelina raised her hand.
"Ervin. Rosaline Lunara. Enter the stage."
Two beams descended.
Ervin appeared with his black spear in hand, his aura still quiet and deep.

Rosaline appeared opposite him, golden-pink light already gathering around her body. She did not smile casually this time. After losing to Max, she had fought carefully and rebuilt her record, but Ervin was not someone she could treat lightly.
"I suppose holding back would be foolish," Rosaline said.
Ervin nodded. "Against you, yes."
Rosaline raised both hands.
Golden-pink light rose like dawn.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary."

The luminous kingdom appeared behind her, filled with rose-gold palaces, radiant walls, falling petals, and the great throne of dawn. The sanctuary spread across the stage, releasing sealing, purification, and sovereign binding power. Rosaline did not test slowly. She used her strongest battlefield control immediately.
"Dawn Edict, First Seal."
"Dawn Edict, Second Seal."
"Dawn Edict, Third Seal."

Three rose-gold seals descended toward Ervin, one targeting his body, one targeting his spear, and one targeting the dark energy flowing around him. At the same time, radiant chains rose from the floor, trying to bind his movement before he could open his abyssal path.
Ervin stepped forward.
His black spear moved once.
A dark spear line pierced through the first seal.

Then he twisted his wrist, and the spear line sank into the second seal like a shadow falling into deep water. The second seal dimmed but did not fully break. Rosaline’s sanctuary reinforced it immediately, and the third seal descended faster.

chapters.title: Chapter 1867: Five Undefeated Geniuses!
paragraphs: Ervin’s eyes sharpened slightly.
"Good control."
Rosaline’s expression remained serious. "I learned from my fight with Max that if I give someone like you space, I lose."
She raised her hand again.
"Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, Royal Mandate of Purifying Light."

A massive golden-pink pillar descended toward Ervin, carrying purification and sealing authority together. The light tried to purify his abyssal aura before it fully awakened, but Ervin’s spear struck upward, and a dark spiral formed around the tip.
"Abyss Spear Art, Hollow Descent Thrust."
The spear pierced into the golden-pink pillar.
The collision shook the stage.

Rosaline’s sanctuary brightened, and the rose-gold throne behind her released greater pressure. Ervin was forced back two steps, which immediately made the spectators realize that Rosaline’s control was working. She could not overpower him directly, but her sanctuary was restricting his rhythm and forcing him to spend more power to move.
Rosaline pressed the advantage.
"Dawn Edict, Fourth Seal."
A crown-shaped seal appeared above Ervin’s head.

At the same time, countless petals gathered around him, each one carrying a soft but dangerous binding light. Ervin’s spear swept out, tearing through hundreds of petals, but more appeared immediately. The Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary was not a simple attack. As long as it remained active, Rosaline could rebuild, reinforce, and suppress again and again.
Ervin finally stopped.
The air around him sank.
The smile on Rosaline’s face faded.
Ervin spoke calmly.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Abyssal Origin Descent."
The black sea appeared behind him.
The broken ancient gate rose from the depths.
The entire battlefield became heavier.

Rosaline’s golden-pink sanctuary trembled as the abyssal pressure spread through it. The petals slowed. The chains sank. The seals dimmed slightly, as if their authority was being dragged downward toward an unknown depth.
Rosaline gritted her teeth and raised both hands.
"Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, Final Dawn Edict, Sovereign Rose Spear."
The entire sanctuary compressed.

The rose-gold throne, the falling petals, the luminous palaces, and the sovereign binding power gathered into a single spear of dawn light. It shot toward Ervin with far more force than before, carrying the full majesty of Rosaline’s Pseudo Cosmic Path.
Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent opened wider.
The broken gate behind him released a deep, soundless pressure.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth."
The gate opened slightly.
The Sovereign Rose Spear struck it.

For several breaths, the golden-pink spear resisted the pull of the abyssal gate. Rosaline poured everything into it, and the dawn spear pierced deeper than many expected, forcing cracks to appear across the shadow surrounding the gate. Ervin’s expression became slightly more serious, and his hand tightened around his spear.
Rosaline was strong.
Her sanctuary was not enough to defeat him, but it was enough to force him to take her seriously.
Then Ervin stepped forward.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
The black sea rose.
The gate pulled.
The Sovereign Rose Spear trembled.

Rosaline’s face turned pale as the golden-pink light began sinking into the broken gate. She tried to maintain the spear, but the abyssal origin pressure dragged its authority downward layer by layer until the spear finally collapsed into scattered dawn fragments.
Ervin moved through those fragments.
His spear stopped before Rosaline’s throat.
Rosaline looked at the spear tip, then slowly lowered her hands.
"I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Rosaline Lunara Defeated.]
The screen updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Ervin]
[Total Battles Fought: 17]
[Total Wins: 17]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rosaline Lunara]
[Total Battles Fought: 17]
[Total Wins: 15]
Rosaline let out a soft breath as the transfer light descended.
"You are difficult to fight," she said.
Ervin withdrew his spear. "So are you."
Rosaline smiled faintly. "That is kind of you to say after swallowing my strongest attack."
Ervin’s expression remained calm. "It was strong enough to make the gate crack."
The transfer light carried both of them back to their pillars.
The arena remained thoughtful after that battle. Ervin had won, but Rosaline had proven again that Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary was not weak.

Against almost anyone below the peak monsters, her sealing and sovereign suppression would have been enough to control the entire fight. Unfortunately for her, Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent was one of the few paths capable of dragging that authority into a deeper darkness.
Max watched Ervin quietly.
That broken gate remained troublesome.
Even now, after seeing it twice, Max still felt that the black sea was only the surface.
The true danger lay behind the gate.
After Ervin defeated Rosaline Lunara, the final competitive stage continued moving forward with an even heavier momentum.

By now, almost every important participant had already crossed seventeen battles, and the records above the arena were beginning to look brutal. The ones at the top had separated themselves from the rest.

Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Revona, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Rakan Thorne, Orion Starfall, Aurelian Lareth, Morgana Starveil, Rosaline Lunara, Selene Vaeloria, Fin Arclight, and Seren Frostveil had all carved their names into the upper half of the ranking field, but the gap between them was no longer equal.
A few losses could now decide whether someone remained close to the championship path or fell into the lower ranks of the top twenty-five.
Angelina Valerius continued calling battles one after another.
Some matches were fierce but brief.
Damian Voss defeated Morgana Starveil after cutting through her Star-Curse Labyrinth with Sword Sovereign Heaven, though Morgana forced him to reveal several sword edicts before admitting defeat.
Rakan Thorne defeated Fin Arclight after opening the Second Limit of the War God Body and shattering the Pale Eclipse Field through sheer physical force.

Orion Starfall fought Seren Frostveil and won after using Nine Star Sovereign Body to break through Frozen World Stillness, though his injuries from the Revona battle made the victory much harder than it should have been.

Aurelian Lareth defeated Rosaline Lunara by suppressing her Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary with Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, but his expression remained cold and unpleasant afterward, as though each victory that was not against Max or Damian felt meaningless to him.
The mid-tier participants continued falling behind.

Then Ervin stepped forward.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
The black sea rose.
The gate pulled.
The Sovereign Rose Spear trembled.
Rosaline’s face turned pale as the golden-pink light began sinking into the broken gate.
She tried to maintain the spear, but the abyssal origin pressure dragged its authority downward layer by layer until the spear finally collapsed into scattered dawn fragments.
Ervin moved through those fragments.
His spear stopped before Rosaline’s throat.
Rosaline looked at the spear tip, then slowly lowered her hands.
"I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Rosaline Lunara Defeated.]

[Total Wins: 17]

[Total Wins: 15]
Rosaline let out a soft breath as the transfer light descended.
"You are difficult to fight," she said.
Ervin withdrew his spear.
"So are you."
Rosaline smiled faintly.
"That is kind of you to say after swallowing my strongest attack."
Ervin’s expression remained calm.
"It was strong enough to make the gate crack."
The transfer light carried both of them back to their pillars.
The arena remained thoughtful after that battle.
Ervin had won, but Rosaline had proven again that Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary was not weak.
Against almost anyone below the peak monsters, her sealing and sovereign suppression would have been enough to control the entire fight.
Unfortunately for her, Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent was one of the few paths capable of dragging that authority into a deeper darkness.
Max watched Ervin quietly.
That broken gate remained troublesome.
Even now, after seeing it twice, Max still felt that the black sea was only the surface.
The true danger lay behind the gate.
After Ervin defeated Rosaline Lunara, the final competitive stage continued moving forward with an even heavier momentum.
By now, almost every important participant had already crossed seventeen battles, and the records above the arena were beginning to look brutal.
The ones at the top had separated themselves from the rest.

Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Revona, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Rakan Thorne, Orion Starfall, Aurelian Lareth, Morgana Starveil, Rosaline Lunara, Selene Vaeloria, Fin Arclight, and Seren Frostveil had all carved their names into the upper half of the ranking field, but the gap between them was no longer equal.
A few losses could now decide whether someone remained close to the championship path or fell into the lower ranks of the top twenty-five.
Angelina Valerius continued calling battles one after another.
Some matches were fierce but brief.
Damian Voss defeated Morgana Starveil after cutting through her Star-Curse Labyrinth with Sword Sovereign Heaven, though Morgana forced him to reveal several sword edicts before admitting defeat.
Rakan Thorne defeated Fin Arclight after opening the Second Limit of the War God Body and shattering the Pale Eclipse Field through sheer physical force.

Orion Starfall fought Seren Frostveil and won after using Nine Star Sovereign Body to break through Frozen World Stillness, though his injuries from the Revona battle made the victory much harder than it should have been.

Aurelian Lareth defeated Rosaline Lunara by suppressing her Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary with Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, but his expression remained cold and unpleasant afterward, as though each victory that was not against Max or Damian felt meaningless to him.
The mid-tier participants continued falling behind.

The round-robin format guaranteed that each of them would eventually collide, and every collision would reshape the upper rankings.

chapters.title: Chapter 1868: Max vs Kaiden!
paragraphs: Then the randomizer began spinning again.
The giant screen above the arena flashed with countless names.
Rakan Thorne.
Aurelian Lareth.
Orion Starfall.
Ervin.
Revona.
Damian Voss.
Kaiden Voidmere.
Max Morgan.
Selene Vaeloria.
Rosaline Lunara.
Morgana Starveil.
The light slowed.
The first name stopped.
[Max Morgan]
The entire arena became alert.

Even before the second name appeared, the atmosphere had already changed. Whenever Max’s name appeared now, the Divine Realm paid attention. He had defeated Rosaline, crushed Rakan in body strength, forced Selene to surrender without fighting, and continued gathering wins without revealing everything.
Every battle involving him carried the possibility of another hidden card being shown.
Then the second name slowed.
It passed over Damian Voss.
It passed over Revona.
It passed over Ervin.
Finally, it stopped.
[Kaiden Voidmere]
The screen enlarged both names at once.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Max Morgan vs Kaiden Voidmere]
For a moment, the arena went completely silent.
Then the shock spread like a wave.
Max Morgan against Kaiden Voidmere.

This was not merely another battle between undefeated participants. This was a collision between two people connected by something far deeper than the tournament rankings. Kaiden Voidmere was the supreme genius of the Grand Void Sanctum, a force whose understanding of space and void stood among the highest in the Divine Realm.
He had moved through the final stage with terrifying ease, folding space, collapsing movement paths, and making opponents lose the very road beneath their feet before their attacks could land.
Max, however, was different.
Max had also walked the path of space.
Max had cultivated the Void Genesis Art.
And the more he had watched Kaiden fight, the more certain he had become of one thing.
The master who had given him the Void Genesis Art was the same master Kaiden had.
They had the same teacher.
They had walked the same path in the Space Concept.

Perhaps their branches had developed differently. Perhaps Kaiden had learned openly under the Grand Void Sanctum, while Max had inherited the Void Genesis Art through a much stranger path. But the source, the rhythm, and the foundation carried the same invisible mark.

Every time Kaiden folded space, every time he collapsed distance, and every time he stepped through a void gap without disturbing the surface of the world, Max could feel the echo of the same inheritance inside his own Space Concept.
Kaiden Voidmere slowly opened his eyes.
On his pillar, a faint silver-gray ripple spread around him.
He looked toward Max.
For the first time in a long while, a small smile appeared on Kaiden’s face.
"So our battle finally came."
Max looked back at him calmly.
"Yes."
The surrounding participants immediately noticed the difference.
Rakan Thorne crossed his arms and grinned. "These two know something we do not."
Orion Starfall, still pale but recovering, smiled with interest. "That expression from Kaiden is rare."
Morgana Starveil tilted her head. "Now this is interesting. That is not the look of two strangers meeting in battle."

Aurelian Lareth’s expression turned colder. Anything that revealed another hidden depth of Max made his mood worse, and Kaiden was not a weak opponent. If Max defeated Kaiden too, then his position in the final rankings would become even more terrifying.
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples erupted with excitement and nervousness.
"Max is fighting Kaiden Voidmere!"
"Kaiden has not lost once!"
"He is from the Grand Void Sanctum. His void and space techniques are insane."
"Max has space power too, right?"
"He used dimensional abilities before. Maybe this battle will show more of it."
Lady Virelia stood quietly before the giant screen, her eyes fixed on Max’s figure.

The seven family heads also grew solemn. They had seen Max use spatial power before, but Kaiden Voidmere was different from ordinary space cultivators. He had the backing of the Grand Void Sanctum, one of the most mysterious first-rate forces in the Divine Realm, and his control of space had looked effortless throughout the final stage.
At another distant viewing platform surrounded by folded space and silver-gray mist, the disciples of the Grand Void Sanctum watched with rare seriousness.
Kaiden was their pride.

He rarely spoke, rarely showed emotion, and rarely needed to use much strength against others. His victories were quiet, clean, and almost impossible to understand for anyone who did not cultivate space.
But now he had been matched with Max Morgan, the black dragon genius who had shaken the entire conference again and again.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
"Max Morgan."
Her gaze shifted.
"Kaiden Voidmere."
The transfer light began gathering above both pillars.
"Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.
Max appeared on one side of the central stage, his white hair moving gently as the space around him settled.

Kaiden appeared opposite him, silver-gray robes fluttering softly, his calm eyes carrying a rare brightness. Unlike many other opponents, he did not immediately release oppressive aura. Instead, he looked at Max as if he was looking at someone familiar and unfamiliar at the same time.
For several breaths, neither of them moved.
Then Kaiden spoke first.
"You have Void Genesis Art."
The words were quiet, but they struck like thunder among those who understood their meaning.
Max looked at him calmly.
"I do."
Kaiden’s eyes became deeper. "I sensed it before, but I was not completely certain. Now that we stand on the same stage, there is no mistake."
Max smiled faintly. "I also sensed it from your techniques."
Kaiden nodded. "Then you understand."
Max’s gaze sharpened slightly.
"Yes. The master who gave me Void Genesis Art is the same master behind your path."
A wave of whispers spread across the participant pillars.
Same master.
Same path.
Same source.
The meaning behind those words was not small.

Kaiden looked at Max for a moment, then said, "In the Grand Void Sanctum, very few people are allowed to approach that inheritance directly. Even among those who do, most only touch the outer shell. You are not from the sanctum, yet your foundation carries the core rhythm. That is why I called you junior brother before."
Max remembered that moment.
Kaiden had sensed it long ago.
He had not said everything then, but the meaning had been clear.
Max looked at him and asked, "Then are you my senior brother?"
Kaiden smiled faintly. "Perhaps. Or perhaps we are both only people walking beneath the shadow of the same master."
Max’s smile grew slightly. "That sounds more accurate."
Kaiden raised one hand slowly.
Space rippled around his fingers.
"Still, same source does not mean same strength."
Max’s eyes brightened with interest.
"Of course."
Kaiden’s silver-gray pupils shone faintly.
"Then let us see how far your Void Genesis Art has gone."
Max raised his hand as well, and the space around him responded with a quiet hum.
The entire arena grew tense.
This was not a battle of brute strength like Max and Rakan.
This was not a clash of sword and divine light like Damian and Aurelian.

This was a battle between two cultivators walking the same mysterious space path, two people whose foundations echoed one another, and two undefeated geniuses whose collision could reveal the true depth of the Void Genesis Art.
Angelina Valerius looked down at them.
Her voice remained calm, but the Eternal Hourglass itself seemed to pay attention.
[Battle Begins.]
The space between Max and Kaiden folded.
And both of them vanished at the same time.

chapters.title: Chapter 1869: Pushing Kaiden!
paragraphs: The space between Max and Kaiden folded, and both of them vanished in the same instant.

For a breath, the central stage looked empty. There was no explosion, no flash of golden light, no sword cry, no thunder, and no roaring dragon aura. Yet every true expert watching felt their skin tighten, because the battlefield had not grown calm. It had grown far more dangerous.
The danger had simply left the visible surface of the world and slipped into the hidden layers of space itself.
Then a line appeared in the air. It was not a sword mark. It was a spatial fracture.

Max and Kaiden appeared on opposite sides of that fracture at almost the same moment. Each had one hand raised, and each was using the same basic rhythm of the Void Genesis Art to twist the folded space between them.
The fracture expanded and then collapsed inward, disappearing before it could tear the stage apart. In the next instant, both of them vanished again.
Kaiden’s voice echoed from somewhere within the warped space.
"Void Genesis Art, Empty Step."

His figure reappeared behind Max without disturbing the air. A palm shot forward carrying no visible energy, yet the space in front of it folded into seven sharp layers. Had it landed on an ordinary opponent, the blow would never have struck from the outside.
Their inner organs, bones, and energy pathways would have been compressed from several spatial layers at once.
Max did not turn around.
"Void Genesis Art, Origin Fold."
The space behind him bent before Kaiden’s palm could arrive. The strike that should have landed on Max’s back folded past him and emerged three meters to his left instead.
At the same time, Max stepped backward through the folded space and appeared in front of Kaiden. His fingers were already pressing toward Kaiden’s chest.
"Void Genesis Art, Space-Sealing Finger."
Kaiden’s eyes sharpened.
"Void Genesis Art, Hollow Displacement."

His body blurred as the space around him shifted half a step away from reality, and Max’s finger passed through nothing but an afterimage. Yet Max’s eyes remained calm, and his finger did not stop. It dipped slightly downward, and the sealed space redirected itself.
Kaiden’s true body had only just emerged when the Space-Sealing Finger arrived before him once more. He raised his hand and blocked.
Boom!
There was no ordinary shockwave. Instead, the space between them sank, twisted, and shattered into countless mirror-like fragments before the laws of the Eternal Hourglass knitted it back together.

The two separated, or rather, the space between them expanded. Max stood on one side of the stage while Kaiden stood on the other. Both remained composed, but the expressions of everyone watching had already changed.
The battle had opened with high-level Void Genesis Art techniques from the very first exchange. Neither man had tested the other with weak moves, and neither had wasted time on ordinary attacks.

That alone marked the difference between this fight and most others. Max and Kaiden both understood that two people trained by the same master, walking the same path of space, had no need for shallow probing.
Kaiden regarded Max quietly. "You handled Hollow Displacement on the first try."
Max replied calmly, "It had the same root as Empty Step."
Kaiden nodded. "Then I will not use the outer forms anymore."
The silver-gray ripples around him deepened.
Max smiled faintly. "Good. I was about to say the same thing."
In the next instant, the entire central stage transformed into a battlefield of invisible folds.
Kaiden raised both hands.
"Void Genesis Art, Thousand-Layer Spatial Cage."

The space around Max split into layer after layer, forming a transparent prison without walls. Each layer overlapped the next, and every overlap carried crushing pressure. The cage did not attempt to bind Max’s body directly. It tried to bind his position in space itself, pinning him to a fixed coordinate no matter how he moved.
Max lifted one finger.
"Void Genesis Art, Origin Point Reversal."

The center of the cage shifted. For one brief instant, the fixed coordinate changed from Max’s position to Kaiden’s own shadow. The Thousand-Layer Spatial Cage collapsed inward, but it closed around the spot where Kaiden had stood a breath earlier rather than around Max.
Kaiden had already moved.
"Void Genesis Art, Void Corridor Severance."

A long corridor of folded space opened beneath Max’s feet. It sought to sever the path between Max and the surrounding arena, isolating him from every direction at once. At the same moment, Kaiden appeared above him with his palm descending like a silent blade.
"Void Genesis Art, Space Burial Palm."
The palm fell, and the space around Max sank as though a tomb had opened beneath him.
Max looked up, and his eyes remained perfectly calm.
"Void Genesis Art, Genesis Void Axis."

A vertical line of invisible force ran through Max’s body. The Space Burial Palm struck that axis and instantly lost its direction. The folded space that had tried to bury him began rotating around the axis instead. It formed a spiral that dragged the burial force away from Max and scattered it harmlessly into the edges of the arena.
Kaiden’s expression shifted slightly, but before he could withdraw, Max stepped forward. There was no distance left between them. Max’s palm pressed toward Kaiden’s shoulder.
"Void Genesis Art, Returning Void Palm."
Kaiden crossed his arms.
"Void Genesis Art, Triple Hollow Shield."

Three layers of hollow space materialized before him. Max’s palm touched the first layer, and it collapsed. The second layer twisted, and then the third layer shattered. Kaiden was driven backward for the first time in the battle.

He slid several meters across the stage, though his feet never truly touched the ground, for space kept folding beneath him to soften the impact. Even so, the fact was plain for everyone to see. Max had seized the advantage.
The Grand Void Sanctum disciples watching from afar went silent, while the Black Dragon Clan disciples erupted with excitement.
"He pushed Kaiden back!"
"Max is using space against Kaiden and still winning!"
"Kaiden Voidmere has never been pushed like this before!"
