Rakan Thorne frowned. "I hate fights like this. They are punching each other with the battlefield itself."
Orion Starfall smiled weakly from his pillar. "That is exactly what makes it frightening."
On the stage, Kaiden studied Max for a few breaths before raising his hand once more. This time, the space around the entire stage grew unstable.
"Void Genesis Art, Eightfold World Folding."

Eight enormous folds spread across the central arena. Each fold contained a partial reflection of the stage, and within every reflection stood another Kaiden. The attack was no illusion. Each reflected Kaiden occupied a temporary spatial layer, and any one of them could become real at the instant of attack.
Eight Kaidens moved as one.
"Void Genesis Art, Eight Hollow Strikes."
Eight palms lashed toward Max from eight separate spatial layers.

Max stood in place, and he neither dodged nor defended. The first strike passed through his shoulder while the second passed through his ribs. The third struck his back, and the fourth struck his chest. The fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth all landed from their own different layers of space.
Yet Max did not move. No blood appeared, and no wound opened anywhere on his body. His clothes fluttered slightly, but he remained completely unharmed.
Kaiden’s eyes widened, and the eight reflected figures faded away.
Max regarded him quietly. "Those attacks will not work on me."
Kaiden’s expression grew more serious. "Why?"
Max raised one hand, and the space around his palm answered him like an obedient subject.
"It’s a secret."
The words were quiet, yet they spread through the arena like a shockwave, and Kaiden’s pupils contracted.

Max continued calmly, "Your attacks are strong. Against almost anyone else here, even many top geniuses, they would be extremely dangerous. But they are still space element attacks. They still rely on folding, cutting, compressing, burying, displacing, or isolating space."
The space around Max became still. It was not controlled and it was not forced. It was simply still, as though it had accepted him of its own accord.
Max looked at Kaiden and said, "I am mostly immune to that."
A wave of shock rolled across the arena. Kaiden slowly lowered his hand, and for the first time in the battle, his calm face showed genuine disbelief.
"Mostly immune to space attacks?"
Max offered no further explanation. He could not reveal everything about the Dimensional Sovereign Body, and he had no intention of exposing its source. The truth itself was simple enough.

Space could bend around him, fold around him, and even attack through him, but wounding him with space itself was nearly impossible unless the attacker held power far beyond his current level. His body did not merely resist spatial force. It belonged to a deeper dimensional foundation altogether.
The Dimensional Sovereign Body made him the true sovereign of space, and turning ordinary space attacks against him was simply foolish.
Kaiden grasped part of it without needing another word, and his gaze deepened.
"So that is why my strikes failed to damage you."
Max nodded lightly. "Yes."

Kaiden closed his eyes briefly, and when he opened them again, his expression had changed. There was no anger in it. There was only understanding, along with a strange sense of clarity. Even so, he did not surrender yet.

Silver-gray light erupted around him, and the space behind him opened into a vast hollow expanse filled with countless shifting planes. The aura of the Void Genesis Art swelled beyond anything he had shown before, and for the first time, Kaiden drove his mastery to its absolute limit.
"Void Genesis Art, Grand Void Convergence."

Every spatial layer around the stage began folding toward a single point above Kaiden’s palm, and the pressure became terrifying. Even though Max was largely immune to spatial attacks, the sheer mastery behind this technique set the whole arena trembling.

The Grand Void Convergence did not simply cut or compress space. It gathered every fold Kaiden could command and condensed them into one point, seeking to collapse the opponent’s very position within reality.
Kaiden looked at Max. "If this still cannot touch you, then I will have my answer."
Max stood calmly. "Then come."
Kaiden pressed his palm forward. The Grand Void Convergence descended, and the point of collapsed space drifted toward Max like a silent star of emptiness.

Max raised his hand as the Void Genesis Art circulated within him. His movement, however, differed from Kaiden’s in nature. Kaiden controlled space with precision, while Max commanded it with the authority of its origin.
"Void Genesis Art, Genesis Returns To Void."

The moment Max spoke, the collapsed point before him trembled. Kaiden’s Grand Void Convergence did not explode. Instead, it began to unfold. Layer by layer, the space Kaiden had compressed was returned to its original state.

The killing pressure vanished and the collapsing coordinates stabilized. The distorted reality mended itself around Max’s palm, and the enormous attack Kaiden had condensed with everything at his disposal dissolved without harming a single strand of Max’s hair.
The Grand Void Sanctum viewing platform fell deathly silent.

Kaiden stared at the scene, and at last he understood. The gap between them did not come only from Max’s immunity to space attacks. That was merely one reason. The deeper reason was mastery, for Max’s command of the Void Genesis Art surpassed his own.

Kaiden’s techniques were refined, powerful, and difficult to counter, but Max had reached a level where he could touch the root rhythm behind them. Whenever Kaiden folded space, Max could return the fold to its origin.

Whenever Kaiden displaced a layer, Max could redirect its axis, and whenever Kaiden compressed space into a killing point, Max could unfold it before it turned fatal. Even if Kaiden had somehow landed a strike, the Dimensional Sovereign Body would have kept the spatial force from truly injuring him.
This was not a battle between equals walking the same path. It was a senior pathwalker meeting someone who had traveled deeper into the inheritance than he ever had.
Kaiden looked at Max for a long moment, and then he smiled faintly.
"I understand now."
Max lowered his hand. Kaiden glanced at the space surrounding Max, and then at Max himself.
"No wonder master chose you."

The words sent another wave of shock through the arena. Master chose you. To everyone else, that sentence could carry countless meanings, but to Max and Kaiden it carried only one. The person behind the Void Genesis Art had not passed it to Max by accident.

chapters.title: Chapter 1871: Divine Son vs Rakan!
paragraphs: Kaiden drew a slow breath and lowered his hands.
"I surrender."
The arena went silent once more. Angelina Valerius regarded Kaiden for a breath, and then she announced calmly, "Kaiden Voidmere has surrendered."
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Kaiden Voidmere Defeated.]
The screen above the stage updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 18]
[Total Wins: 18]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Kaiden Voidmere]
[Total Battles Fought: 18]
[Total Wins: 17]
The result shone above the arena. Kaiden Voidmere, the supreme genius of the Grand Void Sanctum, had lost. He had not lost because he was weak, nor because his Void Genesis Art was flawed.
He had lost because Max Morgan’s mastery stood higher, and because Max’s body rendered space itself nearly incapable of harming him.

At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples erupted into wild cheers yet again. At the Grand Void Sanctum, the atmosphere stayed silent and complicated. Some disciples looked unwilling to accept it, but the elders said nothing at all.
They had seen the truth with perfect clarity. Kaiden had not surrendered out of cowardice. He had surrendered because he understood the gap more deeply than anyone watching from outside.

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Kaiden stood across from Max and bowed his head slightly. It was not the bow of a defeated man surrendering his dignity. It was the acknowledgment of someone who had glimpsed a higher level of his own path.
"Junior brother," Kaiden said softly, "walk far."
Max looked at him and nodded. "I will."
The transfer light descended and carried Kaiden back to his pillar, and Max returned to his own a moment later.

The other participants watched him in silence. He had defeated Rakan in a contest of body strength, and he had forced Selene to surrender without ever fighting. Now he had defeated Kaiden Voidmere on the path of space itself.
After Max defeated Kaiden Voidmere, the atmosphere of the final competitive stage grew even heavier. Another undefeated name had fallen.

Kaiden’s defeat felt different from Rakan’s, different from Orion’s, and different from the loss Aurelian had suffered at Damian’s hands. He had not been overwhelmed by raw force, cut down by sword authority, or exhausted by a countering Pseudo Cosmic Path. He had lost on the very path he took the most pride in.

The Void Genesis Art had been matched against the Void Genesis Art, and Max had displayed higher mastery and deeper authority. On top of that, his body had rendered spatial attacks nearly meaningless.
The Grand Void Sanctum fell into thoughtful silence, while the Black Dragon Clan erupted yet again.

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Max returned to his pillar calmly, and Kaiden sat down with a faint smile resting on his face. His loss had not crushed him. Instead, it seemed to have answered a question he had carried in his heart, and after acknowledging Max as someone chosen by the same master, his expression had grown much lighter than before.
Angelina Valerius waited until the screen finished updating the records, and then she raised her hand once more.
"The next battle will now begin."

The giant screen above the arena began to rotate. At this stage of the tournament, every single name carried weight. Most participants had already fought eighteen or nineteen battles. The weaker among them had long dropped out of the upper race, while the true monsters kept carving out their positions through victories and rare defeats.
One loss could reshape the top five, and one major victory could restore a damaged reputation. A single bad matchup could ruin everything.
The names flashed past, among them Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Revona, Ervin, Aurelian Lareth, Rakan Thorne, Orion Starfall, Morgana Starveil, Rosaline Lunara, and Kaiden Voidmere.
The light slowed, and the first name stopped.
[Rakan Thorne]

Across the Divine Realm, the War God Palace disciples snapped to attention at once. Rakan had already suffered one crushing defeat against Max, but since then he had won battle after battle with fierce dominance.

He remained one of the strongest body cultivators in the conference, and most participants below the absolute peak still could not withstand even his First or Second Limit. His record remained excellent, and his fighting spirit had not dimmed in the least.
The second name kept spinning and then slowed further. Aurelian Lareth’s golden eyes narrowed.
The name stopped.
[Aurelian Lareth]
The screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Rakan Thorne vs Aurelian Lareth]

The arena erupted immediately, for this was another major battle. Rakan Thorne, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, would face Aurelian Lareth, the Divine Son of the second elven faction. One of them represented the extreme of physical body cultivation and close combat war power.

The other represented divine light, royal bloodline authority, and long-range Heavenly Luminance suppression. Both men had already lost to someone at the peak, yet both remained terrifying enough to dominate nearly everyone beneath that level.
On his pillar, Rakan cracked his neck and grinned. "So I finally get the shining prince."
Aurelian looked at him coldly. "You should worry less about my title and more about whether your fists can reach me."
Rakan’s grin widened. "If they reach you once, you will understand why people respect the War God Palace."
Aurelian’s expression did not change. "Then try."
The War God Palace disciples began to roar.
"Rakan!"
"First Warlord!"
"Crush the Divine Son!"
"Break through that light!"

Inside the viewing halls of the second elven faction, the atmosphere ran colder but burned no less intensely. Aurelian had already lost to Damian, and the humiliation of that defeat had not faded. If he lost again to Rakan, his standing in the eyes of the Divine Realm would sink even further.
Several elders stared at the screen with sharp eyes.
"The Divine Son cannot lose this."
"Rakan’s close combat is frightening, but he has a clear weakness."
"He must be kept away."
"His fists are only meaningful if they reach the target."

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Max watched the stage calmly. This battle would be a clash of styles. If Rakan dragged Aurelian into close combat, Aurelian would suffer, because even with the Crownless Divine King he would not want to trade blows against Rakan’s Third Limit for long.

But if Aurelian held his distance and used the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion to suppress the battlefield, then Rakan would have to fight through layers of divine light before he could ever land a clean hit.
Angelina looked toward both participants. "Rakan Thorne. Aurelian Lareth. Enter the stage."

Two beams of light descended. Rakan landed heavily on one side of the central stage, and the stone beneath his feet cracked slightly under the weight of his body. Aurelian appeared opposite him with golden-white light flowing around him like a sacred robe.
Compared to Rakan’s violent war aura, Aurelian’s presence felt colder, brighter, and more distant, like a divine sun hanging high above a battlefield.
Angelina raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Rakan moved first. He did not hesitate, and he wasted no time on slow probing. The instant the battle began, the bronze markings on his arms lit up.
"War God Body, First Limit, War Blood Awakening."
His blood roared like war drums.
Boom!
The stage shattered beneath his feet as he charged. In a single instant he crossed half the distance to Aurelian with his fist drawn back and battle intent blazing in his eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1872: Rakan Going All Out!
paragraphs: Aurelian raised one hand.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Spear Rain."
Hundreds of golden-white spears formed in the air and rained down toward Rakan. Each spear carried divine light strong enough to punch through ordinary defenses, but Rakan did not slow.

He punched forward and the air burst apart, shattering dozens of spears before they could touch him. The remaining spears struck his body and left burning marks across his shoulders and arms, yet he pushed through them like a war beast breaking out of a storm.
Aurelian’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sunwheel Descent."
A blazing golden wheel materialized above Rakan and dropped with crushing force. Rakan roared and punched upward to meet it.
"War God Fist, Mountain-Breaking Drum."
His fist struck the sunwheel.
Boom!

The golden wheel cracked, but the impact forced Rakan’s charge to falter. That small pause was all Aurelian needed. He slid backward through radiant light and opened the distance between them once more.
Rakan clicked his tongue. "Running already?"
Aurelian replied coldly, "Choosing distance is not running. It is understanding the battlefield."
He raised both hands.
"Heavenly Luminance, Twelve Sacred Wings."

Twelve radiant wings spread open behind him, and countless feathers of light streaked toward Rakan from every direction. They did not simply aim for his body. They targeted his joints, his eyes, his throat, his knees, and his path of movement, forcing him to either block or waste precious time tearing through them.
Rakan’s grin vanished.
"Second Limit."
The sound of divine metal being reforged rang out from his bones.
"War Bone Reforging."

His body grew heavier and harder. He crossed his arms and bulled straight through the feather storm. Golden-white feathers exploded against his skin, carving shallow wounds and burning lines across his flesh, yet none of them managed to halt his advance.
Aurelian lifted one finger.
"Divine Luminance Chain Edict."

Golden-white chains rose from the ground and dropped from the sky at the same time, coiling around Rakan’s arms, legs, waist, and neck. These were no ordinary bindings. They carried divine authority, and they sought to dull his physical power by suppressing the rhythm of war beating inside his body.
Rakan’s muscles tightened. "Break!"
The chains cracked, but before they fully shattered, Aurelian’s next attack was already falling.
"Heavenly Luminance, Crowned Sun Judgment."
A crown of light appeared above the stage and unleashed a pillar of divine radiance directly onto Rakan. The attack caught him before he could completely tear free of the chains.
Boom!
Rakan was driven down to one knee.
The War God Palace disciples clenched their fists.
"He is suppressing Rakan from a distance!"
"Break it!"
"First Warlord, break through!"
On the stage, Rakan lowered his head for a moment, and then he laughed. "Good. Annoying, but good."
His flesh began to rumble.
"Third Limit."
The bronze markings across his body joined into a single pattern.
"War Flesh Unbound."
Boom!

Rakan’s aura exploded upward. The Divine Luminance chains shattered, and the pillar of the Crowned Sun Judgment cracked apart from within. Rakan rose to his feet covered in blood and light burns, yet his battle intent had only grown more violent.
Aurelian’s face turned colder.
Rakan vanished from where he stood. With the Third Limit open, his speed was terrifying, and he appeared before Aurelian almost instantly with a punch driving toward his chest.
Aurelian’s pupils contracted.
"Heavenly Luminance Battle Form, Divine Step."
He darted backward, but Rakan’s fist still grazed past his shoulder.
Boom!
The passing force alone tore through Aurelian’s radiant armor and sent him sliding several meters across the stage.
The entire arena shook with excitement.
"He touched him!"
"Rakan almost landed a clean blow!"
"If that punch had connected properly, Aurelian would be badly injured!"
Aurelian glanced at his torn shoulder armor, and his expression turned ugly.
Rakan grinned. "You see? Distance is useful only until I cross it."
Aurelian’s golden-white light flared brighter. "You are right."
He raised his hand toward the sky. "That is why I will not let you cross it again."
Behind him, sacred halls, radiant pillars, a golden throne, and an endless sun took shape, and his Pseudo Cosmic Path descended with overwhelming pressure.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."
Boom!
The entire stage was swallowed in divine light. Rakan’s body sank slightly beneath the pressure, but he refused to retreat. Instead he laughed loudly and clenched his fists.
"Good. Use everything."
Aurelian’s eyes were cold.
"Divine Dominion, Luminance Decree."

A golden-white decree unfurled above the stage and released countless sacred words that pressed down on Rakan. They slowed his blood, weakened his war rhythm, and smothered the explosive force of his three opened limits.
Rakan punched forward.
"War God Fist, Battlefield Collapse."
His fist shattered dozens of radiant words, but more kept descending. He tried to charge, only to find the ground beneath him covered in sacred lines that locked onto his feet.
Aurelian raised his other hand.
"Divine Dominion, Twelve Pillars of Sacred Judgment."

Twelve radiant pillars surrounded Rakan and fired golden-white beams from every direction. Rakan crossed his arms and weathered the first wave. Then he roared and slammed his foot down, cracking the stage beneath him.

He forced his way forward through the beams, but every step drained more of his strength. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion empowered Aurelian while it weakened Rakan, and it turned the entire battlefield hostile toward him. Even with the Third Limit open, closing the distance was no longer easy.
Aurelian gave him no room to breathe.
"Divine Dominion, Royal Mandate of the Endless Sun."
The endless sun above the divine kingdom brightened, and golden-white light poured down onto Aurelian himself. His aura swelled, and every attack he made took on the weight of a divine execution.
Rakan fought his way through the Twelve Pillars of Sacred Judgment and finally reached striking range again.
"War God Fist, Three-Limit Heaven Breaker!"

His fist drew back as the power of War Blood Awakening, War Bone Reforging, and War Flesh Unbound gathered into one terrifying punch. The entire arena could feel that if this blow landed cleanly, even Aurelian’s sacred armor would break.
Aurelian’s expression turned sharp, but he did not block. He retreated upward instead.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Radiant Ascension Step."

His body rose into the air along a pillar of light, and Rakan’s fist tore through nothing but the space he had just abandoned. The punch detonated against the stage instead and shattered a massive portion of the battlefield.
Before Rakan could recover his stance, Aurelian struck from above.
"Divine Dominion, Sacred Sun Spearfall."

Hundreds of massive divine spears formed around the endless sun and plunged down toward Rakan one after another. This was no longer the ordinary Sacred Spear Rain from the opening exchange. Every spear now carried the authority of a Pseudo Cosmic Path, and every one of them sought to pin Rakan to the stage before he could leap upward.

chapters.title: Chapter 1873: Divine Son Previals!
paragraphs: Rakan looked up and grinned fiercely. He punched, and one spear shattered. He punched again, and another broke apart. He charged through the falling divine spears and smashed them one after another, but their numbers were simply too great. His body began collecting wounds. Golden-white light pierced his shoulder, another spear grazed his ribs, and a third struck his thigh and made him stumble for half a breath.
Aurelian’s voice descended from above.
"Crownless Divine King."

The golden throne behind him shattered into fragments of light that flowed into his body. His aura condensed sharply, and the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion contracted into a smaller but far more oppressive form. The divine sun at his back became a burning crown, and countless runes gathered around his hands.
Rakan’s eyes widened slightly.
Aurelian pointed downward.
"Crownless Divine King, Light That Judges All War."

The divine runes fell like a rain of judgment. Rakan roared and pushed his physical power to its absolute limit. His three limits burned as one, and his body resembled a bronze war statue drenched in blood. He charged upward into the falling light, straining to reach Aurelian before the long-range suppression could grind him down completely.
For several breaths, the battlefield became a violent collision between golden judgment and bronze war power. Rakan broke through one layer, then another, and then another after that.
The War God Palace disciples screamed his name.
"Rakan!"
"Break through!"
"First Warlord!"
"Reach him!"
And Rakan did reach the edge of Aurelian’s defensive range. His fist rose once more.
"Three-Limit Heaven Breaker!"
Aurelian’s eyes turned to ice.
"Crownless Divine King, Final Luminance Judgment."
A massive divine sword of golden-white light took form above him and came crashing down before Rakan’s fist could fully release.
Boom!

The fist met the divine sword, and for a moment Rakan actually held the blade in place. His muscles bulged, blood burst from the wounds across his body, and the stage cracked further beneath him as he forced his fist upward against the Final Luminance Judgment, inch by grinding inch.
Aurelian’s face darkened.
Rakan laughed through gritted teeth. "Your light is strong, prince, but not heavy enough."
Aurelian raised his other hand.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Solar Execution Array."

The entire divine kingdom behind him released hundreds of smaller golden-white blades. They did not strike at random. They arranged themselves into a circular array around Rakan and began cutting at him from the sides, from behind, and from above, all while the Final Luminance Judgment kept his strongest fist occupied.

Rakan wanted to move, but he could not. If he withdrew his fist, the divine sword would fall on him. If he kept resisting, the Solar Execution Array would carve him apart piece by piece. Golden-white blades struck his body one after another.

His back split open, his shoulder bled, and his arms began to tremble. Even the Third Limit of the War God Body could not shrug off so many attacks empowered by the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion.

Max watched the fight with narrowed eyes. Aurelian’s choice was plain to see. He had no intention of meeting Rakan fairly in close combat. He was using distance, altitude, suppression, and layered long-range attacks to deny Rakan any chance at a decisive blow.
It was not cowardice. It was simply the correct strategy. Rakan was stronger up close, Aurelian was more dangerous at range, and Aurelian was making certain the battle never left his range.
On the stage, Rakan roared one final time. The bronze light around his body surged violently, and he shattered the Final Luminance Judgment with a single desperate punch.
Crack!
The massive divine sword broke apart, but before Rakan could follow through, Aurelian’s Solar Execution Array condensed into one final spear above him.
"Crownless Divine King, Sun-Piercing Verdict."

The spear descended. Rakan tried to raise his arms, but his body had taken too much damage under the relentless suppression. The spear crashed into his crossed guard and hammered him down into the stage.
Boom!

The central stage caved inward, and dust, light, and broken stone rose in every direction. When the glare faded, Rakan knelt inside a crater with both arms trembling and blood covering most of his body.

His War God Body still burned, but its bronze light had turned unstable. He tried to rise, only for the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion to press down on him again while several golden-white spears formed overhead, poised to fall if he continued.

Aurelian hovered in the air, breathing hard. His face was pale, and his aura no longer held steady. The fight against Rakan had clearly cost him a great deal, and if Rakan had reached him cleanly even once, the outcome might have been very different. But Rakan had not.
Angelina Valerius looked down at the stage. "Rakan Thorne is unable to continue."

Rakan clenched his teeth, and for a moment it seemed he might force himself up regardless. Then he looked at the golden-white spears above him, glanced at Aurelian, and finally laughed with open bitterness.
"Fine. I lose."
Angelina announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Rakan Thorne Defeated.]
The screen above the arena updated immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Aurelian Lareth]
[Total Battles Fought: 19]
[Total Wins: 18]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rakan Thorne]
[Total Battles Fought: 19]
[Total Wins: 17]
The Divine Realm erupted in mixed reactions. The second elven faction finally released a wave of cheering after the suffocating gloom that had followed Aurelian’s loss to Damian.

Their Divine Son had defeated the first Warlord of the War God Palace. Even if the victory had come through range and suppression rather than direct confrontation, a victory was still a victory, and in a round-robin stage every win mattered.

At the War God Palace, the disciples seethed with frustration, yet none of them could claim Rakan had fought poorly. He had charged through the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, shattered countless divine spears, and broken the Final Luminance Judgment itself. He had nearly reached Aurelian more than once.
But Aurelian’s long-range attacks had been too layered, too constant, and too perfectly suited to denying Rakan the close combat battle he craved.
On the stage, Aurelian descended slowly, while Rakan struggled to his feet once the pressure lifted, his body already being stabilized by the laws of the Eternal Hourglass.
He looked at Aurelian and snorted. "If I had landed one clean punch, you would not be standing so neatly."
Aurelian regarded him coldly. "But you did not."
Rakan stared at him for a breath, and then he laughed. "That is true."
Aurelian offered nothing further. The transfer light descended and carried both of them back to their pillars.
Max watched Aurelian quietly. This victory had restored a measure of the Divine Son’s pride, but it had also revealed something important.

Aurelian could defeat Rakan so long as he kept his distance, suppressed the battlefield, and stacked long-range divine attacks without permitting a single clean exchange up close. Yet if Rakan had ever reached him properly, even Aurelian would have been in danger. Aurelian was strong, but he was not without weakness.
After Aurelian Lareth and Rakan Thorne returned to their pillars, the final competitive stage pressed onward, and Angelina Valerius did not slow the rhythm of the tournament.

By this point, audiences throughout the Divine Realm had already witnessed too many shocking battles, and everyone understood that showing every remaining match in full would only drag the stage out endlessly.
The records were approaching their final stretch, and the important names had begun colliding with one another more frequently.

Some battles still carried real weight, some were decided almost instantly, and some merely confirmed what many had already guessed about the gulf between the upper monsters and the rest of the top twenty-five.

chapters.title: Chapter 1874: Ervin vs Orion!
paragraphs: The next significant match paired Ervin against Orion Starfall.

The moment their names appeared together, the arena fell quiet once again. Orion had already fought one of the most exhausting battles of the final competitive stage against Revona, and although the laws of the Eternal Hourglass had stabilized his injuries, no one believed he had fully recovered.

His aura remained weaker than before, and his face still carried a trace of pallor. The star marks on his body no longer shone with the effortless brilliance they had displayed at the start of the final round.
Even so, when he stepped onto the stage, he was still smiling. It was the same bright and almost careless smile that made him look as though nothing in the world could truly spoil his mood.
His armor bore faint cracks from his previous battle, and the wounds beneath it had only recently closed, yet his eyes were clear. He looked across the stage at Ervin and laughed softly.
"I really wanted an easier opponent after fighting Revona," Orion said.
Ervin stood opposite him with his black spear in hand, his expression as calm as ever. "Then your luck is poor."
Orion sighed with exaggerated helplessness. "Clearly."

A few spectators laughed, but the laughter faded quickly, because everyone understood this would be no light battle. Orion was the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court and the man who had forced Revona to use Return To Nothing.

Ervin was the mysterious spear genius whose Abyssal Origin Descent had swallowed Selene’s Heavenly Luminance Genesis and defeated Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary. Both had already proven themselves among the true monsters of the final stage.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]

Orion did not bother testing him. The instant the battle began, all nine star marks across his body lit up together. A vast starry sky opened behind him, and nine ancient stars descended one after another. They entered his hands, his spine, his heart, his bones, his blood, and his flesh, transforming his entire body into a living vessel of celestial power.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Nine Star Sovereign Body."
Boom!

A majestic star palace materialized behind Orion, ringed by nine immense stars and crowned with an empty throne of starlight. The pressure pouring from his body climbed sharply, and his smile grew brighter as he stepped forward.
"I already learned not to waste time against monsters."
The moment his voice fell, Orion vanished. He reappeared before Ervin like a falling star, his fist wreathed in blazing stellar heat.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, First Star Fist."
Ervin raised his spear, and the fist crashed into the shaft.
Boom!

Starlight burst outward in a circular wave, and Ervin’s feet slid backward for the first time. Before he could fully steady himself, Orion changed stars. The heat in his fist vanished, and heavy dead-star pressure flowed into his shoulder instead.
"Sixth Star Pressure Strike."

Orion’s shoulder slammed forward. Ervin shifted his spear and blocked again, but the pressure drove him back another two steps. The audience grew restless at once. Orion’s injuries had weakened him, yet with the Nine Star Sovereign Body active, he remained terrifying.
Every part of his body could become a different star weapon, and every movement changed the nature of his attack.
Orion stepped to the left.
"Second Star Step."

His body shifted like a comet changing orbit. Ervin’s spear thrust toward the place Orion had just occupied, but Orion had already appeared at his right side. His elbow carried the sharpness of a meteor as it dropped toward Ervin’s ribs.
"Third Star Elbow."
Ervin’s eyes sharpened, and his spear turned.
"Abyss Spear Art, Hollow Moon Guard."

A crescent of dark spear force rose between them and caught the elbow, but Orion’s fourth star had already entered his leg. He abandoned the elbow strike halfway and lashed out with a kick of terrifying speed.
"Fourth Star Crescent Kick."
The kick hammered the side of Ervin’s spear guard.
Bang!
Ervin was forced back yet again.
Across the Divine Realm, the Nine Star Court disciples roared with excitement.
"Senior Brother Orion!"
"He is still suppressing Ervin!"
"Even after fighting Revona, he is still this strong!"
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Rakan Thorne grinned. "That star bastard still has plenty left."
Kaiden Voidmere nodded faintly. "His injuries are affecting him, but his control remains excellent."
Max watched quietly. Orion’s condition was clearly below its peak, yet his battle sense had not dulled at all.

He knew Ervin was dangerous, so he refused to give him the space to slowly open his abyssal path. He kept changing stars and shifting rhythm, forcing close exchanges before Ervin could drag the battlefield into his own pace.
On the stage, Orion’s assault grew fiercer.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Seven-Star Revolving Impact."
Seven star forces rotated through his body within a single breath. His fists, elbows, knees, shoulders, and palms struck one after another, and each blow carried a different celestial property.
Heat, weight, sharpness, speed, pressure, burning blood, and crown-like suppression flowed through his attacks so quickly that most opponents would have been overwhelmed on the spot.

Ervin retreated six steps, then nine, and then twelve. For the first time since revealing his strength, he looked as though he had been pushed into a corner. Yet no panic touched his expression, and his abyss-like eyes stayed calm. At the thirteenth step, his foot stopped.
Orion’s fist descended again.
"Ninth Star Crown Fist."

The crown-shaped starlight above his head flashed, and the fist fell with majestic pressure. It did not equal Starfall Extinction, but it still carried enough force to crush most defensive techniques.
This time, Ervin moved differently. His spear tip lowered, and the air beneath Orion’s fist sank.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Reversal."
The star force in Orion’s fist suddenly tilted downward, as if an invisible current had seized it. His punch missed Ervin’s shoulder by a hair’s width and struck the stage instead.
Boom!

The stage caved in, and in the same instant, Ervin’s spear rose from below. Orion’s eyes widened slightly. He twisted his body in midair and blocked with his forearm, but the spear force still grazed his side and tore a wound across his armor. Blood splashed onto the stage.

It was the same bright and almost careless smile that made him look as though nothing in the world could truly spoil his mood.
His armor bore faint cracks from his previous battle, and the wounds beneath it had only recently closed, yet his eyes were clear.
He looked across the stage at Ervin and laughed softly.
"I really wanted an easier opponent after fighting Revona," Orion said.
Ervin stood opposite him with his black spear in hand, his expression as calm as ever.
"Then your luck is poor."
Orion sighed with exaggerated helplessness.
"Clearly."
A few spectators laughed, but the laughter faded quickly, because everyone understood this would be no light battle.
Orion was the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court and the man who had forced Revona to use Return To Nothing.
Ervin was the mysterious spear genius whose Abyssal Origin Descent had swallowed Selene’s Heavenly Luminance Genesis and defeated Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary.
Both had already proven themselves among the true monsters of the final stage.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Orion did not bother testing him.
The instant the battle began, all nine star marks across his body lit up together.
A vast starry sky opened behind him, and nine ancient stars descended one after another.
They entered his hands, his spine, his heart, his bones, his blood, and his flesh, transforming his entire body into a living vessel of celestial power.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Nine Star Sovereign Body."
Boom!
A majestic star palace materialized behind Orion, ringed by nine immense stars and crowned with an empty throne of starlight.
The pressure pouring from his body climbed sharply, and his smile grew brighter as he stepped forward.
"I already learned not to waste time against monsters."
The moment his voice fell, Orion vanished.
He reappeared before Ervin like a falling star, his fist wreathed in blazing stellar heat.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, First Star Fist."
Ervin raised his spear, and the fist crashed into the shaft.
Boom!
Starlight burst outward in a circular wave, and Ervin’s feet slid backward for the first time.
Before he could fully steady himself, Orion changed stars.
The heat in his fist vanished, and heavy dead-star pressure flowed into his shoulder instead.
"Sixth Star Pressure Strike."
Orion’s shoulder slammed forward.
Ervin shifted his spear and blocked again, but the pressure drove him back another two steps.
The audience grew restless at once.
Orion’s injuries had weakened him, yet with the Nine Star Sovereign Body active, he remained terrifying.
Every part of his body could become a different star weapon, and every movement changed the nature of his attack.
Orion stepped to the left.
"Second Star Step."
His body shifted like a comet changing orbit.
Ervin’s spear thrust toward the place Orion had just occupied, but Orion had already appeared at his right side.
His elbow carried the sharpness of a meteor as it dropped toward Ervin’s ribs.
"Third Star Elbow."
Ervin’s eyes sharpened, and his spear turned.
"Abyss Spear Art, Hollow Moon Guard."
A crescent of dark spear force rose between them and caught the elbow, but Orion’s fourth star had already entered his leg.
He abandoned the elbow strike halfway and lashed out with a kick of terrifying speed.
"Fourth Star Crescent Kick."
The kick hammered the side of Ervin’s spear guard.
Bang!
Ervin was forced back yet again.
Across the Divine Realm, the Nine Star Court disciples roared with excitement.
"Senior Brother Orion!"
"He is still suppressing Ervin!"
"Even after fighting Revona, he is still this strong!"
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Rakan Thorne grinned.
"That star bastard still has plenty left."
Kaiden Voidmere nodded faintly.
"His injuries are affecting him, but his control remains excellent."
Max watched quietly.
Orion’s condition was clearly below its peak, yet his battle sense had not dulled at all.
He knew Ervin was dangerous, so he refused to give him the space to slowly open his abyssal path.
He kept changing stars and shifting rhythm, forcing close exchanges before Ervin could drag the battlefield into his own pace.
On the stage, Orion’s assault grew fiercer.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Seven-Star Revolving Impact."
Seven star forces rotated through his body within a single breath.
His fists, elbows, knees, shoulders, and palms struck one after another, and each blow carried a different celestial property.
Heat, weight, sharpness, speed, pressure, burning blood, and crown-like suppression flowed through his attacks so quickly that most opponents would have been overwhelmed on the spot.
Ervin retreated six steps, then nine, and then twelve.
For the first time since revealing his strength, he looked as though he had been pushed into a corner.
Yet no panic touched his expression, and his abyss-like eyes stayed calm.
At the thirteenth step, his foot stopped.
Orion’s fist descended again.
"Ninth Star Crown Fist."
The crown-shaped starlight above his head flashed, and the fist fell with majestic pressure.
It did not equal Starfall Extinction, but it still carried enough force to crush most defensive techniques.
This time, Ervin moved differently.
His spear tip lowered, and the air beneath Orion’s fist sank.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Reversal."
The star force in Orion’s fist suddenly tilted downward, as if an invisible current had seized it.
His punch missed Ervin’s shoulder by a hair’s width and struck the stage instead.
Boom!
The stage caved in, and in the same instant, Ervin’s spear rose from below.
Orion’s eyes widened slightly.
He twisted his body in midair and blocked with his forearm, but the spear force still grazed his side and tore a wound across his armor.
Blood splashed onto the stage.

chapters.title: Chapter 1875: Orion Giving His All!
paragraphs: Orion landed several meters away and looked down at the wound. Then he smiled.
"So you were waiting."
Ervin raised his spear calmly. "You were too fast to interrupt carelessly."
Orion laughed. "That is a compliment, right?"
"Yes."

The moment Ervin answered, the air around him changed. It sank, the light sank, and even the sound sank with it. The invisible pressure that had shocked everyone during his battle with Selene returned, spreading across the central stage like the arrival of a bottomless sea.

A black sea appeared behind Ervin, vast and silent and impossibly deep. From within that sea rose the broken ancient gate, half submerged and covered in mysterious symbols that no one could fully read. The moment it appeared, the nine stars inside Orion’s body flickered.
Ervin’s voice rang across the stage.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Abyssal Origin Descent."
Boom!

The battlefield transformed completely. The star palace behind Orion still shone brightly, but the black sea behind Ervin seemed to drag at its light. The nine stars within Orion’s body remained powerful, yet now every movement he made had to fight against the pressure of descent.
His star force did not vanish the way it had against Revona’s Void Origin Realm. Instead, it sank. It grew heavier, harder to circulate, harder to release, and harder to change quickly.
Orion felt the difference at once, and his smile dimmed slightly.
"This path really is unpleasant."
Ervin replied calmly, "Your stars shine too brightly."
Orion clenched his fists. "Then try swallowing them."

He rushed forward again, and the battle grew grander than before. Orion’s Nine Star Sovereign Body erupted with its full brilliance as he pushed all nine stars to their limit. He no longer relied on quick changes alone. Instead, he began combining several stars at once.

His First Star burned through the abyssal pull while his Second Star accelerated his movement. His Sixth Star deepened his pressure, and his Ninth Star anchored his authority. He crossed the sinking battlefield like a star refusing to fall.
Ervin answered with his black spear.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, First Depth Tide."

The black sea surged, and a wave of abyssal pressure rose from the ground to swallow half the stage. Orion strode through it with his body glowing brighter, though his speed visibly slowed. Ervin’s spear lanced out from within the wave, silent and precise. Orion blocked with his fist.
Boom!
Starlight and abyssal force detonated against each other. Orion was pushed back three steps, while Ervin gave up only one.
Orion’s eyes lit up again. "Good."
He gathered five stars into his arm.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Five-Star Heaven Breaker."
His fist shot forward, and Ervin raised his spear to meet it.
"Abyss Spear Art, Gate Shadow Thrust."

The thrust carried the shadow of the broken gate. It collided with Orion’s fist, and the five-star force shuddered violently. For a moment the star power seemed on the verge of piercing through, but the gate’s shadow dragged part of it downward and the attack lost its stability.
Orion gritted his teeth and changed once more, driving the Ninth Star into his fist at the final moment.
Boom!
The unstable attack exploded, and both men were hurled backward.

Orion landed with one knee briefly touching the ground while blood ran from his lips. His old injuries had torn open again. Starlight leaked from the cracks in his armor, and the nine stars within his body flickered unsteadily. Even so, his smile returned brighter than before.
Ervin’s sleeve had been shredded, and a wound ran across his left shoulder. He regarded Orion with rare seriousness.
"You are injured more than you show."
Orion rose slowly. "And you are stronger than you look."
The audience was completely absorbed. No one dared call this an easy victory for either side. Orion was weakened, yet he was still forcing Ervin to fight in earnest.
Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent was terrifying, yet Orion’s Nine Star Sovereign Body refused to sink without a fight.

The black sea rose again, and the nine stars blazed in answer. Through the next several exchanges, the entire stage looked like a starry heaven straining to escape a bottomless abyss. Orion’s punches birthed brilliant starbursts while Ervin’s spear carved dark lines through the battlefield.
Each time Orion gathered his power, the broken gate pulled at it, and each time Ervin tried to bury the stars, Orion shifted his star force and erupted from a different angle.
At last, Orion stepped back. His breathing had turned rough, and blood ran down his chin once more. Yet his eyes shone with the same reckless brilliance he had shown against Revona.
"I suppose I only have one move left that can trouble you."
Ervin’s grip tightened around his spear. "Starfall Extinction."
Orion smiled. "You saw it."
"I did."
"Then defend well."

The moment Orion spoke, the nine stars inside his body went still, and then they began to collapse inward. A terrible pressure radiated from his fist as the star palace behind him reappeared in a broken and desperate form.

The nine stars surrounding the palace shattered into streams of pure star essence and rushed into his arm. His body shook violently, several wounds reopened at once, and blood dripped onto the stage beneath his feet.
The Nine Star Court disciples fell silent. They knew what this technique had cost him against Revona, and now he was using it again while nowhere near fully recovered.
Orion’s smile did not waver.
"This technique is still incomplete," he said. "But if I wait until it is perfect, I will never know how far it can go."
The star essence compressed around his fist.
"Starfall Extinction."

Orion vanished. He appeared before Ervin with his final fist already falling. The compressed star essence roared within that strike, layered and collapsing, with each layer built to erupt the moment the one before it was swallowed or broken.
This was the technique Orion had forged himself, the move that had driven Revona to use Return To Nothing. Even in his weakened state, it carried shocking destructive force.

chapters.title: Chapter 1876: Revona vs Rakan!
paragraphs: Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent responded instantly. The black sea rose higher than it ever had, and the broken gate behind him began to open. It did not open slightly. It opened far wider than before. A soundless pressure spilled out from behind the gate, and for one brief instant, several of the top geniuses felt their hearts tighten.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
’That gate again.’
Ervin’s voice remained calm, but his aura had clearly grown heavier.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
The broken gate pulled, and Orion’s Starfall Extinction struck its edge.
Boom!

The star force exploded, but instead of spreading outward, it was dragged inward by the abyssal gate. The first layer of Starfall Extinction collapsed while still resisting. The second layer erupted and tore a crack across the gate’s shadow. The third layer burned like a dying star and forced Ervin back half a step.

Ervin’s expression shifted slightly. Orion roared and drove his fist deeper, and the star force pressed onward. For a moment it seemed that Starfall Extinction might pierce through the gate’s pull, but Orion’s body was no longer in peak condition.
The brilliance in his fist flickered and his arm trembled. The star essence within his body began breaking apart before the technique could reach its full eruption.
Ervin stepped forward as the black sea surged.
"Endless Depth."
The broken gate swallowed. The remaining layers of Starfall Extinction sank one by one into the abyssal opening, their light dimming like a star falling beneath an endless sea.
Orion tried to force out one final burst, but his body could no longer sustain it, and the last star layer collapsed before it could fully detonate.
The gate closed partway, and the starlight vanished.
Orion stood before Ervin with his fist still extended and blood dripping from his arm. For a moment, neither of them moved. Then Orion sighed.
"Again... not enough."
His body swayed. Ervin’s spear came to rest before his throat, but he did not thrust. Orion looked at the spear tip and laughed softly.
"I surrender before I faint standing."
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Orion Starfall Defeated.]
The arena stayed silent for a few breaths before the Nine Star Court disciples began cheering once more. They cheered not because Orion had won, but because he had fought with everything he had left.
Even wounded, exhausted, and far from his peak, he had forced Ervin to open the broken gate wider and use Return To Depth in earnest. That alone was enough to prove his strength all over again.
Ervin withdrew his spear. "You would have been more dangerous at full strength."
Orion smiled tiredly. "I will take that as comfort."
Ervin nodded. "It was meant as one."

The transfer light descended and carried both of them back to their pillars. Orion sat down the moment he returned, laughing weakly to himself as the Eternal Hourglass began healing his injuries once again.
Ervin remained standing, though his gaze lingered on Orion a moment longer than usual. The battle had not been easy, and everyone who understood the clash could see it plainly.
Orion had lost, but he had not fallen cheaply. And Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent had once again proven itself one of the most mysterious and dangerous Pseudo Cosmic Paths in the entire final stage.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Orion Starfall Defeated.]

The result drew sighs from many watchers. Orion was incredibly strong, and almost no one doubted that he belonged among the peak geniuses of the conference. Yet his repeated clashes against monsters like Revona and Ervin had left him in a punishing position.

His strength was real, his Pseudo Cosmic Path was majestic, and his self-created technique had shocked the Divine Realm. Even so, in this final stage, brilliance alone could still lose to a worse matchup.
The next major match arrived quickly.
[Damian Voss vs Morgana Starveil]

Morgana entered the arena wearing a bitter smile, fully aware that this was not a favorable fight. Her Star-Curse Labyrinth was extremely dangerous against most opponents, but Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven had already proven it could cut through the structure behind powerful Pseudo Cosmic Paths. She still fought with everything she had.
The Star-Curse Labyrinth opened, curse mirrors filled the stage, and countless witch symbols strained to twist Damian’s direction, his senses, and his sword rhythm.

Damian did not rush. He raised his sword and used "Sword Sovereign Heaven, First Edict, All Blades Refuse Submission," then followed with "Sword Sovereign Heaven, Third Edict, Blade Meets The Moonless Curse."

His blade carved through the curse mirrors one by one. When Morgana attempted to activate "Star-Curse Labyrinth, Nameless Witch Burial," Damian answered with "Sword Sovereign Heaven, One Sword Divides Heaven" and split the burial curse before it could close around him.
Morgana surrendered with a sigh, though no shame showed on her face.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Morgana Starveil Defeated.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Damian Voss]
[Total Battles Fought: 20]
[Total Wins: 20]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Morgana Starveil]
[Total Battles Fought: 20]
[Total Wins: 15]
"Of course he won," Rakan muttered from his pillar, though his eyes stayed sharp.
Morgana returned to her pillar and looked at Damian with a smile that was half amused and half weary. "Swordsmen are really unpleasant opponents."
Damian only nodded slightly, his expression as calm as ever.
Then another match seized everyone’s attention.
[Revona vs Rakan Thorne]
The moment those two names appeared together, the arena went quiet again, for this was no simple matchup.

Rakan Thorne possessed terrifying physical strength, and against most energy-based geniuses his War God Body was a walking nightmare. He could charge through attacks, break defensive formations with his bare fists, and drag opponents into close combat where very few could survive him.

Revona, however, was no ordinary long-range or energy-based fighter. Her Void Origin Eyes did more than block attacks. They erased force, nullified the structures of techniques, and dismantled the foundation of an enemy’s power before it ever fully reached her.

chapters.title: Chapter 1877: Max vs Divine Son!
paragraphs: When the battle began, Rakan opened the First Limit of the War God Body at once and charged with brutal speed. Revona erased the pressure surrounding his first punch, but Rakan’s physical body kept coming regardless.

The fist did not fully vanish, because the body behind it remained real, heavy, and terrifying. The blow forced Revona to retreat for the first time, and many spectators immediately understood that Rakan truly was a dangerous opponent for her.
Rakan laughed and opened the Second Limit. His bones roared like divine metal, and his charge became even harder to stop.

Revona’s Void Origin Eyes erased the outer force of his punches, yet every strike still carried enough physical momentum to shake the space around her. Again and again Rakan forced his way closer, smashing through layers of void ripples with the stubbornness of a war beast that refused to stop moving.

But Revona stayed calm. She did not panic, and she did not spend her power recklessly. Instead, she studied the rhythm of Rakan’s body. She watched the moment his blood surged, the instant his bones locked, and the brief pause between one explosive step and the next.

Her Void Origin Eyes made no attempt to erase him whole. They targeted the most critical points of his physical release, weakening the link between his movement and the war power bursting out of his body.
Rakan opened the Third Limit with a roar.
"War God Body, Third Limit, War Flesh Unbound."

His aura exploded, and the entire stage shook beneath him. For several breaths he truly seemed capable of smashing through everything. He drove Revona backward through sheer pressure, forcing her to weave movement and nullification together.

One of his punches nearly reached her shoulder, and its passing force tore a line through her sleeve and drew blood from her arm. The War God Palace disciples roared wildly, convinced that Rakan was about to overwhelm her.
Then Revona finally opened her Pseudo Cosmic Path.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Void Origin Realm."
The world behind her turned hollow. There was no sky, no ground, no sound, and no color. There was only origin-level emptiness.
The moment the Void Origin Realm spread, Rakan’s charge slowed. His War God Body still burned fiercely, but the force released by each step began disappearing before it could fully gather.

His fists remained dangerous, yet the explosive pressure around them was stripped away layer by layer. He tried to break through with "Three-Limit Heaven Breaker," but Revona condensed the Void Origin Realm around his fist and hollowed out most of its force before the punch could land.

Even then, the battle was far from easy. Rakan was simply too strong to fall to ordinary nullification. He kept advancing beneath the Void Origin Realm even as his body bled and his aura flickered, and he laughed as he threw punch after punch, forcing Revona to retreat several times.
At one point he shattered a section of her void field through raw physical momentum and very nearly reached her true body.
But nearly was not enough.
Revona’s eyes shone with terrifying clarity.
"Void Origin Realm, Return To Nothing."
The hollow world condensed into a single point before Rakan’s strongest punch, and his fist crashed into it.
For one brief moment, the War God Palace disciples believed he would break through. The bronze force of the War God Body roared violently as the Third Limit poured everything into that single strike.

But Return To Nothing did not try to withstand the punch the way a normal defense would. It folded the power inward, erased the gathered force, and returned the released war pressure to nothingness before any of it could touch her body.
Rakan’s fist stopped inches from her chest, and his eyes widened slightly.

Then Revona moved. A void ripple struck his chest, not to destroy his body directly, but to erase what remained of the War God Body’s released balance. Rakan’s bronze aura flickered wildly, and his knees sank into the cracked stage.
He tried to rise again, but his three limits had already been drained too far, and the Void Origin Realm pressed down around him like an invisible hollow sea.
For the first time, Rakan stopped smiling. Then he laughed bitterly.
"Fine. I lose."
[Winner: Revona.]
[Rakan Thorne Defeated.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 20]
[Total Wins: 20]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rakan Thorne]
[Total Battles Fought: 20]
[Total Wins: 18]

The result set off another wave of discussion across the Divine Realm. Revona had defeated Orion in a battle that pushed her to the very edge, and now she had beaten Rakan despite his terrifying War God Body. It proved once again that she was no mere counter to long-range fighters.
She stood among the strongest geniuses of the entire final stage, and her Void Origin Eyes and Void Origin Realm could adapt even against close combat monsters.

Rakan returned to his pillar with a helpless grin, while Revona sat down quietly upon reaching hers. Her aura wavered unsteadily, and it was obvious that defeating Rakan had cost her dearly, but a victory was a victory. Her undefeated record remained intact.
The records kept shifting. The upper rankings were growing clearer, yet the final order had still not been decided.

Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand once more, and the giant screen above the arena began to spin. The names flashed rapidly past, and yet nearly everyone in the arena felt an invisible pressure before the result even appeared.
Among the rotating names were Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Aurelian Lareth, Ervin, Kaiden Voidmere, Rakan Thorne, Revona, Orion Starfall, Selene Vaeloria, and Rosaline Lunara.
The light slowed, and the first name stopped.
[Max Morgan]
The entire arena went silent. Then the second name continued spinning. It passed over Damian, over Ervin, over Kaiden, and over Rakan.
Then it stopped.
[Aurelian Lareth]
For one breath, not a single sound could be heard. Then the screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Max Morgan vs Aurelian Lareth]
Angelina Valerius looked toward the two pillars and announced calmly.
"Max Morgan. Aurelian Lareth. Enter the stage."

chapters.title: Chapter 1878: Same Attacks!
paragraphs: Two beams of light descended from above the arena. One fell upon Max Morgan’s pillar, and the other fell upon Aurelian Lareth’s.

The moment both lights touched them, the entire Divine Realm seemed to grow still. This was not like Max’s battle against Rakan, where everyone had wondered whether his body could challenge the first Warlord of the War God Palace.

It was not like his battle against Kaiden, where the mystery of the Void Genesis Art had captured the attention of every space cultivator. This battle carried something much colder, much deeper, and far more personal.

Max Morgan stood against Aurelian Lareth. The black dragon genius faced the Divine Son of the second elven faction. The one who had risen like a monster through every stage of the Cosmic Ascension Conference now stood opposite the one who carried golden-white divine light and the prestige of a royal elven faction upon his shoulders.
Max appeared on one side of the central stage with his white hair falling around his face and his expression calm and unreadable.
No Emotion Severing Path appeared, and no Divine King Punishment rumbled above him. No dragon scales covered his skin, and no Draconic Essences roared through his body.
He looked almost ordinary compared to the terrifying pressure he had shown against Rakan and Kaiden, yet no one in the arena dared believe anymore that his calmness meant weakness.

Aurelian appeared opposite him. Golden-white light flowed around the Divine Son like a sacred robe. His pale golden hair drifted gently behind him, and his eyes shone with the cold pride of a man raised to stand above others.

Even after his loss to Damian Voss, his bearing remained noble, arrogant, and sharp. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline within him stirred faintly, and the moment it did, Max felt something inside his own body answer.
Aurelian felt it too, and his gaze turned colder.

Neither of them needed to speak the truth aloud. Aurelian already knew what he carried, for he had always known. He knew the source of his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline had once belonged to Max, and he knew that Max had uncovered that truth.
That was why the tension between them had never been simple hatred. It was a silent war over ownership, over identity, and over the right to stand beneath the name of divine light.

By now, Max’s own Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline had almost fully reawakened. The wounds left behind by the theft had healed enough that his light could circulate through his body with stability and brilliance once more.

His Dimension of Light had also grown stronger, rendering most light-based attacks meaningless against him. Yet one thing was still missing. The source itself remained inside Aurelian, and only by reclaiming it could Max’s bloodline truly return to completeness and evolve toward its real peak as a true Divine Bloodline.
Across the stage, Aurelian regarded him with a faint, cold smile.
"So it finally came to this."
Max looked at him calmly. "Yes."
Aurelian’s smile deepened, and there was no ignorance in it. There was only arrogance, defiance, and a frigid refusal to bow his head before the original owner of the power he carried.
"You have been waiting for this battle for a long time," Aurelian said.
Max’s eyes stayed calm. "So have you."
Aurelian’s golden-white light burned brighter. "Do not think that knowing the origin of something means you can take it back."
Max looked at the light surrounding him, and for a moment his expression turned cold enough to make even the air above the stage feel heavier.
"It feels strange," Max said quietly.
Aurelian narrowed his eyes. "What does?"
Max raised one hand and watched a faint golden-white glow bloom in his palm. "Feeling something inside me answer from across the stage."
The words were vague enough that the crowd could not grasp their true meaning.

To most spectators, it sounded like a mysterious resonance between two similar light-based powers. But Aurelian understood exactly what Max meant, and because he understood, his expression grew colder still.
"You speak as though bloodline alone decides ownership," Aurelian said. "Power belongs to the one who can wield it."
Max smiled faintly. "Then prove that it listens to you."

Aurelian’s eyes sharpened. For the first time, a trace of anger surfaced beneath his noble expression. It was not because Max had exposed the truth. It was because Max had touched the one fear Aurelian never allowed himself to admit.

What if the stolen power had never truly accepted him? What if it obeyed only because the original owner had been absent? And what if, now that Max stood before him, the bloodline inside his body remembered?
Aurelian slowly raised one hand as golden-white light gathered in his palm.
"Then watch carefully," he said coldly. "I will show you who stands above this light now."
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Aurelian attacked instantly.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Spear Rain."
Hundreds of golden-white spears formed in the air and plunged toward Max like divine punishment.

Each spear carried brilliant sacred power, sharp enough to pierce defensive barriers and pure enough to burn away darkness, curses, and corrupted energy. Against most opponents, an opening like this would force an immediate defense.
Max did not move. He only raised his hand, and golden-white light gathered around his fingers.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Spear Rain."
The same attack materialized above Max. Hundreds of golden-white spears took shape in the air, nearly identical in structure, rhythm, and radiance to the ones Aurelian had summoned.
The only difference was that Max’s light felt quieter and purer. It was less domineering and less forced, and somehow it felt more natural.
The two spear rains collided in midair.
Boom!
Golden-white light exploded across the stage, and countless fragments of sacred radiance scattered like broken stars.
The arena froze.
"He used the same technique?"
"That was Heavenly Luminance!"
"Max Morgan can use Heavenly Luminance power too?"
"How is that possible?"
Aurelian stared at Max, and his expression shifted for the first time.
Max lowered his hand calmly. "Surprised?"
Aurelian’s golden eyes went colder. "You copied my technique?"
Max shook his head. "No."
He raised his hand again.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sunwheel Descent."
A golden-white sunwheel blazed into existence above Max and spun toward Aurelian with terrifying speed.
Aurelian’s face hardened, and he summoned his own wheel at once.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sunwheel Descent."
The two wheels crashed together, and the impact rocked the stage. Both sunwheels shattered in the same instant.

Aurelian stepped back half a pace, not because he had truly been hurt, but because the shock in his heart had disturbed his rhythm. He could accept that Max was strong. He could accept Max wielding strange sword paths, dragon power, dimensional ability, and even the Void Genesis Art.

But watching Max command Heavenly Luminance techniques with such natural control struck at something far more fragile inside him. That light was supposed to be his symbol. It was his status, and it was his proof that he was the Divine Son.
Max watched him quietly. "Try something stronger."
Aurelian’s face darkened.
"Heavenly Luminance, Twelve Sacred Wings."

Twelve golden-white wings unfurled behind him, and countless feathers of light streaked toward Max from every direction, filling the stage with radiant blades. The attack was fast, dense, and oppressive, and every feather carried cutting force, burning heat, and purification power together.
