chapters.title: Chapter 1879: What can a thief do with stolen light?
paragraphs: Max stood still, and the feathers reached him. Or rather, they reached him and dissolved. The golden-white blades touched his body, but the light within them seemed to sink into an unseen luminous dimension surrounding him.
They could not pierce his skin, they could not burn his flesh, and they could not so much as disturb his breathing. They faded harmlessly away, as though returning to the place they had come from.
Aurelian’s eyes widened slightly.
Max watched the vanishing feathers and said calmly, "Too light."
Aurelian’s face turned ugly, and the Divine Realm erupted in disbelief.
"His attacks are not hurting Max!"
"He is not even defending!"
"The Twelve Sacred Wings vanished the moment they touched him!"
"What kind of light resistance is that?"
Max took one step forward as golden-white radiance climbed around his body. He lifted his hand, and twelve wings of light opened behind him as well.

Compared to Aurelian’s wings, Max’s looked less ornamental and less royal, yet far more intimate with the essence of light itself. They did not resemble the decoration of a throne. They looked like something born directly from a living source.
"Heavenly Luminance, Twelve Sacred Wings."
The feathers shot forward, and Aurelian raised his hand quickly.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Mirror Guard."
A golden-white mirror formed in front of him, and Max’s feathers struck it.
Crack!
The mirror split apart. Aurelian swept his arm and scattered the remaining feathers with a wave of divine light, but his expression had grown far colder than before.
He could no longer ignore what was happening. Max was not merely imitating the outer form of his techniques. He was wielding the Heavenly Luminance power with frightening compatibility.
Max looked at him and asked, "Does it bother you?"
Aurelian clenched his jaw. "What?"
"That when you look at me, the power inside you answers," Max said quietly.
The words remained vague enough for the audience to misread, but to Aurelian they felt like a blade sliding beneath his ribs.
Aurelian’s light erupted.
"Heavenly Luminance, Crowned Sun Judgment."

A crown of sacred light appeared above the stage and released a massive golden-white pillar straight down at Max. This attack carried far greater power than everything before it, enough to crush weaker Pseudo Cosmic Paths if wielded properly.
Max looked up as the pillar descended, and he did not dodge. The Crowned Sun Judgment struck him head-on.
Boom!
The stage around Max shattered beneath the force of the blow. Golden-white light swallowed his figure whole, and the arena barrier flared brightly from the impact.

Aurelian stared into the pillar with cold eyes. Then the light faded, and Max still stood there, entirely unharmed. His clothes had not even been singed. A faint golden-white glow flowed around him for a moment before sinking back into his body like water returning to the sea.
Max raised his eyes toward Aurelian. "Again."
The word was soft, yet it made Aurelian’s expression stiffen. For the first time, something close to disbelief entered the Divine Son’s eyes.
"No."
Max tilted his head slightly. "No?"
Aurelian’s aura surged violently.
"Heavenly Luminance, Royal Sun Spear."
A massive spear of divine light formed in his hand and shot toward Max’s chest. Max opened his palm, and the spear struck him and dissolved.
"Heavenly Luminance, Divine Flame Burial."
Golden-white flames rose from beneath Max’s feet and swallowed him, and then the flames simply disappeared.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Sun Cage."
A cage of radiant light closed around Max, every bar burning with sealing power. Max walked straight through it, and the cage shattered without offering the slightest resistance.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sun King’s Execution."
Aurelian shaped a giant blade of sacred light and swung it down with both hands. Max raised one finger, and the blade struck that finger and broke.
This time, the entire arena went completely silent.
Aurelian stared at Max’s finger, and then at Max’s face. His breathing had grown heavy.
Max lowered his hand slowly. "Do you understand now?"
Aurelian’s eyes turned cold and furious. "Understand what?"

Max stepped closer. The stage beneath his feet glowed faintly with golden-white light, but unlike Aurelian’s light, Max’s radiance made no attempt to dominate the battlefield. It simply existed, calm and absolute, as though the light around him felt no need to prove itself.
"You are trying to use light attacks that was never truly yours." Max said smiling.
Aurelian’s face changed. The sentence still was not open enough for the crowd to grasp the full truth, but it struck Aurelian directly.

The power he carried, the power he had treated as proof of his divinity, was failing against Max again and again. His attacks held enough force to injure other peak geniuses, yet against Max they collapsed as though they had lost their reason to harm him.
Max continued, his voice pitched low enough that only Aurelian could hear him clearly through the surrounding explosions of light. "Because what you carry came from me."
Aurelian’s pupils shrank. For one breath, all his arrogance cracked, and then it returned as fury.
"Shut up."

Golden-white light erupted behind him. Sacred halls appeared and radiant pillars rose, and a golden throne manifested beneath an endless sun. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion descended with overwhelming majesty, spreading across the central stage like a divine kingdom declaring judgment upon the world.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path," Aurelian said coldly, his voice trembling with anger he could barely suppress. "Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."
Boom!

The dominion swallowed the battlefield. This time, Aurelian held nothing back. The sacred halls poured out endless light while the radiant pillars locked onto Max. The throne beneath the sun blazed with oppressive authority, and the golden-white crown above Aurelian’s head grew nearly solid.
"Divine Dominion, Luminance Decree."
A sacred decree unfurled above Max and released countless words of divine judgment. Max stood beneath it as the words struck him, and they dissolved.
Aurelian’s expression twisted.
"Divine Dominion, Twelve Pillars of Sacred Judgment."

Twelve radiant pillars encircled Max and fired beams of Heavenly Luminance empowered by the Pseudo Cosmic Path from every direction. The beams struck him and faded against his body, like sunlight vanishing into a deeper light. Max slowly walked forward through the barrage, and his voice stayed calm.
"You are using my own bloodline’s light against me."
Aurelian’s face paled slightly.
"Divine Dominion, Royal Mandate of the Endless Sun."

The endless sun above the divine kingdom flared brighter than it ever had. A massive pillar of golden-white authority came crashing down, pouring all of its judgment, purification, and suppression onto Max.
Max stopped walking. The light struck him in full, the ground around him cracked, and the barrier trembled. Yet Max remained standing.

The Dimension of Light within him opened in silence, and the Heavenly Luminance power straining to injure him was drawn into that inner dimension, where it was scattered, absorbed, and rendered harmless.

It was not that Aurelian’s attack was weak. Against almost anyone else, it would have been terrifying. Against Max, however, light itself held almost no meaning as a weapon unless it was used as an attack by someone who was way too stronger than him.

Max looked at Aurelian through the pillar of radiance, and Aurelian stared back. For the first time, true anxiety surfaced in the Divine Son’s eyes. He could not understand it, and he could not accept it.

His Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion had injured Morgana, suppressed Rakan at range, and fought Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven to the very limit. Yet against Max, it felt as though he were throwing water into the ocean.
Max stepped forward again, and the Royal Mandate shattered around him.
"You relied on something that was never truly yours," Max said softly. "You built status on it. You built pride on it. You built your path on it."
Aurelian’s lips tightened, and Max’s gaze grew colder.
"But when the owner stands before you, what can a thief do with stolen light?"

sentences.text: Max stood still, and the feathers reached him.
Or rather, they reached him and dissolved.
The golden-white blades touched his body, but the light within them seemed to sink into an unseen luminous dimension surrounding him.
They could not pierce his skin, they could not burn his flesh, and they could not so much as disturb his breathing.
They faded harmlessly away, as though returning to the place they had come from.
Aurelian’s eyes widened slightly.
Max watched the vanishing feathers and said calmly, "Too light."
Aurelian’s face turned ugly, and the Divine Realm erupted in disbelief.
"His attacks are not hurting Max!"
"He is not even defending!"
"The Twelve Sacred Wings vanished the moment they touched him!"
"What kind of light resistance is that?"
Max took one step forward as golden-white radiance climbed around his body.
He lifted his hand, and twelve wings of light opened behind him as well.
Compared to Aurelian’s wings, Max’s looked less ornamental and less royal, yet far more intimate with the essence of light itself.
They did not resemble the decoration of a throne.
They looked like something born directly from a living source.
"Heavenly Luminance, Twelve Sacred Wings."
The feathers shot forward, and Aurelian raised his hand quickly.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Mirror Guard."
A golden-white mirror formed in front of him, and Max’s feathers struck it.
Crack!
The mirror split apart.
Aurelian swept his arm and scattered the remaining feathers with a wave of divine light, but his expression had grown far colder than before.
He could no longer ignore what was happening.
Max was not merely imitating the outer form of his techniques.
He was wielding the Heavenly Luminance power with frightening compatibility.
Max looked at him and asked, "Does it bother you?"
Aurelian clenched his jaw.
"What?"
"That when you look at me, the power inside you answers," Max said quietly.
The words remained vague enough for the audience to misread, but to Aurelian they felt like a blade sliding beneath his ribs.
Aurelian’s light erupted.
"Heavenly Luminance, Crowned Sun Judgment."
A crown of sacred light appeared above the stage and released a massive golden-white pillar straight down at Max.
This attack carried far greater power than everything before it, enough to crush weaker Pseudo Cosmic Paths if wielded properly.
Max looked up as the pillar descended, and he did not dodge.
The Crowned Sun Judgment struck him head-on.
Boom!
The stage around Max shattered beneath the force of the blow.
Golden-white light swallowed his figure whole, and the arena barrier flared brightly from the impact.
Aurelian stared into the pillar with cold eyes.
Then the light faded, and Max still stood there, entirely unharmed.
His clothes had not even been singed.
A faint golden-white glow flowed around him for a moment before sinking back into his body like water returning to the sea.
Max raised his eyes toward Aurelian.
"Again."
The word was soft, yet it made Aurelian’s expression stiffen.
For the first time, something close to disbelief entered the Divine Son’s eyes.
"No."
Max tilted his head slightly.
"No?"
Aurelian’s aura surged violently.
"Heavenly Luminance, Royal Sun Spear."
A massive spear of divine light formed in his hand and shot toward Max’s chest.
Max opened his palm, and the spear struck him and dissolved.
"Heavenly Luminance, Divine Flame Burial."
Golden-white flames rose from beneath Max’s feet and swallowed him, and then the flames simply disappeared.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Sun Cage."
A cage of radiant light closed around Max, every bar burning with sealing power.
Max walked straight through it, and the cage shattered without offering the slightest resistance.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sun King’s Execution."
Aurelian shaped a giant blade of sacred light and swung it down with both hands.
Max raised one finger, and the blade struck that finger and broke.
This time, the entire arena went completely silent.
Aurelian stared at Max’s finger, and then at Max’s face.
His breathing had grown heavy.
Max lowered his hand slowly.
"Do you understand now?"
Aurelian’s eyes turned cold and furious.
"Understand what?"
Max stepped closer.
The stage beneath his feet glowed faintly with golden-white light, but unlike Aurelian’s light, Max’s radiance made no attempt to dominate the battlefield.
It simply existed, calm and absolute, as though the light around him felt no need to prove itself.
"You are trying to use light attacks that was never truly yours." Max said smiling.
Aurelian’s face changed.
The sentence still was not open enough for the crowd to grasp the full truth, but it struck Aurelian directly.
The power he carried, the power he had treated as proof of his divinity, was failing against Max again and again.
His attacks held enough force to injure other peak geniuses, yet against Max they collapsed as though they had lost their reason to harm him.
Max continued, his voice pitched low enough that only Aurelian could hear him clearly through the surrounding explosions of light.
"Because what you carry came from me."
Aurelian’s pupils shrank.
For one breath, all his arrogance cracked, and then it returned as fury.
"Shut up."
Golden-white light erupted behind him.
Sacred halls appeared and radiant pillars rose, and a golden throne manifested beneath an endless sun.
The Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion descended with overwhelming majesty, spreading across the central stage like a divine kingdom declaring judgment upon the world.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path," Aurelian said coldly, his voice trembling with anger he could barely suppress.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."
Boom!
The dominion swallowed the battlefield.
This time, Aurelian held nothing back.
The sacred halls poured out endless light while the radiant pillars locked onto Max.
The throne beneath the sun blazed with oppressive authority, and the golden-white crown above Aurelian’s head grew nearly solid.
"Divine Dominion, Luminance Decree."
A sacred decree unfurled above Max and released countless words of divine judgment.
Max stood beneath it as the words struck him, and they dissolved.
Aurelian’s expression twisted.
"Divine Dominion, Twelve Pillars of Sacred Judgment."
Twelve radiant pillars encircled Max and fired beams of Heavenly Luminance empowered by the Pseudo Cosmic Path from every direction.
The beams struck him and faded against his body, like sunlight vanishing into a deeper light.
Max slowly walked forward through the barrage, and his voice stayed calm.
"You are using my own bloodline’s light against me."
Aurelian’s face paled slightly.
"Divine Dominion, Royal Mandate of the Endless Sun."
The endless sun above the divine kingdom flared brighter than it ever had.

Yet against Max, it felt as though he were throwing water into the ocean.
Max stepped forward again, and the Royal Mandate shattered around him.
"You relied on something that was never truly yours," Max said softly.
"You built status on it.
You built pride on it.
You built your path on it."

"But when the owner stands before you, what can a thief do with stolen light?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1880: Take Care of It!
paragraphs: Aurelian’s expression finally broke.
"Shut up!"
The golden throne behind him shattered, and its fragments flew into his body. His aura condensed sharply into something unstable and terrifying.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Crownless Divine King."

The divine kingdom contracted around him. The sacred halls vanished, the radiant pillars compressed, and the endless sun became a burning crown at his back. All the authority of the dominion merged into his flesh, his spear, and his bloodline.
This was the state he had used against Damian, the form that turned him into a living weapon of divine judgment.
Aurelian appeared before Max in an instant.
"Crownless Divine King, Light That Judges All Blades."

A spear of condensed divine light lanced toward Max’s throat. Max did not draw Dragonheart. He raised his hand and caught the spear. The light exploded between his fingers, and then it simply disappeared.
Aurelian froze.
Max regarded him from a distance of only a few steps. "You still do not understand."
He squeezed, and the spear shattered. Aurelian stumbled back in shock, and Max followed calmly.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Palm Seal."
Max’s palm struck Aurelian’s chest.
Boom!
Aurelian flew backward with golden-white blood spraying from his mouth, and he crashed into one of the remaining radiant pillars of his own dominion.
The audience erupted.
"Max used Heavenly Luminance to injure him!"
"Aurelian’s light cannot hurt Max, but Max’s light can hurt him!"
"What is happening?"
"Is Max’s Heavenly Luminance stronger?"
Aurelian struggled to his feet, and his eyes were no longer calm. The arrogance still lingered, but now it was tangled with confusion, fear, and disbelief.
Max kept walking toward him. "You were proud of this power," he said quietly. "But every time you use it, you only remind me of what I will take back."
Aurelian’s breath caught, because this time he understood the meaning completely, and his face drained of color. Max had not spoken loudly, and he had not exposed the truth for the world to hear.

The surrounding storm of golden-white light hid his words from most people, and the distortion of the dominion kept anyone else from hearing clearly. But Aurelian heard every word, and each one struck his mind harder than any fist.
Take back. That meant Max knew. Max knew what had been done, and he knew where the source remained. Max knew that the bloodline inside Aurelian had never truly been his.
Aurelian’s hands trembled, and he forced them still.
"No," he whispered.
Max’s eyes were cold. "Yes."
Aurelian roared and raised both hands.
"Crownless Divine King, Final Luminance Judgment."
The enormous divine sword of golden-white light took shape above him. This was the same attack Damian had cut apart, but this time Aurelian poured far more desperation into it.
His bloodline burned and his dominion shook, and the endless sun behind him dimmed as every scrap of its remaining authority flowed into the blade.
The divine sword descended.
Max looked up as golden-white light rose around his own body. He did not use a Pseudo Cosmic Path, for he did not yet possess a perfected light-based path of his own.
But he had the Dimension of Light, he had his almost fully reawakened Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, and he held authority over the very light Aurelian was wielding.
Max raised his palm.
"Heavenly Luminance, First Dawn Reversal."

A quiet golden-white light spread from his hand. It did not clash violently against the Final Luminance Judgment. Instead, it seeped into the descending divine sword and disturbed the bloodline rhythm within it.
The massive blade shuddered. Its outer layer remained powerful, but its inner structure began to loosen, as though something inside it had recognized Max and ceased obeying Aurelian completely.
Aurelian’s eyes widened in horror. "No..."

Max’s palm closed, and the Final Luminance Judgment shattered from within. Fragments of divine light rained down around Max like broken glass. Aurelian stumbled backward as the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion flickered violently behind him.
Then Max appeared in front of him, and this time his palm stopped mere inches from Aurelian’s chest.
Aurelian froze, and the golden-white light around him shook uncontrollably.
Max looked into his eyes and spoke in a voice meant for him alone.
"Take care of my bloodline until then."
Aurelian’s face lost every trace of color. Max’s eyes remained calm, but the killing intent buried beneath that calm was so cold that Aurelian felt his very soul tighten.
"It will not be long before I come for it."
Aurelian’s lips parted, but no words emerged. In that moment, he no longer resembled the proud Divine Son who had stood above countless geniuses.
He looked like a man who had suddenly realized that the throne beneath him had been built over a pit, and that the owner of the pit had finally returned.
Max did not strike his heart. He could have, and he wanted to. But Angelina Valerius hovered above the stage, and the laws of the Eternal Hourglass tracked every movement.
If Max tried to kill Aurelian here, or attempted to extract the stolen bloodline source in front of everyone, Angelina would intervene at once.

Max was certain of it. Even if he could resist her for a moment, the risk was not worth taking. This was not the place, and this was not the time. He would wait until he had the right moment, the right ground, and the certainty to reclaim what was his without losing everything else.
So he did not kill him. He only pressed two fingers against Aurelian’s chest.
"Heavenly Luminance, Dawn Break."
Boom!
A controlled burst of golden-white light slammed into Aurelian’s body. His remaining dominion shattered, and the Crownless Divine King state collapsed.

Aurelian was hurled backward and crashed into the ground, rolling across the cracked stage before coming to rest near the edge of the arena. Golden-white blood stained his lips while his aura guttered weakly.
He tried to lift himself, but his hands shook too badly to hold him.
Max stood where he was, calm and untouched.
Aurelian looked up at him from the ground, and no arrogance remained in his eyes. There was only silence, only disbelief, and only a fear he tried and failed to hide.
Angelina Valerius looked down at the stage for a moment, and then she announced the result calmly.
"Aurelian Lareth is unable to continue."
The screen above the arena changed.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Aurelian Lareth Defeated.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 19]
[Total Wins: 19]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Aurelian Lareth]
[Total Battles Fought: 20]
[Total Wins: 18]

The result shone above everyone, and the Divine Realm stayed silent. Aurelian Lareth, the Divine Son of the second elven faction, had lost yet again. But this defeat was different from the one Damian had handed him.
Damian had cut down his dominion with the sword. Max had rendered the very light he relied upon useless.

The viewing halls of the second elven faction went deathly still. Elders stared at the screen with rigid faces, unable to comprehend how Max could wield Heavenly Luminance power so naturally, or why Aurelian’s strongest light-based attacks had failed to harm him at all.
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples exploded into thunderous cheers.

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Damian Voss studied Max with narrowed eyes, and Kaiden Voidmere’s expression turned thoughtful. Ervin watched in silence while Revona’s Void Origin Eyes flickered faintly.
Rakan Thorne let out a low laugh, though even he kept his voice down.
Max stood on the stage and looked at Aurelian one final time. Aurelian, sprawled on the cracked ground, stared back at him. No words passed between them this time, because none were needed.
The transfer light descended and carried the defeated Divine Son back to his pillar, and a moment later, Max returned to his own.

The battle had ended, but for Aurelian Lareth, something far worse than defeat had just begun. He now understood that the power he had treated as his divine proof was no shelter at all. It was a debt, and Max Morgan had come to collect it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1881: Ervin vs Kaiden!
paragraphs: After Max Morgan defeated Aurelian Lareth, the entire final competitive stage stayed silent for a long while.
It was not because the battle had been the most destructive one so far.

In terms of pure destruction, Orion’s Starfall Extinction against Revona had shaken the arena just as fiercely, and so had Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven against Aurelian’s Divine Dominion, along with Rakan’s physical collision against Aurelian’s long-range Heavenly Luminance suppression.
What set Max’s victory apart was the manner in which he had won.

He had not cut Aurelian’s light apart the way Damian had. He had not tried to overpower the Divine Son with brute force the way Rakan had attempted, and he had not erased the attacks the way Revona would have.
He had simply stood there and let the Heavenly Luminance power collapse around him, as though Aurelian’s divine light had no right to harm him at all.
Then he had used that very same light to break Aurelian’s dominion, shatter his pride, and leave him silent on the ground.
The spectators across the Divine Realm could not grasp the full truth, but they could feel the humiliation buried inside that defeat. Aurelian Lareth had lost far more than a battle.
The symbol he carried had been challenged, and the authority of the second elven faction’s Divine Son had been shaken before every major force watching the Cosmic Ascension Conference.

Aurelian sat on his pillar with his head lowered slightly. He did not speak, and he did not look at Max. The golden-white light around his body had gone quiet, almost suppressed, and even the faint crown-like glow that usually hovered above him had vanished.
The laws of the Eternal Hourglass mended his injuries, but they could not mend the fear Max had planted inside his heart.
On another pillar, Max stood calmly with his expression unchanged, and he did not spare Aurelian another glance. The battle had ended, and he had already said everything that needed saying.
For now, the stolen bloodline source would remain inside Aurelian, because the Eternal Hourglass, Angelina Valerius, and the eyes of countless great powers made reclaiming it here impossible.
But the debt had been marked, and the warning had been delivered. It would not be long.
Angelina Valerius waited until the arena’s atmosphere settled somewhat before raising her hand again.
"The final competitive stage will continue."

The giant screen above the stage began to spin once more, and the participants forced themselves to recover their focus. Max’s victory over Aurelian had been shocking, but the round-robin stage was not yet finished. The top rankings remained unsettled, and several major battles still lay ahead.
Damian Voss stood undefeated, Revona stood undefeated, and Max stood undefeated as well. Ervin was the same as well.

Kaiden Voidmere had fallen to Max, yet no one dared underestimate him on the strength of that single result. In fact, after watching Max’s battle with Kaiden, many people had begun to suspect that Kaiden’s true power had never been fully displayed.
That suspicion took on far greater weight when the screen stopped again.
The first name appeared.
[Ervin]
The arena immediately grew quieter. Then the second name slowed and came to rest.
[Kaiden Voidmere]
For a moment, the spectators seemed to draw breath as one. The screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Ervin vs Kaiden Voidmere]
A wave of excitement rolled through the Divine Realm, because this was another major battle. Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent had defeated Selene, Rosaline, and Orion.

His broken gate had swallowed Heavenly Luminance Genesis, Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, and Starfall Extinction in turn. Every time he fought seriously, watchers felt as though they were staring into a bottomless abyss whose true depth remained hidden.

Kaiden Voidmere, however, was no ordinary opponent. Against Max, his brilliance had been eclipsed, because Max’s mastery of the Void Genesis Art surpassed his own and the Dimensional Sovereign Body rendered spatial attacks nearly meaningless.

That battle had made Kaiden appear suppressed, but anyone with real judgment understood the truth. Kaiden had not been weak. He had simply drawn the worst possible opponent, a man who walked the same path at a higher level and stood almost immune to the very element Kaiden relied upon.
Against Ervin, no such restriction existed. Kaiden could finally show the true terror of the Grand Void Sanctum.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both participants.
"Ervin."
"Kaiden Voidmere."
"Enter the stage."

Two beams of light descended. Ervin appeared on one side of the central stage with his black spear resting calmly in his hand. His aura remained quiet, but after so many battles, no one mistook that quietness for weakness anymore.
It was the silence of something lying deep beneath the surface, something that had no need to roar because everything above it would eventually sink.
Kaiden appeared opposite him in silver-gray robes, his expression calm and thoughtful. Unlike the aftermath of his battle with Max, no trace of helplessness lingered in his eyes now.
He regarded Ervin with genuine seriousness, and the space around him began to ripple before the battle had even begun.
Ervin studied him calmly. "You held back against Max."
Kaiden shook his head. "No. I simply had no chance to show more against him."
Ervin’s eyes deepened slightly.
Kaiden continued, "Against him, all my attacks were useless but not against you."
Ervin raised his spear. "Then show me."
Kaiden’s silver-gray pupils shone. "I will."
Angelina raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Kaiden moved first.
"Void Genesis Art, Empty Step."
His body vanished, and at almost the same instant, dozens of spatial ripples bloomed around Ervin. They were neither afterimages nor illusions.
Each ripple was a folded path that could deliver Kaiden’s attack from a different angle, and each one carried enough distortion to tear an ordinary defense apart.
Ervin’s spear moved.
"Abyss Spear Art, Hollow Moon Guard."
A dark crescent took shape around him. Kaiden appeared above the crescent and pressed one palm downward.
"Void Genesis Art, Space Burial Palm."
The space around Ervin sank like a collapsing tomb. The Hollow Moon Guard trembled and then cracked beneath the pressure. Ervin stepped back once and thrust his spear upward.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Thrust."
The spear lanced toward Kaiden’s palm, but Kaiden’s body slid sideways without his feet ever moving.
"Void Genesis Art, Hollow Displacement."
The spear passed through the place where Kaiden should have been, and in the next instant, he appeared behind Ervin.
"Void Genesis Art, Sevenfold Severing Line."

Seven invisible spatial lines slashed toward Ervin’s back. Ervin spun sharply and swept his spear behind him, but two of the seven lines still slipped through his defense and opened shallow wounds across his shoulder and waist.

sentences.text: After Max Morgan defeated Aurelian Lareth, the entire final competitive stage stayed silent for a long while.
It was not because the battle had been the most destructive one so far.

In terms of pure destruction, Orion’s Starfall Extinction against Revona had shaken the arena just as fiercely, and so had Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven against Aurelian’s Divine Dominion, along with Rakan’s physical collision against Aurelian’s long-range Heavenly Luminance suppression.
What set Max’s victory apart was the manner in which he had won.
He had not cut Aurelian’s light apart the way Damian had.
He had not tried to overpower the Divine Son with brute force the way Rakan had attempted, and he had not erased the attacks the way Revona would have.
He had simply stood there and let the Heavenly Luminance power collapse around him, as though Aurelian’s divine light had no right to harm him at all.
Then he had used that very same light to break Aurelian’s dominion, shatter his pride, and leave him silent on the ground.
The spectators across the Divine Realm could not grasp the full truth, but they could feel the humiliation buried inside that defeat.
Aurelian Lareth had lost far more than a battle.
The symbol he carried had been challenged, and the authority of the second elven faction’s Divine Son had been shaken before every major force watching the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Aurelian sat on his pillar with his head lowered slightly.
He did not speak, and he did not look at Max.
The golden-white light around his body had gone quiet, almost suppressed, and even the faint crown-like glow that usually hovered above him had vanished.
The laws of the Eternal Hourglass mended his injuries, but they could not mend the fear Max had planted inside his heart.
On another pillar, Max stood calmly with his expression unchanged, and he did not spare Aurelian another glance.
The battle had ended, and he had already said everything that needed saying.
For now, the stolen bloodline source would remain inside Aurelian, because the Eternal Hourglass, Angelina Valerius, and the eyes of countless great powers made reclaiming it here impossible.
But the debt had been marked, and the warning had been delivered.
It would not be long.
Angelina Valerius waited until the arena’s atmosphere settled somewhat before raising her hand again.
"The final competitive stage will continue."
The giant screen above the stage began to spin once more, and the participants forced themselves to recover their focus.
Max’s victory over Aurelian had been shocking, but the round-robin stage was not yet finished.
The top rankings remained unsettled, and several major battles still lay ahead.
Damian Voss stood undefeated, Revona stood undefeated, and Max stood undefeated as well.
Ervin was the same as well.
Kaiden Voidmere had fallen to Max, yet no one dared underestimate him on the strength of that single result.
In fact, after watching Max’s battle with Kaiden, many people had begun to suspect that Kaiden’s true power had never been fully displayed.
That suspicion took on far greater weight when the screen stopped again.
The first name appeared.
[Ervin]
The arena immediately grew quieter.
Then the second name slowed and came to rest.
[Kaiden Voidmere]
For a moment, the spectators seemed to draw breath as one.
The screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Ervin vs Kaiden Voidmere]
A wave of excitement rolled through the Divine Realm, because this was another major battle.
Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent had defeated Selene, Rosaline, and Orion.
His broken gate had swallowed Heavenly Luminance Genesis, Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, and Starfall Extinction in turn.
Every time he fought seriously, watchers felt as though they were staring into a bottomless abyss whose true depth remained hidden.
Kaiden Voidmere, however, was no ordinary opponent.
Against Max, his brilliance had been eclipsed, because Max’s mastery of the Void Genesis Art surpassed his own and the Dimensional Sovereign Body rendered spatial attacks nearly meaningless.
That battle had made Kaiden appear suppressed, but anyone with real judgment understood the truth.
Kaiden had not been weak.
He had simply drawn the worst possible opponent, a man who walked the same path at a higher level and stood almost immune to the very element Kaiden relied upon.
Against Ervin, no such restriction existed.
Kaiden could finally show the true terror of the Grand Void Sanctum.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both participants.
"Ervin."
"Kaiden Voidmere."
"Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.
Ervin appeared on one side of the central stage with his black spear resting calmly in his hand.
His aura remained quiet, but after so many battles, no one mistook that quietness for weakness anymore.
It was the silence of something lying deep beneath the surface, something that had no need to roar because everything above it would eventually sink.
Kaiden appeared opposite him in silver-gray robes, his expression calm and thoughtful.
Unlike the aftermath of his battle with Max, no trace of helplessness lingered in his eyes now.
He regarded Ervin with genuine seriousness, and the space around him began to ripple before the battle had even begun.
Ervin studied him calmly.
"You held back against Max."
Kaiden shook his head.
"No.
I simply had no chance to show more against him."
Ervin’s eyes deepened slightly.
Kaiden continued, "Against him, all my attacks were useless but not against you."
Ervin raised his spear.
"Then show me."
Kaiden’s silver-gray pupils shone.
"I will."
Angelina raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Kaiden moved first.
"Void Genesis Art, Empty Step."
His body vanished, and at almost the same instant, dozens of spatial ripples bloomed around Ervin.
They were neither afterimages nor illusions.
Each ripple was a folded path that could deliver Kaiden’s attack from a different angle, and each one carried enough distortion to tear an ordinary defense apart.
Ervin’s spear moved.
"Abyss Spear Art, Hollow Moon Guard."
A dark crescent took shape around him.
Kaiden appeared above the crescent and pressed one palm downward.
"Void Genesis Art, Space Burial Palm."
The space around Ervin sank like a collapsing tomb.
The Hollow Moon Guard trembled and then cracked beneath the pressure.
Ervin stepped back once and thrust his spear upward.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Thrust."
The spear lanced toward Kaiden’s palm, but Kaiden’s body slid sideways without his feet ever moving.
"Void Genesis Art, Hollow Displacement."
The spear passed through the place where Kaiden should have been, and in the next instant, he appeared behind Ervin.
"Void Genesis Art, Sevenfold Severing Line."
Seven invisible spatial lines slashed toward Ervin’s back.
Ervin spun sharply and swept his spear behind him, but two of the seven lines still slipped through his defense and opened shallow wounds across his shoulder and waist.

chapters.title: Chapter 1882: Kaiden’s True Strength!
paragraphs: The arena stirred at once.
"He injured Ervin!"
"Kaiden is much sharper than he looked against Max!"
"Against Max his attacks seemed useless, but against Ervin every spatial cut is dangerous!"
Kaiden did not pause. He raised both hands, and the entire central stage split into overlapping planes.
"Void Genesis Art, Thousand-Layer Spatial Cage."

Ervin’s surroundings folded again and again. Transparent layers of space formed a prison around him, and every layer shifted to its own rhythm. If Ervin moved forward, the distance stretched away from him. If he moved backward, the ground folded beneath his feet, and if he thrust his spear, the attack was rerouted through another plane entirely.
Ervin’s expression grew more serious.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."

The black sea appeared behind him, and the broken gate rose from its depths. The moment his Pseudo Cosmic Path descended, the pressure across the battlefield changed. The folded spatial cage began to sink, as though its layers had suddenly gained weight.
The black sea spread toward the transparent walls, pulling at them and dragging them downward, straining to collapse space itself into the abyssal current.
Kaiden’s eyes sharpened.
"Grand Void Sanctum, Void Anchor Seal."

Silver-gray anchors materialized within the spatial layers. They pierced into the folded planes and pinned them in place, keeping the Thousand-Layer Spatial Cage from sinking entirely into Ervin’s abyssal pressure. The clash between the cage and the black sea set the arena trembling. Space fought to fold while the abyss fought to drag everything down.
Ervin lifted his spear.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, First Depth Tide."
The black sea surged upward, and Kaiden raised one hand to meet it.
"Void Genesis Art, World-Folding Barrier."

The tide crashed into the folded barrier and split across several spatial planes. Rather than striking Kaiden directly, most of the abyssal wave was rerouted into empty layers of space. Yet the abyssal pressure was too strange to be fully contained. Even after redirection, part of it kept sinking down through the folds, and Kaiden was forced back half a step.
His expression grew even more focused as Ervin advanced.
"Abyss Spear Art, Gate Shadow Thrust."
The shadow of the broken gate gathered around his spear tip, and the thrust crossed the distance between them like a black line drawn up from the bottom of the sea.
Kaiden did not block in any ordinary way. His hands moved, and the space in front of him twisted into a spiral.
"Void Genesis Art, Spiral Exile Gate."

The spear thrust entered the spiral and vanished. For one brief moment, everyone believed Kaiden had exiled the attack into some distant spatial layer entirely. Then Kaiden’s head snapped around. The spear thrust had reappeared behind him, having forced its way back through the exile gate by riding the abyssal pull into the battlefield.
Kaiden’s eyes narrowed.
"Void Genesis Art, Origin Fold Reversal."
The space behind him folded backward and barely diverted the thrust past his shoulder. Even so, the black spear force grazed him and tore a line through his silver-gray robe.
Kaiden and Ervin retreated at the same moment, and neither of them looked relaxed any longer.
Rakan Thorne’s eyes gleamed from his pillar. "Now this is a fight."
Damian Voss watched quietly. "Kaiden is showing far more than he did against Max."
Revona nodded faintly. "Because Ervin cannot ignore spatial attacks."
Orion Starfall smiled weakly. "And because Ervin’s abyss can drag space itself down. What a troublesome pair."

Max observed the battle calmly, and he understood Kaiden’s strength better than most. Against him, Kaiden had looked restrained only because the Dimensional Sovereign Body and a higher mastery of the Void Genesis Art had ruined the matchup entirely.

Now, against Ervin, Kaiden’s true power was finally coming into view. His spatial control ran anything but shallow. His techniques were layered, precise, and frighteningly difficult to predict, and even Ervin’s abyss could not swallow them casually.
On the stage, Kaiden drew a slow breath, and the space behind him opened. A vast silver-gray void unfolded, filled with countless corridors, mirrors, and broken spatial planes.
This was no ordinary field technique. It was the manifestation of his deepest spatial foundation, a terrifying maze of the void where every direction could be folded, severed, or exiled at his will.
Kaiden’s voice rang out calmly.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."
The silver-gray void expanded.
"Grand Void Labyrinth."

The moment the name appeared, the entire central stage shifted. The ground grew distant and the sky became layered. Ervin now stood at the center of a labyrinth built from folded space, where every wall was a passage, every passage was a blade, and every blade could become a prison.

Compared to Max’s sovereign command over space, Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth was something different in nature. It did not attempt to rule space as a true sovereign would. Instead, it turned space into an endless battlefield of traps, routes, distortions, and points of exile.
This was Kaiden’s true power, a Pseudo Cosmic Path forged from the Void Genesis Art and the deepest spatial principles of the Grand Void Sanctum.
Inside the Grand Void Labyrinth, Kaiden’s aura climbed sharply.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Corridor of Ten Thousand Cuts."

The spatial corridors around Ervin opened, and invisible cuts poured in from every direction. Ervin spun his spear and released a deep abyssal ring, but the cuts did not all arrive within the same layer.

Some came through present space while others emerged from folded space. Some appeared only after a delay of half a breath, and some bypassed the spear ring entirely to materialize right beside his body.
Blood splashed, and several wounds opened across Ervin’s arms and shoulders.
The arena erupted.
"Kaiden is suppressing Ervin!"
"This is his Pseudo Cosmic Path!"
"The Grand Void Labyrinth, what a terrifying path!"
Ervin’s eyes grew darker, and the black sea behind him climbed higher.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth."

The broken gate opened, and the pull of the abyssal origin surged outward to drag at the Grand Void Labyrinth. Several spatial corridors bent downward and began sinking toward the black sea. But Kaiden’s figure appeared at the end of one corridor with his hand already descending.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Exile Palm."

The palm struck the air, and Ervin’s left side vanished. It was not his body that disappeared, but rather the space around his left side, which was exiled for a brief moment and broke his balance. Kaiden pressed the advantage at once.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Mirror Burial."

Dozens of mirrored spaces bloomed around Ervin, each one reflecting a different version of him. Then all the reflections collapsed inward, seeking to bury his real body among the false spatial layers.
Ervin drove his spear into the ground.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Second Depth Pressure."

The black sea deepened, and the mirrored spaces sank sharply and cracked beneath the pressure. Yet the Grand Void Labyrinth was too flexible to break so easily. The shattered mirrors simply reformed into new corridors, and from those corridors, Kaiden attacked again and again.

For the first time in the tournament, Ervin was being driven to the edge. Wounds accumulated across his body, and his spear movements grew heavier. The black sea remained terrifying, but every time it tried to swallow Kaiden’s path, the Grand Void Labyrinth shifted and opened a fresh route.

Kaiden never lingered in one place long enough to be dragged down. He fought like a master of endless distance, never striking from where Ervin expected and never allowing the abyss to fully claim his position.
The Grand Void Sanctum disciples finally erupted.
"Senior Brother Kaiden!"
"Show them the Grand Void Labyrinth!"
"This is his true strength!"

Even the elders of the Grand Void Sanctum looked satisfied. Against Max, Kaiden’s pride had been smothered by an impossible counter. Against Ervin, the Divine Realm could finally see why Kaiden Voidmere ranked among the strongest geniuses of the entire conference.

chapters.title: Chapter 1883: Mysterious Ervin!
paragraphs: On the stage, Ervin took another wound across his chest, and his black spear dipped slightly. Kaiden appeared far above him through a folded corridor.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, World Exile Coffin."

The entire labyrinth compressed. Six massive spatial walls formed around Ervin, closing in from above, from below, and from all four sides. Every wall contained countless folded planes leading away from the battlefield.

If they sealed completely, Ervin would suffer far worse than imprisonment. His very position would be exiled into the outer folds of Kaiden’s Pseudo Cosmic Path, and escape would be nearly impossible without breaking the labyrinth from within.
Ervin looked up, and his expression finally changed. It showed no fear and no panic. It showed complete seriousness.
"You are strong," he said.
Kaiden’s voice answered from everywhere within the labyrinth. "So are you."

Ervin closed his eyes briefly, and then the black sea behind him went utterly still. The broken gate ceased its trembling. The abyssal pressure no longer spread wildly, and instead it gathered inward, growing darker, deeper, and far more ancient.

The water of the black sea sank below the stage, yet its presence became more frightening rather than less, as though only the surface had disappeared while the true abyss awakened beneath everyone’s feet.
Ervin opened his eyes.
"I did not want to use this unless I had to."
Kaiden’s gaze sharpened. Ervin raised his spear with both hands.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."
The broken gate opened wider than it had against Selene, wider than it had against Rosaline, and wider than it had against Orion.
"Gate of the Second Depth."
Boom!

A pressure far beyond the previous gate erupted across the stage. The World Exile Coffin stopped closing, and its six spatial walls shook violently. The corridors of the Grand Void Labyrinth twisted downward while the mirrors cracked.
Even the folded paths grew heavy, as though the very concept of distance had been dragged into a deeper layer of abyssal origin.
Kaiden’s expression changed for the first time. "The Second Depth."
Ervin stepped forward, and the black spear in his hand seemed to merge with the gate at his back.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Second Depth Spear, Sunken World."

He thrust, but the spear did not fly toward Kaiden. It struck the Grand Void Labyrinth itself. For a moment, the entire Pseudo Cosmic Path went silent, and then the silver-gray labyrinth began to sink. Corridor after corridor collapsed downward while mirror after mirror shattered.
The folded planes lost their routes and tumbled into the invisible depth opened by the Second Depth Gate.
Kaiden immediately fought to stabilize his path with both hands.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Infinite Corridor Rotation."

The surviving corridors began spinning rapidly, working to scatter the abyssal pull across countless spatial layers. For a moment it worked, and the sinking slowed. Kaiden’s control was astonishing, and many experts could see that he was resisting Ervin’s full-strength abyss through pure spatial mastery alone.
But Ervin stepped forward again.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Second Depth Spear, Return Of The Sunken Path."

The spear moved a second time, and now the abyssal force followed the very routes Kaiden had created. It did not assault the labyrinth from outside. It entered the corridors themselves and dragged them down from within.
Kaiden’s face paled slightly as the Grand Void Labyrinth shuddered. He raised one hand and gathered every remaining spatial fold into a single point.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Final Corridor, Void Beyond Return."

A dark silver passage opened behind Ervin. This was no ordinary exile gate. It was the deepest corridor Kaiden could currently open, a path built to cast its target beyond the returning folds of the battlefield entirely.
If Ervin fell into it, even his Abyssal Origin Descent would need to burn enormous power just to find a way back.
The corridor opened beneath Ervin’s feet, and he sank halfway into it. The arena gasped.
Kaiden pressed both hands downward. "Go."
The Void Beyond Return swallowed Ervin’s lower body. But Ervin’s spear struck the edge of the corridor, and the broken gate behind him released a terrifying and soundless pull.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
The black sea rose up through the corridor, and the abyss invaded the Void Beyond Return itself. Kaiden’s eyes widened.

The exile corridor should have led away from the battlefield, away from the current spatial layer, and away from anything easily reached. But the abyssal origin cared nothing for ordinary direction. It treated all depth as something that could be dragged lower still.

The Void Beyond Return began sinking backward, and Ervin stepped out of it. His face was pale and blood ran from several wounds across his body, yet his eyes remained calm and deep. He had been pushed to the absolute edge.
Had he hesitated for even a single breath, Kaiden’s final corridor might have sealed him away long enough to decide the battle. But he had not hesitated, and he had spent everything.
Ervin raised his spear one final time.
"Second Depth Spear, Abyss Returns All Roads."

The spear descended, and the remains of the Grand Void Labyrinth collapsed. Silver-gray corridors shattered across the sky while the folded planes broke apart. The mirrors of space sank into darkness.
Kaiden tried to slip through one last fold, but the abyssal force traced the route and arrived before him in the same instant.
Ervin’s spear stopped at Kaiden’s throat, and the entire arena went silent.

Kaiden stood motionless with blood at the corner of his mouth, his silver-gray robes torn, and his aura flickering. His Grand Void Labyrinth had collapsed, yet his eyes stayed calm. There was no shame in them. There was only acceptance.
"You really hid that deeply," Kaiden said.
Ervin’s breathing came slightly heavy. "You forced me to."
Kaiden looked at the spear resting before his throat, and then he smiled faintly.
"Then I have no complaints."
He lowered his hands.
"I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Kaiden Voidmere Defeated.]
The screen above the arena updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Ervin]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 21]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Kaiden Voidmere]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 19]
The Divine Realm erupted. This time, no one dared claim that Kaiden’s loss to Max had made him look weak.

Against Ervin, he had unveiled his true power in the terrifying Grand Void Labyrinth, and he had pushed the Abyssal Origin Descent so far that Ervin was forced to open the Gate of the Second Depth and fight at full strength to win.
Kaiden had lost, but he had made one of the most mysterious geniuses of the final stage reveal a deeper layer of his Pseudo Cosmic Path.
On his pillar, Max gave Kaiden a faint nod. He had always known Kaiden was strong, and now everyone else knew it too.

Ervin returned to his pillar a moment later, his aura quieter than before yet visibly drained. The black spear in his hand still carried a trace of the Second Depth’s pressure, and several top geniuses regarded him with renewed caution.
Damian Voss narrowed his eyes slightly while Revona’s Void Origin Eyes flickered. Rakan Thorne grinned with open interest.
Orion Starfall laughed weakly from his pillar. "So he had another gate after all. How unfair."
Kaiden sat down quietly as the Eternal Hourglass healed his injuries. He had lost again, but this defeat carried an entirely different meaning. Against Max, he had been countered.
Against Ervin, he had truly fought to his limit, and because of that, his strength had finally been witnessed by the entire Divine Realm.

"Abyssal Origin Descent."
The broken gate opened wider than it had against Selene, wider than it had against Rosaline, and wider than it had against Orion.
"Gate of the Second Depth."
Boom!
A pressure far beyond the previous gate erupted across the stage.
The World Exile Coffin stopped closing, and its six spatial walls shook violently.
The corridors of the Grand Void Labyrinth twisted downward while the mirrors cracked.
Even the folded paths grew heavy, as though the very concept of distance had been dragged into a deeper layer of abyssal origin.
Kaiden’s expression changed for the first time.
"The Second Depth."
Ervin stepped forward, and the black spear in his hand seemed to merge with the gate at his back.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Second Depth Spear, Sunken World."
He thrust, but the spear did not fly toward Kaiden.
It struck the Grand Void Labyrinth itself.
For a moment, the entire Pseudo Cosmic Path went silent, and then the silver-gray labyrinth began to sink.
Corridor after corridor collapsed downward while mirror after mirror shattered.
The folded planes lost their routes and tumbled into the invisible depth opened by the Second Depth Gate.
Kaiden immediately fought to stabilize his path with both hands.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Infinite Corridor Rotation."
The surviving corridors began spinning rapidly, working to scatter the abyssal pull across countless spatial layers.
For a moment it worked, and the sinking slowed.
Kaiden’s control was astonishing, and many experts could see that he was resisting Ervin’s full-strength abyss through pure spatial mastery alone.
But Ervin stepped forward again.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Second Depth Spear, Return Of The Sunken Path."
The spear moved a second time, and now the abyssal force followed the very routes Kaiden had created.
It did not assault the labyrinth from outside.
It entered the corridors themselves and dragged them down from within.
Kaiden’s face paled slightly as the Grand Void Labyrinth shuddered.
He raised one hand and gathered every remaining spatial fold into a single point.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Final Corridor, Void Beyond Return."
A dark silver passage opened behind Ervin.
This was no ordinary exile gate.
It was the deepest corridor Kaiden could currently open, a path built to cast its target beyond the returning folds of the battlefield entirely.
If Ervin fell into it, even his Abyssal Origin Descent would need to burn enormous power just to find a way back.
The corridor opened beneath Ervin’s feet, and he sank halfway into it.
The arena gasped.
Kaiden pressed both hands downward.
"Go."
The Void Beyond Return swallowed Ervin’s lower body.
But Ervin’s spear struck the edge of the corridor, and the broken gate behind him released a terrifying and soundless pull.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
The black sea rose up through the corridor, and the abyss invaded the Void Beyond Return itself.
Kaiden’s eyes widened.
The exile corridor should have led away from the battlefield, away from the current spatial layer, and away from anything easily reached.
But the abyssal origin cared nothing for ordinary direction.
It treated all depth as something that could be dragged lower still.
The Void Beyond Return began sinking backward, and Ervin stepped out of it.
His face was pale and blood ran from several wounds across his body, yet his eyes remained calm and deep.
He had been pushed to the absolute edge.
Had he hesitated for even a single breath, Kaiden’s final corridor might have sealed him away long enough to decide the battle.
But he had not hesitated, and he had spent everything.
Ervin raised his spear one final time.
"Second Depth Spear, Abyss Returns All Roads."
The spear descended, and the remains of the Grand Void Labyrinth collapsed.
Silver-gray corridors shattered across the sky while the folded planes broke apart.
The mirrors of space sank into darkness.
Kaiden tried to slip through one last fold, but the abyssal force traced the route and arrived before him in the same instant.
Ervin’s spear stopped at Kaiden’s throat, and the entire arena went silent.
Kaiden stood motionless with blood at the corner of his mouth, his silver-gray robes torn, and his aura flickering.
His Grand Void Labyrinth had collapsed, yet his eyes stayed calm.
There was no shame in them.
There was only acceptance.
"You really hid that deeply," Kaiden said.
Ervin’s breathing came slightly heavy.
"You forced me to."
Kaiden looked at the spear resting before his throat, and then he smiled faintly.
"Then I have no complaints."
He lowered his hands.
"I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Kaiden Voidmere Defeated.]
The screen above the arena updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Ervin]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 21]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Kaiden Voidmere]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 19]
The Divine Realm erupted.
This time, no one dared claim that Kaiden’s loss to Max had made him look weak.

Against Ervin, he had unveiled his true power in the terrifying Grand Void Labyrinth, and he had pushed the Abyssal Origin Descent so far that Ervin was forced to open the Gate of the Second Depth and fight at full strength to win.
Kaiden had lost, but he had made one of the most mysterious geniuses of the final stage reveal a deeper layer of his Pseudo Cosmic Path.
On his pillar, Max gave Kaiden a faint nod.
He had always known Kaiden was strong, and now everyone else knew it too.
Ervin returned to his pillar a moment later, his aura quieter than before yet visibly drained.
The black spear in his hand still carried a trace of the Second Depth’s pressure, and several top geniuses regarded him with renewed caution.
Damian Voss narrowed his eyes slightly while Revona’s Void Origin Eyes flickered.
Rakan Thorne grinned with open interest.
Orion Starfall laughed weakly from his pillar.
"So he had another gate after all.
How unfair."
Kaiden sat down quietly as the Eternal Hourglass healed his injuries.
He had lost again, but this defeat carried an entirely different meaning.
Against Max, he had been countered.
Against Ervin, he had truly fought to his limit, and because of that, his strength had finally been witnessed by the entire Divine Realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 1884: Damian vs Rakan!
paragraphs: Angelina Valerius let the uproar from Ervin and Kaiden’s battle settle for a short while before she raised her hand once more, and the giant screen above the arena began to spin.

By now, the final competitive stage had moved far past the point where ordinary matches could satisfy the crowd. Too many shocking battles had already taken place. Max had defeated Rosaline, Rakan, Kaiden, Selene, and Aurelian.

Revona had ground Orion down to exhaustion and had later beaten Rakan as well. Ervin had just forced Kaiden to unveil the full terror of the Grand Void Labyrinth before defeating him with the Gate of the Second Depth.
The remaining battles grew heavier with each round, and every new pairing between major geniuses seemed capable of reshuffling the rankings at the top.
The first name slowed and appeared.
[Damian Voss]
A wave of noise rolled through the arena, and the second name soon followed.
[Rakan Thorne]

This time the noise swelled even louder, because another major battle had arrived. It was another clash between monsters, pitting the strongest genius of the Sword God Palace against the first Warlord of the War God Palace.
The crowd inside the Eternal Hourglass came alive at once, and across the Divine Realm, countless watching forces straightened before their viewing screens.
At the Black Dragon Clan, many disciples who had just been dissecting Ervin and Kaiden’s battle turned their full attention back to the large screen.
At the War God Palace, the disciples who had felt both proud and frustrated during Rakan’s earlier matches leaned forward again.
Although Rakan had already suffered defeats in the final stage, no one there had lost faith in his power. After all, the ones who had beaten him so far were monsters among monsters.
Now he was about to face Damian Voss.
Above the arena, Angelina’s voice rang out calmly.
"Damian Voss."
"Rakan Thorne."
"Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended, and Damian appeared first. He stood in flowing sword robes with his long hair drifting slightly behind him, his expression as calm and cold as ever.
The sword in his hand rested quietly, yet no one who had watched him fight could overlook the terrifying sharpness hidden inside that stillness.

Damian’s sword was not loud like Rakan’s fists, nor majestic like Rosaline’s dawn kingdom. It was not strange like Morgana’s curses, and it was not immeasurable like Revona’s void. Even so, everyone present understood that once he drew it in earnest, it became one of the deadliest things in the entire conference.

Rakan appeared opposite him. The first Warlord of the War God Palace still carried that fierce and open battle aura around him. His body seemed carved from battle itself, broad-shouldered and sturdy and terrifyingly solid.

Even after so many punishing fights, he still looked like the sort of man who would rather collapse after spending everything than retreat a single step early. He rolled his shoulders once, looked at Damian, and grinned.
"Well," Rakan said, "we finally get a proper rematch."
Damian regarded him calmly. "The first one ended too early."
Rakan laughed. "That is true. Back then the first round ended before we could go all out."
He clenched both fists, and the air around his knuckles began to tremble. "This time, no one is stopping us."
Damian’s sword tilted slightly downward. "This time," he replied, "I intend to finish it."
The moment those words fell, the atmosphere in the arena sharpened again. Even Max, standing on his pillar, narrowed his eyes slightly.
Rakan’s raw physical strength was terrifying, and the three broken limits of the War God Body had already placed him at the summit of body cultivators among the younger generation.
Against most opponents, that alone would have been enough to crush them outright. But Damian was not most opponents.
His sword had already brought down the Divine Son, one of the strongest geniuses of the elf race, and even top monsters like Orion and Kaiden treated him with caution.
Angelina raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Rakan moved first. He did not test, he did not circle, and he did not waste a single breath on a probing exchange.
"War God Body, First Limit."
Boom!

The first limit broke instantly. His body released a frightening pressure as the muscles across his arms and torso surged with explosive force. He took one step and the stage cracked beneath his feet. Then his fist shot forward.
"War God Fist, Mountain-Breaker Rush."
The punch came on like a charging fortress, carrying overwhelming body force and battle aura together.
Damian drew his sword.
"Falling River Cut."
A clean silver-white line appeared, and sword met fist.
Clang!

The shockwave exploded outward and swept across the arena in a ring of pressure. Rakan’s body did not retreat, and Damian’s sword did not bend. For a brief instant, the battlefield seemed caught between a mountain of flesh and a river of steel.
Then Rakan’s second fist came.
"War God Fist, Iron Heaven Smash."
Damian’s sword turned.
"Crosswind Return."

The blade redirected the strike rather than meeting it head-on, and Rakan’s punch slid past Damian’s left shoulder. In the same motion, Damian’s sword flashed upward toward Rakan’s ribs. Rakan twisted his body and caught the strike on his hardened forearm.
Sparks burst outward, and a thin line of blood appeared.
The crowd roared immediately, because Damian had drawn first blood.
Rakan only grinned wider. "Good!"
He stepped forward again and threw three punches in succession, each heavier than the last.
"War God Fist, Shattering Drum."
"War God Fist, Bonequake Burst."
"War God Fist, Heaven-Hammer Drive."
Every punch came from a different angle, and each carried enough physical force to break apart the protective barriers of peak geniuses.
Damian’s sword moved swiftly through the storm of fists, sometimes blocking and sometimes diverting, and sometimes slipping around an attack to strike at Rakan’s weak points.
For a while, neither man seemed willing to reveal his deepest cards. Even so, this early exchange already burned hotter than most battles of the final stage.
The Sword God Palace disciples watched with shining eyes, while the War God Palace disciples shouted Rakan’s name, especially when his fists managed to force Damian back half a step.

chapters.title: Chapter 1885: Tyrant Heaven Shatter!
paragraphs: But that half step only sharpened Damian’s gaze, and his sword style changed at once. Rather than continuing to meet Rakan’s ferocity head-on, his blade became cleaner, colder, and far more precise.
"Thousand Thread Severance."
The silver-white sword light split into countless narrow lines. Each line targeted a different part of Rakan’s movement, cutting at the wrist, the shoulder joint, the knee, the waist, and the ankle.
It was not a technique built to overpower strength. It was a sword art designed to sever rhythm, structure, and continuity within an opponent’s body.

Rakan’s face grew more serious. He crossed both arms before him and took the attack head-on, but the lines of sword light still bit into his skin one after another. Several shallow wounds opened at once, and more importantly, his next forward burst lost its perfect rhythm.
Damian stepped in.
"Silent Star Draw."
A vertical sword line fell straight toward Rakan’s chest.
Rakan roared. "War God Body, Second Limit."
Boom!

The second limit broke. His aura surged wildly and his body force climbed to a new height. The sword strike still landed, but this time Rakan met it with both palms pressed together and caught the descending blade between them.
Blood spilled from his hands, yet he forced the sword aside and drove his knee toward Damian’s abdomen.
Damian stepped back, though not entirely, and the knee passed within inches of him. Rakan pressed forward immediately.
"War God Fist, Battlefield Tyrant."

His whole body lunged behind the punch. This was no longer merely a fist technique. It was his full body weight, his second-limit War God Body, and the fury of a battle-crazed warlord compressed into one unstoppable blow.
Damian’s eyes narrowed.
"Sword Guard, White Horizon."
A broad silver-white arc opened in front of him.
Boom!

The Battlefield Tyrant crashed into the White Horizon. The sword guard trembled violently, and the stage beneath Damian’s feet cracked under the pressure. For a moment, it looked as though Rakan might truly blast through on brute force alone.
Then Damian’s right hand shifted. The White Horizon guard folded inward and became a slanted current.
"White Horizon, Turning Edge."

Rakan’s force was redirected to the side. His punch tore apart an entire section of the stage instead of Damian’s body, and before he could correct his posture, Damian’s sword slashed twice across his torso.
Blood sprayed, and the War God Palace disciples fell silent for a moment.
Rakan’s breathing grew heavier, but he refused to retreat. Instead, he laughed.
"Good. Very good."
His body released a terrifying red-gold battle aura.
"War God Body, Third Limit."

The instant the third limit broke, the entire arena trembled. This was the true peak of Rakan’s physical body. His muscles tightened like tempered divine metal, and veins of battle-red force ran across his skin.

The surrounding air seemed unable to bear the pressure radiating from his flesh. Compared to his first and second limits, the third was a complete leap, and it was the level that had earned him the title of first Warlord of the War God Palace.
Rakan bent slightly at the knees. Then he vanished.
The crowd gasped as he reappeared before Damian like a red-gold cannonball.
"War God Fist, Worldsplitter."
The punch exploded forward, and Damian blocked.
Clang!
For the first time, Damian was driven back several full steps. Before he could steady himself, Rakan was already on him again.
"War God Fist, Nine Battlefield Tremors."
Nine consecutive punches descended like falling war drums, and each strike landed heavier than the one before it.

Damian’s sword moved in a storm of silver-white brilliance as he blocked and redirected them one after another, yet even so, the pressure bearing down on him climbed sharply. On the ninth strike, the air burst apart and Damian slid backward across the stage.
The War God Palace erupted in cheers.
"That is it!"
"Senior Brother Rakan!"
"Crush him!"
Rakan lifted his chin with blood running from the cuts across his body, and his battle aura soared like wildfire.
"This is the body of the War God Palace," he said. "Can your sword cut through it?"
Damian looked at him quietly, and then he raised his sword again.
"It already has."

The words were calm, but in the next instant, his aura changed. The sky above the stage seemed to sharpen. The sword in his hand grew brighter, purer, and colder than before. The surrounding sword intent did not explode wildly.
It condensed instead, until it felt as though every strand of sharpness in the world had gathered around Damian’s blade.
Max watched carefully, and he understood at once that Damian had stopped merely fighting. Now he was beginning to cut in earnest.
Damian took one step forward.
"Sword Path, Seven Line Clear Severance."
One slash came, and then another, and then a third. He did not attack with overwhelming visual force. He attacked with terrifying precision.

Each sword line cut into the exact flow of Rakan’s body force, landing where his joints transferred power, where his muscles chained explosive force together, and where the rhythm of his War God Body surged between its limits.

Rakan met him head-on. He punched through the first line, broke the second with his elbow, and destroyed the third with a downward smash. But the fourth line cut across his thigh while the fifth slashed his shoulder.
The sixth severed the rhythm of his next forward charge, and the seventh landed across his chest and drew a deep line of blood.
Rakan staggered, though only once. Then he roared and gathered everything he had into a final charge.
"War God Body, Three Limits Unified."
His red-gold battle aura compressed fully around him.
"War God Palace Secret Art, Tyrant Heaven Shatter."

This was Rakan’s strongest attack, and it was far more than a fist or a burst of body force. It was the complete union of his three broken limits, his battle will, and the entire ferocity of the War God Palace’s body-cultivating path.
When he launched the punch, it felt as though a whole battlefield of war spirits charged behind it.
The Divine Realm held its breath, and even the top geniuses on the pillars watched without blinking.
Damian looked at the incoming Tyrant Heaven Shatter, and at last his sword path truly rose.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."

A vast sword heaven appeared behind him. Countless ancient swords floated in silence above a silver-white firmament, and at the very center stood one enormous sword shadow that seemed to rule over all the rest.
Unlike loud and crushing domains, Damian’s Pseudo Cosmic Path was frightening because of its purity. It carried no waste, no unnecessary flourish, and no unstable violence.
It was the kind of path that sent an instinctive chill through every swordsman watching, because it looked like a path created for the sole purpose of proving that the sword stood above all.
