It was the kind of path that sent an instinctive chill through every swordsman watching, because it looked like a path created for the sole purpose of proving that the sword stood above all.

chapters.title: Chapter 1886: Damian Wins!
paragraphs: "Sword Sovereign Heaven."
The name alone made the arena feel colder. Rakan’s eyes widened, but he did not stop.
Damian’s voice stayed calm.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, First Edict."
The enormous sovereign sword behind him trembled.
"All force beneath the sword shall be judged."

Then Damian slashed. The silver-white sword line descended and met Tyrant Heaven Shatter head-on, and for a moment the two attacks held. Rakan roared and poured every ounce of power from his three broken limits into the punch.
The battlefield spirits behind him shook wildly as they strained to push through the sovereign sword line.

Then Damian’s sword brightened, and the Sword Sovereign Heaven pressed down. The War God Palace’s secret art cracked, the battlefield spirits split apart, and Tyrant Heaven Shatter broke. The silver-white line continued forward and struck Rakan directly.
Boom!

Rakan was blasted backward across the stage. His huge body crashed and rolled, carving a long trench into the arena floor before finally coming to rest near the very edge of the battlefield. Blood ran from his mouth and chest while the battle aura around him flickered violently.
The three broken limits of his War God Body began collapsing one after another.
The War God Palace disciples fell silent.

Rakan forced himself to rise. He planted one knee into the shattered stage and pushed himself halfway up while breathing heavily. His fists still trembled with unwillingness, and the red-gold aura around him struggled to flare one last time.
Damian appeared before him, and his sword stopped at Rakan’s throat. The entire arena went silent.
Rakan looked at the blade, and then up at Damian. For a few breaths he said nothing. Then, slowly, he laughed. The sound was hoarse and pained, yet entirely sincere.
"So this is the sword of the Sword God Palace."
Damian’s expression remained calm.
Rakan shook his head lightly. "I gave it all."
"I know," Damian replied.
Rakan exhaled slowly. The unwillingness drained from his eyes and was replaced by the clear acceptance of a warrior who had lost only after emptying himself completely.
"Then I lose."
Angelina Valerius announced the result at once.
"Winner, Damian Voss."
The giant screen above the arena changed.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Damian Voss]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 22]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rakan Thorne]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 19]

The Divine Realm erupted once more. Damian Voss remained undefeated. Rakan Thorne had given everything, drawing on all three broken limits of the War God Body and even the War God Palace’s secret art, and Damian’s sword had still cut him down in the end.
At the Sword God Palace, countless disciples cheered with pride blazing across their faces. At the War God Palace, the disciples were disappointed, yet not one of them looked ashamed of Rakan.
Their first Warlord had not lost through weakness. He had lost after fighting at his absolute peak against one of the strongest swordsmen the Divine Realm had produced in generations.

Saint Reiner, still hidden in the shadows of the War God Palace, watched in silence. A faint glint crossed his eyes before he murmured to himself, "Damian is indeed terrifying, but the one I truly want to watch is still that boy."

On the pillars of the Eternal Hourglass, the other top geniuses watched quietly, and Max’s eyes lingered on Damian a moment longer than the rest. That sword was truly dangerous, and dangerous in a way that demanded respect.
Rakan had been anything but weak. Among the body cultivators of the younger generation, he stood absolutely among the very best. Yet Damian had cut through all of it and won cleanly in the end.
The battle had ended, but the pressure gathering at the top of the rankings had only grown heavier.
Rakan returned to his pillar with his wounds still knitting under the laws of the Eternal Hourglass, though his eyes stayed bright. He had lost, yet no one could claim he had fallen cheaply.
He had opened all three limits of the War God Body, unleashed the War God Palace’s secret art, and driven his body to its edge before Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven finally cut through him.
It was a defeat, but it was equally proof of why Rakan Thorne was called the first Warlord.
Damian returned to his pillar in silence. His sword had been sheathed again, his expression calm and his aura restrained. Yet after that battle, everyone sensed his danger even more keenly.
He had remained undefeated through every match, and each time someone forced him to reveal a little more, his sword grew more frightening.
The Sword God Palace disciples across the Divine Realm were still cheering, while many great forces had fallen into solemn discussion about just how far his Sword Sovereign Heaven could truly reach.

Angelina Valerius waited until the stage restored itself. The shattered ground mended, the sword marks faded, and the bloodstains vanished beneath the golden flow of the Eternal Hourglass laws. Then she raised one hand again.
"The next battle will now be selected."

The giant screen above the arena began spinning, and the names of the remaining participants flashed rapidly through the air. At this point, nearly every battle among the top names carried real importance.
Some participants had already lost their chance to reach the very summit, but pride, ranking, and future reputation still hung in the balance.
A victory over a major genius could reshape how the entire Divine Realm regarded them, while a crushing defeat could damage even an ancient faction’s prestige.
The light slowed, and one name appeared.
[Orion]
The arena stirred immediately.
Orion was still seated on his pillar, recovering from his previous brutal battles.

He had lost to Revona after forcing her to use Return To Nothing, and then lost to Ervin after pressing the Abyssal Origin Descent hard enough to make the broken gate open wider. His record was no longer perfect, yet no one dared underestimate him.
If anything, his defeats had painted his reputation in sharper colors.
Orion was not someone who lost through weakness. He was someone who lost only after burning everything he had against monsters of the highest tier.
Across the Divine Realm, the Nine Star Court disciples snapped to attention at once.
"Senior Brother Orion again!"
"Who is his opponent?"
"He has already fought Revona and Ervin. Please do not let it be another terrible matchup."
"He still has the Nine Star Sovereign Body. Even injured, he can fight anyone."
On his pillar, Orion looked up at his own name and sighed with a helpless smile. "Again? The Eternal Hourglass really refuses to let me rest."
Rakan, still recovering nearby, laughed. "Maybe it likes watching you suffer."
Orion turned his head and smiled at him. "Coming from someone who just got cut down by Damian, that sounds strangely comforting."
Rakan grinned. "At least I lost after punching everything I could reach."
Orion shrugged lightly. "Then I shall try to punch something bright this time, depending on who appears."
As though answering his words, the second name slowed. The spinning light passed over Max Morgan, then over Damian Voss, then over Revona, and then over Ervin. Then it stopped.

chapters.title: Chapter 1887: Orion vs Divine Son!
paragraphs: [Aurelian Lareth]
The moment the name appeared, the arena dropped into a sudden and sharp silence. Then the giant screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Orion Starfall vs Aurelian Lareth]
The atmosphere changed instantly, because this was no casual match. It was a battle between the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court and the Divine Son of the second elven faction.

Orion Starfall, whose Nine Star Sovereign Body had shaken the arena and whose self-created Starfall Extinction had forced even Revona to reveal one of her deepest moves, would now face Aurelian Lareth, the proud Divine Son who carried the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion and had already fought Damian, Rakan, Rosaline, and Max.
Both of them had suffered major defeats. Both of them still carried terrifying strength. And both of them needed this battle for entirely different reasons.

Orion needed to prove that even after losing to Revona and Ervin, he still belonged among the absolute peak. His body was not fully recovered, his star power had been drained again and again, and his strongest technique had been used repeatedly in battles where ordinary geniuses would have collapsed long before.
Yet the more he fought, the clearer one truth became. Orion’s brilliance had never come from an easy path. It came from his willingness to keep shining even while wounded.
Aurelian needed something entirely different. He needed restoration.
After losing to Damian, his pride had been damaged. After losing to Max, something far deeper than pride had been shaken.

The entire Divine Realm had watched his Heavenly Luminance attacks fail to harm Max, and although most people did not know the hidden truth behind that scene, everyone understood that something strange and humiliating had taken place.
The Divine Son of the second elven faction had returned to his pillar in silence, and since then he had not spoken a single unnecessary word.

Now he had been matched against Orion. For the second elven faction, this was a chance to recover some face. For the Nine Star Court, it was a chance to prove that their strongest genius could still challenge the highest tier even after terrible matchups and repeated exhaustion.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the top geniuses reacted one after another.
Rakan crossed his arms as his grin returned. "This should be good. Orion’s stars against that fellow’s divine light."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly. "A battle between two people who desperately need a win. That usually turns ugly."
Kaiden Voidmere looked thoughtful. "Orion’s Nine Star Sovereign Body will let him close the distance, but Aurelian’s long-range suppression is difficult to cross if he controls the field early."
Ervin’s gaze stayed deep. "Orion is not at full strength."
Revona opened her eyes slightly. "But his will is not weak."

Damian Voss looked between the two names without speaking. He had defeated Aurelian himself, and he had also witnessed Orion’s Starfall Extinction. His silence made the coming battle feel heavier still, because everyone knew Damian never wasted attention on fights that lacked meaning.

Max stood on his pillar calmly, and his gaze rested on Aurelian for a brief moment. The Divine Son’s expression was cold, but the arrogance he once wore had changed. Something in him had quieted after the battle with Max.

It was not humility, and it was not peace. It was a tightened, suppressed, dangerous kind of silence. He looked like a man trying to hold a cracked throne together with both hands while pretending no one could see the fractures.
Then Max looked toward Orion, who was smiling again. He was pale, injured, and exhausted, and he was smiling all the same.

Max’s eyes turned slightly thoughtful. Orion had been pushed hard throughout the final stage. He had fought Revona, Ervin, and many other dangerous opponents, yet his spirit had never dimmed. Even in defeat he carried no shame.
What he carried was hunger. He wanted to discover how far his stars could go, and every loss only seemed to sharpen his determination to refine them.
Outside, the Divine Realm boiled with discussion.
"The Nine Star Sovereign Body against the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."
"Can Orion break through Aurelian’s long-range light suppression?"
"He forced Revona to use Return To Nothing, but he has already burned through too much."
"Aurelian lost terribly to Max, but he is still the Divine Son. Against anyone else, his Heavenly Luminance Dominion remains terrifying."
"If Orion uses Starfall Extinction again, can Aurelian block it?"
"Or will Aurelian suppress him before he can gather enough star force?"

At the Nine Star Court, the elders watched with solemn faces. They understood Orion’s current condition better than anyone. His body had been repaired by the Eternal Hourglass, but repair did not mean he had returned to his absolute peak.

The Nine Star Sovereign Body was powerful, yet it placed terrifying demands on his foundation. Starfall Extinction was worse still, being self-created, incomplete, and dangerous to use repeatedly. Orion’s will could carry him far, but no amount of will could erase every cost.

At the viewing halls of the second elven faction, the atmosphere had turned deathly cold. Aurelian had to win. No one spoke those words aloud, yet everyone understood them. He had already lost to Damian, and he had lost even more humiliatingly to Max.

If he fell to Orion as well, especially while the Divine Realm still questioned the authority of his Heavenly Luminance power, the Divine Son’s prestige would suffer another heavy blow. Even though Orion ranked among the strongest geniuses present, a defeat at this point would remain dangerous for Aurelian’s standing.

Inside the arena, Orion slowly rose to his feet. His body still looked a little unsteady, but his smile stayed bright. He looked toward Aurelian’s pillar and said, "Divine Son, I hope you are not too angry today. Angry opponents are troublesome."
Aurelian looked down at him with cold golden eyes. "You should worry about yourself."
Orion chuckled. "I have been doing that since Revona nearly erased me and Ervin nearly drowned my stars. It has not helped much."
Aurelian’s expression did not move. "Then this battle will end quickly."
Orion’s smile widened slightly, though his eyes turned sharper. "That is what everyone says before it becomes difficult."
The tension between them thickened.
Angelina Valerius looked at both participants. Her silver-white robe stirred faintly as the laws of the Eternal Hourglass gathered around the central stage once more.

The arena had already finished repairing itself after Damian and Rakan’s battle, yet now, as Orion and Aurelian prepared to step forward, the barrier brightened more than usual. It was as though the Eternal Hourglass itself anticipated another large-scale collision.
Above the stage, the announcement still shone.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Orion Starfall vs Aurelian Lareth]

Orion Starfall lifted his head as faint starlight began gathering around his body. Aurelian Lareth stood opposite him in the distance, and golden-white radiance rose slowly behind his figure like a sacred sun.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
"Orion Starfall."
"Aurelian Lareth."
"Enter the stage."

chapters.title: Chapter 1888: A Good Match!
paragraphs: The battle began the moment Orion Starfall and Aurelian Lareth landed on the central stage. There was no casual greeting this time, and there was no slow testing.
The instant Angelina Valerius’s hand lowered and the words appeared above the arena, both of them unleashed their power without a moment’s hesitation.
[Battle Begins.]
Orion’s smile remained on his face, but the starry light in his eyes turned sharp enough to make the air tremble.

He knew his body was not in perfect condition. He had already fought Revona to the edge and used Starfall Extinction against her, and then he had pushed himself against Ervin and lost after forcing the abyssal gate to open deeper.

The laws of the Eternal Hourglass had repaired his injuries, but some exhaustion could not be erased so easily. His foundation was still strained, his meridians still carried the echo of overdrawn star power, and his flesh still remembered the burden of converging the nine stars into himself again and again.
But he did not care.
Aurelian Lareth stood opposite him with a face colder than before. After losing to Max, the arrogance around him had hardened into something more dangerous.

He no longer looked like a proud prince waiting for others to kneel. He looked like a man whose throne had been cracked in front of the entire Divine Realm, and who now intended to bury the next opponent beneath enough light to make everyone forget that humiliation.
Golden-white radiance erupted behind him first.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."

Aurelian opened his Pseudo Cosmic Path directly. Sacred halls rose behind him, and radiant pillars pierced the sky. A golden throne manifested beneath an endless sun, and the entire stage was swallowed in divine light before Orion had even taken his first step.
The pressure that descended ran far stronger than the openings he had used in most of his earlier battles. Aurelian had no intention of preserving strength, and he had no intention of showing mercy.
After Max had made his Heavenly Luminance power look useless, he needed to prove that against everyone else, the Divine Son’s light remained terrifying.
Orion’s smile widened slightly. "Straight to the dominion. Good. I was afraid you might still be in a bad mood."
Aurelian’s eyes turned icy. "You talk too much."
Orion lifted one hand, and nine ancient stars appeared behind him. "Then I will fight more."
The nine stars descended at once.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Nine Star Sovereign Body."
Boom!

The stars entered Orion’s flesh, his bones, his blood, his spine, his heart, his arms, his legs, and his soul foundation. His aura erupted upward and pushed against the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion with radiant celestial force.
Behind him a vast star palace appeared, cracked from previous burdens yet still majestic, surrounded by nine immense stars that turned like crowns of heaven.
The Divine Realm roared.
"They both opened Pseudo Cosmic Paths immediately!"
"Aurelian is not holding back after his loss to Max!"
"Orion is injured, but he still activated the Nine Star Sovereign Body from the start!"
"This will be brutal!"
Aurelian raised one hand.
"Divine Dominion, Twelve Pillars of Sacred Judgment."

Twelve radiant pillars appeared around Orion and fired golden-white beams from every direction. Each beam carried the authority of a Pseudo Cosmic Path, and each one sought to purify the star power inside Orion’s body before it could fully circulate.
Orion vanished.
"Second Star Step."
His body slid through starlight and crossed the first beam by a hair’s width. Then he twisted his torso, gathered burning star force into his fist, and punched the second beam directly.
"First Star Fist."
Boom!
The beam shattered. A third beam struck toward his back, but Orion’s body spun in midair as the sixth star entered his shoulder.
"Sixth Star Pressure Crash."

His shoulder slammed into the beam and crushed it apart with dead-star heaviness. Aurelian’s eyes narrowed slightly, and the twelve pillars adjusted their angles at once. The beams no longer fired at random. They locked onto Orion’s movement rhythm, trying to seal off every possible path before he could shift again.
Orion laughed softly. "Not bad."
The third star entered his elbow.
"Third Star Elbow, Meteor Break."
His elbow fell like a plunging meteor and smashed through the nearest radiant pillar. The fourth star entered his leg next, and he kicked through another pillar with a crescent arc of starlight.
"Fourth Star Crescent Kick."

Two pillars shattered, but Aurelian’s dominion rebuilt them instantly. Golden-white light poured down from the endless sun, repairing the broken pillars and strengthening the divine kingdom. Aurelian’s expression stayed cold as his hand pressed downward.
"Divine Dominion, Luminance Decree."

A golden-white decree unfolded above Orion. Sacred words descended and targeted his body, his star circulation, and the rhythm of his Nine Star Sovereign Body. The moment the words touched him, Orion felt the star power in his limbs grow heavier. The decree was straining to suppress the connection between the nine stars and his flesh.
His smile faded slightly. "Annoying."
Aurelian’s voice was cold. "Fall."
The decree brightened. Orion’s knees bent under the pressure, and the radiant pillars around him fired again.
Rakan Thorne frowned from his pillar. "That decree is restricting his star changes."
Kaiden Voidmere nodded slightly. "Aurelian is not giving him the chance to build rhythm."
Ervin watched calmly. "Orion’s body is still not at full strength."
Revona’s eyes stayed fixed on the stage. "But his will has not weakened."
On the stage, Orion drew a deep breath. The ninth star entered his spine, and his entire body straightened beneath the decree.
"Ninth Star Crown Stabilization."

The star palace behind him trembled, and a crown of starlight appeared faintly above his head. The sacred words pressing down on him began cracking one after another. Orion clenched his right fist and poured three stars into his arm at once.
"Three-Star Heaven Breaker."
He punched upward, and the punch tore straight through the Luminance Decree.
Crack!
The decree split apart, and Orion rushed through the falling fragments of sacred light. His speed climbed again, and in a single breath he arrived before Aurelian.
"Five-Star Revolving Impact."

His fist, his elbow, his knee, his shoulder, and his palm struck one after another, and each carried a different star force. Aurelian formed a golden-white mirror with one hand and a sacred spear with the other.
"Divine Dominion, Sacred Mirror Guard."
"Heavenly Luminance, Royal Sun Spear."
The mirror blocked Orion’s fist while the spear thrust toward his chest. Orion shifted the second star into his waist, twisted around the spear, and drove his knee into the mirror.
"Fifth Star Knee, Falling Orbit."
Boom!
The mirror shattered, and Aurelian retreated half a step. That half step made the Nine Star Court disciples erupt.
"He pushed him back!"
"Senior Brother Orion!"
"Break the dominion!"

Aurelian’s face darkened. After his loss to Max, being forced back by another opponent felt like a second blade scraping across his pride. His crown blazed brighter, and the golden throne behind him released a more oppressive radiance.
"Divine Dominion, Royal Mandate of the Endless Sun."

The endless sun poured golden-white light into Aurelian’s body. His aura surged, and the dominion pressed outward in every direction. Orion’s star palace trembled beneath the pressure, and the nine stars around it flickered slightly.
Aurelian raised both hands.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Sacred Sun Spearfall."

chapters.title: Chapter 1889: Orion’s Grit and WIll!
paragraphs: Hundreds of massive golden-white spears formed above the stage, and then they descended.

Orion looked up. The sky was gone, and only the divine spears remained. He grinned again, but this time blood had already appeared at the corner of his mouth. The pressure of the dominion was forcing his injuries to reopen, and every time he changed stars too quickly, his body screamed in protest.
Still, he stepped forward.
"Seven-Star Revolving Body."

Seven stars lit up inside him at once, and he moved into the falling spearfield. The first spear grazed his shoulder, the second pierced through the starlight around his arm, and the third tore open a wound on his thigh.

Yet Orion kept moving. He punched one spear apart, kicked another aside, broke a third with his elbow, and smashed through the fourth with his shoulder. Starlight burst from his body over and over, and each time he should have slowed, he forced another star to rotate into position.
Aurelian’s eyes grew colder. "Still moving?"
Orion laughed through the blood. "Unfortunately for you, yes."
He jumped. The second star pushed his speed beyond its previous limit, and the sixth star added crushing weight to his descent.
"Second Star Step."
"Sixth Star Falling Heaven Strike."
Orion dropped toward Aurelian like a collapsing star. Aurelian raised his palm.
"Crownless Divine King."

The golden throne shattered, and its fragments flowed into his body as the dominion condensed instantly. The sacred halls vanished, the radiant pillars shrank, and the endless sun became a blazing crown behind him. Aurelian’s aura turned sharper and more unstable as all the dominion’s authority merged into his flesh.
He pointed upward.
"Crownless Divine King, Light That Judges All Stars."
A beam of condensed golden-white judgment shot toward Orion. Orion did not dodge. The ninth star entered his fist.
"Ninth Star Crown Fist."
His fist collided with the judgment beam.
Boom!

The explosion swallowed the center of the stage. Orion was thrown backward with blood spraying from his arm, but the judgment beam shattered as well. Aurelian stepped through the explosion, his speed far greater in the Crownless Divine King state.
"Radiant Execution Step."
He appeared before Orion and thrust with a spear of condensed light.
"Crownless Divine King, Sun-Piercing Verdict."

The spear drove toward Orion’s chest. Orion twisted aside, but his accumulated injuries left him half a breath too slow. The spear tore through the armor near his ribs and left a deep, bleeding wound. Aurelian followed with another attack at once.
"Crownless Divine King, Solar Execution Array."
Dozens of golden-white blades formed around Orion and slashed toward him from every angle.
Orion’s face finally turned serious.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Full Star Rotation."

All nine stars rotated through his body at terrifying speed, and he moved as though a star were being torn through nine different orbits at once. His fists broke the front blades, his knees shattered the lower ones, and his elbows destroyed the blades at his sides.
His shoulders smashed through two that came from behind. Even so, some still landed. Blood scattered across the stage, and Orion’s breathing grew heavier.
Aurelian pressed harder. He gave Orion no time to rest, and he gave him no room to speak. He attacked like a man trying to erase all memory of his own earlier humiliation.
"Crownless Divine King, Final Luminance Judgment."

The enormous divine sword of golden-white light formed above the stage, and the spectators went silent. This attack had failed against Damian, and it had shattered uselessly against Max. But against Orion, it remained terrifying.

The divine sword descended, carrying the concentrated authority of Aurelian’s dominion, his bloodline power, and his Crownless Divine King state. The pressure was so heavy that even Orion’s star palace groaned beneath it.
Orion looked up. His body was wounded, his star power was strained, and his previous battles had taken too much from him. Yet his eyes were still bright.
He laughed softly. "Good."
The nine stars inside his body began to gather, and the Nine Star Court elders watching from afar shot to their feet.
"He cannot use that again."
"His body will not hold."
"Orion, do not force it."

But Orion could not hear them, and perhaps he would not have listened even if he could. He had fought Revona, and he had fought Ervin. He had been beaten down again and again by people whose paths were every bit as terrifying as his own.
Yet he had never accepted that his stars should stop shining simply because an opponent was stronger, stranger, or better rested.
He clenched his fist, and the nine stars collapsed inward.
"Starfall Extinction."
The entire arena trembled.

This Starfall Extinction was different from the ones he had used against Revona and Ervin. It did not have the same fullness he could produce at his peak, and it did not have the same stable foundation.

It was rough, bloody, and dangerous to himself. Yet it carried something sharper than before. It carried will. Every star inside his body burned as though Orion were forcing them to shine even while cracked.
He rushed upward, and Starfall Extinction met Final Luminance Judgment.
Boom!

The collision split the stage in half. Golden-white divine light and collapsing star essence erupted together. Aurelian pressed both hands downward and poured more power into the divine sword, while Orion roared and drove his fist upward, the star essence layers within Starfall Extinction detonating one after another.

The first layer broke the outer divine light. The second layer cracked the judgment runes. The third layer forced the divine sword to tremble. The fourth layer shattered Orion’s own arm armor, and the fifth layer tore blood from his shoulder. But he did not stop.
Aurelian’s expression changed. "How are you still pushing?"
Orion looked up through the raging light, his teeth stained with blood and his smile fierce and bright. "Because I am not done."
The sixth layer of Starfall Extinction erupted.
Crack!
Final Luminance Judgment split. The seventh layer followed, and the divine sword shattered.
Aurelian’s pupils contracted. Orion broke through the falling fragments of golden-white light and appeared before him, his fist still carrying the last remnant of collapsing star power.
Aurelian tried to retreat.
"Radiant Ascension Step."
Orion’s left hand shot out and seized the edge of Aurelian’s radiant robe before he could fully escape. "Not this time."
The eighth star entered Orion’s other fist.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Eighth Star Collapse Fist."
The punch landed on Aurelian’s chest.
Boom!

Aurelian was blasted backward with golden-white blood spilling from his mouth. His Crownless Divine King state trembled violently, but he still did not fall. He raised both hands, his eyes filled with fury and disbelief.
"Divine Dominion, Solar Execution Array."
The golden-white blades formed again. Orion staggered and nearly dropped to one knee. Then he stood.
Aurelian’s face twisted. "Why do you refuse to fall?"
Orion breathed heavily, and then he smiled. "Because I already lost enough today."
He stepped forward as the nine stars behind him flickered. Not all of them were stable anymore, but they still answered him.
"Because if I keep losing without taking one back, my master will laugh at me."

He stepped again, and the Solar Execution Array descended. Orion rushed straight into it. Blades cut his arms, light tore across his shoulder, and one radiant blade sliced across his side. But he kept moving.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Final Orbit Break."

His body became a streak of unstable starlight, weaving through the execution array while taking every wound he could not avoid. The second star gave him speed, the fourth star changed his angle, and the sixth star added pressure. The ninth star stabilized his core just enough to keep him from collapsing.
Then he appeared before Aurelian again.
Aurelian’s eyes widened.

chapters.title: Chapter 1890: Orion Wins!
paragraphs: Orion raised his fist. There was almost no star power left in him, so he gathered every last trace of it into a single point.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Last Star Fist."

The fist struck Aurelian’s chest, and this time Aurelian’s remaining dominion broke. The burning crown behind him shattered, the Crownless Divine King state collapsed completely, and the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion scattered into broken golden-white fragments.
Aurelian flew backward and crashed into the ground, carving a long trench across the stage before coming to rest near the edge.

Orion landed on one knee. His right arm trembled, and blood dripped from his chin. His aura flickered so weakly that many spectators wondered whether he would faint before the announcement could even arrive.
Aurelian tried to stand. His hand pressed against the cracked ground, and golden-white light flickered around him, but it shattered almost instantly.
He forced one knee beneath himself, only for his body to tremble and drop back down. His eyes were filled with humiliation, rage, and disbelief.
He had lost again. This time it had not been to Damian’s sword, and it had not been to Max’s strange immunity and hidden bloodline truth.
He had lost to Orion Starfall, a wounded opponent who had already been drained by earlier battles and still refused to fall until the very end.
Angelina Valerius looked down at the stage. "Aurelian Lareth is unable to continue."
The screen above the arena changed.
[Winner: Orion Starfall.]
[Aurelian Lareth Defeated.]

For a moment, the Divine Realm was silent. Then the Nine Star Court erupted. Their disciples shouted so loudly that even the viewing formations trembled, and the elders who had been tense throughout the battle finally released long breaths.
Orion had not won cleanly, and he had not won easily. He had won while wounded, exhausted, bleeding, and nearly collapsing under the burden of his own technique. But he had won.
The screen updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Orion Starfall]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 20]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Aurelian Lareth]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 19]
On the stage, Orion slowly pushed himself up. He swayed once, then steadied himself with a laugh.
"That was... harder than I wanted."
Rakan Thorne burst into laughter from his pillar. "You look half-dead."
Orion turned his head slightly and smiled weakly. "Only half. That means I can still brag."
Even Damian Voss’s eyes softened slightly as he looked at Orion. Revona watched in silence, though there was respect in her gaze. Ervin studied Orion a moment longer than usual as well.

He had defeated Orion before, but after witnessing this battle, he understood even more clearly that Orion Starfall’s greatest strength was not only his Nine Star Sovereign Body or his Starfall Extinction. It was the simple fact that he never truly stopped fighting.
Max stood on his pillar and looked at Orion with a faint smile.

Aurelian, by contrast, was carried back to his pillar by the transfer light in silence. The Divine Son’s face was pale and his aura unstable, and for the third time in this final stage, his pride had been broken in front of the entire Divine Realm.

The final competitive stage continued, but after this battle everyone understood one thing clearly. Orion Starfall might have lost before, and he might have been wounded and exhausted, yet as long as a single star inside him still burned, he remained dangerous enough to defeat even the Divine Son.

After Orion defeated Aurelian, the entire final competitive stage seemed to settle into a strange silence. It was not the silence of boredom. It was the silence that followed too many shocking results overturning expectation after expectation.

The Divine Son of the second elven faction had now suffered yet another defeat. Damian Voss had cut through his Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion. Max Morgan had made his light-based attacks look meaningless.
Now Orion Starfall, wounded and exhausted from his previous battles, had still forced his way through the full pressure of the Divine Son’s dominion and won through sheer refusal to fall.

Aurelian returned to his pillar in silence. His pale golden hair hung slightly across his face, and the golden-white radiance around his body flickered weakly as the laws of the Eternal Hourglass healed his injuries.

Yet no law could mend the damage done to his pride. His expression stayed cold, but that coldness had turned brittle. It no longer felt like the calm arrogance of a Divine Son who believed the world should kneel. It felt like the frozen surface of a lake concealing cracks beneath.

Orion, on the other hand, returned to his pillar and sat down at once with a tired laugh. His aura was unstable, his breathing was heavy, and several traces of golden-white light still clung to the wounds across his body.
Even so, his smile stayed bright. The Nine Star Court disciples across the Divine Realm were still cheering, and many who had watched him lose twice before now regarded him with renewed respect.
Orion Starfall had proven that his earlier defeats had never been proof of weakness. He had simply been fighting monsters from the very beginning.
Rakan Thorne looked at him from a nearby pillar and laughed loudly. "You really do not know when to stay down."
Orion leaned back slightly and waved a weak hand. "It was a fun battle."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly. "You say that after kneeling on it for half the battle?"
Orion glanced at her and sighed. "Witches should be more merciful to injured men."
Morgana’s smile deepened. "Injured men should stop pretending they are heroic when they are half-dead."
Even a few tense participants could not help reacting to that exchange, but the light atmosphere lasted only a moment.

Everyone knew the final stage had not ended. The strongest names still had to finish their remaining battles, and some of the most important pairings had yet to appear. Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Revona, Ervin, and Kaiden Voidmere all still hung over the arena like mountains.

Angelina Valerius waited for the stage to finish restoring itself. The cracks left by Orion’s Last Star Fist closed, the burned marks from Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion faded, and the final traces of star essence dissolved into the golden laws of the Eternal Hourglass. Then she raised her hand again.
"The next battle will now be selected."

The giant screen above the arena began to spin, and the atmosphere tightened immediately. Names flashed across the screen, among them Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Revona, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Rakan Thorne, Orion Starfall, Morgana Starveil, Rosaline Lunara, Selene Vaeloria, and Aurelian Lareth.

Each passing name carried its own weight, but by now the audience had grown especially sensitive to the top-tier pairings. Whenever the names of two monsters appeared close together, the whole Divine Realm held its breath.
The first name slowed, and then it stopped.
[Revona]

The fist struck Aurelian’s chest, and this time Aurelian’s remaining dominion broke.
The burning crown behind him shattered, the Crownless Divine King state collapsed completely, and the Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion scattered into broken golden-white fragments.
Aurelian flew backward and crashed into the ground, carving a long trench across the stage before coming to rest near the edge.
Orion landed on one knee.

chapters.title: Chapter 1891: Revona vs Kaiden!
paragraphs: The arena went quiet at once. Revona opened her eyes on her pillar. Her face remained calm and pale, and the Void Origin Eyes carried their usual unfathomable stillness. She had already proven herself one of the strongest geniuses of the final stage.

She had defeated Orion after being pushed to the edge by Starfall Extinction, and she had defeated Rakan by adapting her Void Origin Realm against his terrifying War God Body. She had erased, nullified, hollowed, and returned attacks to nothing again and again, until even the top geniuses treated her with caution.
Her strength did not come from loud displays. It came from the terrifying certainty that no attack was guaranteed to matter once it entered the range of her eyes.
Across the Divine Realm, many spectators leaned forward.
"Revona again."
"Who will she fight this time?"
"She is still undefeated, right?"
"Yes. She defeated Orion and Rakan. Her Void Origin Eyes are simply monstrous."
"Only Max, Damian, Ervin, and Kaiden might truly pressure her now."
As though answering that thought, the second name began to slow. The light passed over Damian Voss, then over Ervin, and then over Max Morgan. Then it stopped.
[Kaiden Voidmere]
For a breath, the entire arena fell silent. Then the giant screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Revona vs Kaiden Voidmere]

A strange pressure descended over the Eternal Hourglass. This was not a battle of brute strength, and it was not a clash of light and star power. It was a confrontation between two of the most mysterious spatial and void-based geniuses in the entire conference. On one side stood Revona, the owner of the Void Origin Eyes.

On the other stood Kaiden Voidmere, the supreme genius of the Grand Void Sanctum. One of them could nullify, erase, and return power to nothing. The other could fold space, create endless corridors, exile attacks beyond return, and trap opponents inside the Grand Void Labyrinth.

The very nature of the battle felt difficult to predict. Would Revona’s Void Origin Eyes erase Kaiden’s spatial folds before they formed? Would Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth split the battlefield into too many layers for her eyes to fully control?
Could the Void Origin Realm drag spatial attacks into nothingness before they reached her, or could Kaiden use exile routes and folded corridors to avoid being caught by her nullification entirely?
The Divine Realm erupted into discussion.
"This might be one of the strangest battles so far."
"Void Origin Eyes against the Grand Void Labyrinth."
"Revona can erase attacks, but Kaiden’s attacks do not always come from the same space."
"If Kaiden splits the battlefield into layered corridors, can her eyes erase all of them at once?"
"But if Revona opens the Void Origin Realm, even spatial layers might be dragged toward nothingness."
"Do not forget that Kaiden pushed Ervin to reveal the Gate of the Second Depth."
"And Revona defeated Orion and Rakan. She is not someone who can be handled with ordinary space tricks."
At the Grand Void Sanctum’s viewing platform, the disciples who had been disappointed after Kaiden’s loss to Ervin grew focused once more.
Kaiden had lost to Max because Max was nearly the worst possible opponent for him, a man who possessed deeper mastery of the Void Genesis Art and a body that could ignore most spatial attacks.

Against Ervin, however, Kaiden had revealed his true power. His Grand Void Labyrinth had driven the Abyssal Origin Descent to its edge and forced Ervin to open the Gate of the Second Depth. No one who had watched that battle could still treat Kaiden as inferior.
Now he would face Revona, and the elders of the Grand Void Sanctum looked solemn.
"Her eyes are dangerous."
"They do not merely defend. They erase the foundation of techniques."
"Kaiden must not let her see the complete structure of the labyrinth too early."
"Layered attacks. Delayed corridors. False routes. He must keep the battlefield changing."
Elsewhere in the Divine Realm, those connected to Revona watched with equal seriousness. Kaiden was not Rakan, whose strength could be dulled through careful nullification and rhythm disruption.
He was not Orion, whose star power could be erased when the timing was right. Kaiden’s power flowed through folded space, hidden layers, shifted positions, delayed routes, and exile corridors.
If Revona misjudged even one layer, an attack could appear from behind her, beneath her, or out of a space that had not existed a breath earlier.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the top geniuses grew serious as well.
Rakan Thorne crossed his arms and grinned. "I hate both of their fighting styles."
Orion, still recovering, laughed weakly. "That is because neither of them is polite enough to stand still and get punched."
Rakan snorted. "Exactly. Very disrespectful."

Morgana Starveil looked at the names with interest. "This one might be decided by perception. If Revona reads the labyrinth fast enough, Kaiden will suffer. If Kaiden hides the true route of his attacks well enough, Revona will be forced to defend blindly."
Ervin watched Kaiden quietly. "His Grand Void Labyrinth is difficult to break. Even the Abyssal Origin Descent had to go deeper."
Damian Voss said nothing, but his eyes stayed fixed on the screen.

Max watched with interest as well. He understood Kaiden’s path better than most after their battle. Kaiden’s weakness against him had made that result look one-sided, but that weakness would not exist against Revona. Here, Kaiden could fully wield space as a weapon, a battlefield, a prison, and an escape route all at once.

At the same time, Max had seen Revona’s Void Origin Eyes bypass the very logic that should have protected other techniques. Her power was not ordinary defense. It came closer to denying the existence of an attack before it could fully become meaningful. This battle would not be simple.

On her pillar, Revona slowly stood. Her long hair drifted gently behind her, and her eyes remained calm, almost empty. She did not look excited, and she did not look nervous. Yet the void-like stillness around her deepened, and the space near her body seemed to grow quieter, as though even movement hesitated near her gaze.

Kaiden Voidmere stood as well, and silver-gray ripples spread from beneath his feet. His expression was composed, but his eyes carried the seriousness of a man with no intention of underestimating his opponent.

After battling Max and Ervin, his prestige had not fallen. If anything, people now understood how unfortunate his matchups had been. Against Revona, he had a chance to show a different side of his strength.
Kaiden looked toward Revona and spoke calmly. "Your eyes are famous."
Revona looked back at him. "Your labyrinth is troublesome."
A faint smile touched Kaiden’s face. "Then this should be meaningful."
Revona’s eyes flickered slightly. "Yes."
The brief exchange was calm, yet the tension beneath it was enough to silence even the loudest spectators.

Angelina Valerius looked toward the two of them. The laws of the Eternal Hourglass gathered around the stage, and the barrier brightened again. It was as though the arena itself was bracing for a battle that might not damage the stage in the usual way, but could twist, erase, fold, and hollow the space within it beyond recognition.
Above the stage, the announcement still shone.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Revona vs Kaiden Voidmere]
Angelina raised her hand.
"Revona."
"Kaiden Voidmere."
"Enter the stage."

chapters.title: Chapter 1892: Injuring Revona!
paragraphs: The two beams of light descended at the same time.

Revona appeared on one side of the central stage, her posture quiet and her eyes calm. There was no grand pressure around her, no violent aura, and no obvious sign that she had already defeated monsters like Orion Starfall and Rakan Thorne.

Yet the stillness surrounding her carried a danger that made many spectators instinctively hold their breath. Her Void Origin Eyes were open, pale and unfathomable, as though every attack that entered her sight had already begun to vanish.
Kaiden Voidmere appeared opposite her. Silver-gray ripples spread beneath his feet, and the space around him folded softly, almost respectfully.

Compared to the calm he had shown against weaker opponents, his expression now was far more focused. After battling Max and Ervin, he had already suffered two defeats, yet neither had broken his confidence.

Against Max, he had been countered by a deeper mastery of the same path and a body almost immune to spatial attacks. Against Ervin, he had pushed the Abyssal Origin Descent all the way to the Gate of the Second Depth before losing.
Now he faced Revona, a different kind of monster entirely.
The entire Divine Realm watched closely.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Kaiden moved first.
"Void Genesis Art, Empty Step."

His body vanished from the stage without a ripple. Revona’s eyes shifted slightly, and a faint void light appeared in her pupils. Kaiden reappeared behind her with one palm already descending toward the space near her shoulder.
"Void Genesis Art, Space Burial Palm."

The space around Revona sank instantly, as if an invisible tomb had opened around her body. The attack did not need to strike her flesh directly. It sought to bury her position in folded space, compressing the battlefield around her until movement became impossible.

Revona turned her head slightly, and the Void Origin Eyes brightened. The sinking space trembled, and then the buried region began to hollow out. Kaiden’s palm fell through emptiness. Revona stepped sideways, and the Space Burial Palm vanished, as though the foundation of the technique had been erased before it could close completely.
Kaiden did not look surprised.
"Void Genesis Art, Sevenfold Severing Line."

Seven invisible spatial cuts appeared around Revona at once. They came from different angles, different distances, and slightly delayed spatial layers. Against most opponents, even perceiving one line would already be difficult, and perceiving all seven at once was nearly impossible.

But Revona’s eyes moved. One line vanished, then another, and then a third. The first three spatial cuts were erased before they reached her. The fourth and fifth dimmed and lost most of their cutting force.
The sixth was diverted by a hollow ripple around her body. Only the seventh slipped through her range at the last moment and grazed her sleeve, drawing a thin line of blood across her forearm.
The arena stirred.
"He injured her."
"Only a shallow wound, but he still reached her."
"Kaiden’s attacks come from too many layers. Even Revona cannot erase everything instantly."
Revona looked at the blood on her arm, and then back at Kaiden. "Good."
Kaiden’s eyes sharpened slightly. "I will take that as praise."
The space beneath him opened into multiple corridors.
"Void Genesis Art, Nine Hollow Routes."

Nine silver-gray paths appeared across the stage, each bending through a different spatial layer. Kaiden’s figure appeared at the end of all nine paths at once. Some were true projections, some were delayed positions, and some were future routes that had not fully formed. To ordinary eyes, it was impossible to tell which path carried the real attack.
Revona stood still as her Void Origin Eyes scanned the battlefield.
Kaiden attacked.
"Grand Void Sanctum, Hollow Route Palm."
Nine palms descended from nine positions. Revona erased four, and two more collapsed under void ripples. But three reached her defensive range at the same time.
She raised her hand.
"Void Origin Palm."
A hollow palm seal spread outward and weakened the three incoming attacks, but Kaiden’s true body slipped through the weakest route and appeared directly before her.
"Void Genesis Art, Origin Fold Strike."

His palm struck toward her chest. Revona’s eyes narrowed. The attack began to disappear, but it did not vanish fully. Kaiden had hidden the real strike inside a folded route, so her eyes erased the outer technique first while the inner force continued forward. The palm struck her shoulder and pushed her back several steps.
The crowd gasped. Revona had retreated.
Kaiden stood where he was with silver-gray light around his hand. Revona’s shoulder trembled faintly, yet her expression stayed calm.
"You hide your attack well."
Kaiden replied, "Your eyes force me to."

The moment his words ended, the atmosphere changed. Kaiden raised both hands, and silver-gray light expanded behind him as the battlefield began splitting into countless folded planes. Corridors appeared in the air. Mirrors of space opened and closed.
The sky seemed to bend into several layers while the ground stretched and shrank at the same time. Every direction became unreliable.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."
The silver-gray void expanded fully.
"Grand Void Labyrinth."
Boom!

The entire stage transformed. Revona stood at the center of a labyrinth built from folded space, hidden passages, mirror routes, exile corridors, and delayed attack points. Every wall was also a doorway, every doorway was also a blade, and every blade could become a prison.
The Grand Void Labyrinth did not try to overwhelm an enemy with one massive attack. It turned the whole battlefield into a trap where an opponent could never be sure where the danger truly came from.
Kaiden’s voice echoed from every direction.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Corridor of Ten Thousand Cuts."
The spatial corridors opened, and invisible cuts poured toward Revona from every layer. Her Void Origin Eyes shone, and cut after cut vanished.
But the Ten Thousand Cuts did not all arrive together. Some came now, some came a breath later, and some appeared behind her only after being reflected through three folded corridors.

Some moved toward her, vanished, and reappeared beneath her feet. Revona erased dozens of them, and then hundreds, yet several still slipped through. Blood appeared on her shoulder, another wound opened near her waist, and a thin cut appeared across her cheek.

Revona looked at the blood on her arm, and then back at Kaiden.
"Good."
Kaiden’s eyes sharpened slightly.
"I will take that as praise."
The space beneath him opened into multiple corridors.
"Void Genesis Art, Nine Hollow Routes."
Nine silver-gray paths appeared across the stage, each bending through a different spatial layer.
Kaiden’s figure appeared at the end of all nine paths at once.
Some were true projections, some were delayed positions, and some were future routes that had not fully formed.
To ordinary eyes, it was impossible to tell which path carried the real attack.
Revona stood still as her Void Origin Eyes scanned the battlefield.
Kaiden attacked.
"Grand Void Sanctum, Hollow Route Palm."
Nine palms descended from nine positions.
Revona erased four, and two more collapsed under void ripples.
But three reached her defensive range at the same time.
She raised her hand.
"Void Origin Palm."
A hollow palm seal spread outward and weakened the three incoming attacks, but Kaiden’s true body slipped through the weakest route and appeared directly before her.
"Void Genesis Art, Origin Fold Strike."
His palm struck toward her chest.
Revona’s eyes narrowed.
The attack began to disappear, but it did not vanish fully.
Kaiden had hidden the real strike inside a folded route, so her eyes erased the outer technique first while the inner force continued forward.
The palm struck her shoulder and pushed her back several steps.
The crowd gasped.
Revona had retreated.
Kaiden stood where he was with silver-gray light around his hand.
Revona’s shoulder trembled faintly, yet her expression stayed calm.
"You hide your attack well."
Kaiden replied, "Your eyes force me to."
The moment his words ended, the atmosphere changed.
Kaiden raised both hands, and silver-gray light expanded behind him as the battlefield began splitting into countless folded planes.
Corridors appeared in the air.
Mirrors of space opened and closed.
The sky seemed to bend into several layers while the ground stretched and shrank at the same time.
Every direction became unreliable.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."
The silver-gray void expanded fully.
"Grand Void Labyrinth."
Boom!
The entire stage transformed.
Revona stood at the center of a labyrinth built from folded space, hidden passages, mirror routes, exile corridors, and delayed attack points.
Every wall was also a doorway, every doorway was also a blade, and every blade could become a prison.
The Grand Void Labyrinth did not try to overwhelm an enemy with one massive attack.
It turned the whole battlefield into a trap where an opponent could never be sure where the danger truly came from.
Kaiden’s voice echoed from every direction.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Corridor of Ten Thousand Cuts."
The spatial corridors opened, and invisible cuts poured toward Revona from every layer.
Her Void Origin Eyes shone, and cut after cut vanished.
But the Ten Thousand Cuts did not all arrive together.
Some came now, some came a breath later, and some appeared behind her only after being reflected through three folded corridors.
Some moved toward her, vanished, and reappeared beneath her feet.
Revona erased dozens of them, and then hundreds, yet several still slipped through.
Blood appeared on her shoulder, another wound opened near her waist, and a thin cut appeared across her cheek.

chapters.title: Chapter 1893: Kaiden’s Terrifying attack!
paragraphs: The arena erupted in shock.
"Kaiden is pushing her back!"
"The Grand Void Labyrinth is too difficult to read!"
"Even Void Origin Eyes cannot erase every attack if the structure keeps changing!"
On the pillars, the top geniuses watched seriously.
Rakan Thorne grinned, though tension lived in his eyes. "I still hate this kind of fight."
Orion Starfall smiled weakly. "Because you cannot punch a corridor that is not there yet?"
Rakan snorted. "Exactly."
Damian Voss looked at the battlefield with narrowed eyes. "Kaiden is forcing her to divide her perception."
Ervin nodded faintly. "If she reads one layer, he attacks from another."

Max watched quietly. He had fought Kaiden himself and knew how dangerous the Grand Void Labyrinth became when the opponent could not ignore spatial attacks. Against him, Kaiden’s path had been suppressed by a cruel mismatch.

Against Revona, the labyrinth finally revealed its true terror. Revona could erase attacks, but she still needed to perceive the foundation of what she erased, and Kaiden kept shifting that foundation before her eyes could fully lock onto it.
On the stage, Revona raised one hand.
"Void Origin Realm."
The world behind her became hollow. There was no sky, no ground, no sound, and no color. There was only origin-level emptiness.

The moment the Void Origin Realm appeared, the Grand Void Labyrinth trembled. Several spatial corridors lost their edges and faded into nothingness. Mirror routes dimmed, and delayed attack points collapsed before releasing their stored force.
Kaiden’s expression grew serious.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Infinite Corridor Rotation."

The labyrinth began rotating. Every corridor changed position, every wall became a different path, and every exile point moved away from Revona’s gaze before her Void Origin Realm could fully hollow it. The clash turned terrifyingly strange. Revona’s emptiness erased routes while Kaiden’s labyrinth created new ones faster than ordinary minds could follow.
Revona stepped forward.
"Void Origin Realm, Hollowing Wave."
A silent wave spread from her, and the nearest corridors vanished. Kaiden appeared far above her through a mirror path.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Exile Palm."

His palm descended. The space around Revona’s left side disappeared for a breath. Her balance shifted, and three spatial cuts came from her blind angle. Revona turned her eyes sharply. Two cuts vanished, but the third landed, and blood splashed from her arm.
Kaiden pressed harder.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Mirror Burial."

Dozens of mirrored spaces appeared around Revona, each one reflecting her from a different angle. Then the mirrors collapsed inward, trying to bury her real position among false layers and seal her inside a distorted spatial grave.

Revona’s Void Origin Realm expanded. The first mirrors dissolved, then the second layer, and then the third. But Kaiden’s attack held five hidden layers. The fourth layer collapsed around her and forced her body half a step into folded space. The fifth layer appeared behind her as a silver-gray blade.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Backflow Severance."

The blade struck toward her back. Revona’s eyes widened slightly, and for the first time she moved quickly. Her body turned, and the Void Origin Eyes erased half the blade, but the remaining force still cut across her shoulder. Blood stained her clothes, and the impact drove her several steps forward.
A rare silence fell over the arena. Revona had been wounded several times. Kaiden had truly pushed her.
The Grand Void Sanctum disciples shouted loudly.
"Senior Brother Kaiden!"
"Suppress her!"
"Break the Void Origin Eyes!"
Kaiden did not celebrate. His breathing had grown heavier. Maintaining the Grand Void Labyrinth while constantly changing routes to escape Revona’s erasure consumed enormous energy.
He had wounded her repeatedly, but every failed corridor was erased completely, and each route lost to the Void Origin Realm could not be restored easily.
Revona stood at the center of the labyrinth with blood flowing from several wounds, yet her expression had not changed. She looked at Kaiden.
"Your labyrinth is dangerous."
Kaiden replied calmly, "Your eyes are worse."
Revona raised her head slightly. "Then I should look more carefully."

The moment she spoke, the Void Origin Eyes changed. They grew deeper. The pale emptiness in her pupils no longer merely erased what came toward her. It began to trace the routes behind the attacks, following each spatial cut back through the folded corridors, mirror layers, and hidden paths that had created it.
Kaiden’s expression shifted slightly.
Revona lifted one hand.
"Void Origin Eyes, Trace To Nothing."

A spatial cut flew toward her. She did not erase only the cut. Her eyes followed its route backward and hollowed the corridor that had produced it, and the corridor vanished. Another attack came from below. Revona’s gaze shifted, the attack disappeared, and the folded plane beneath it collapsed into nothingness.
Kaiden immediately changed tactics.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Thousand False Roads."

Thousands of narrow corridors appeared at once, spreading in every direction like a silver-gray web. Only a few held real attacks. The rest were false routes meant to overwhelm Revona’s perception and make her waste power erasing empty paths.
Revona stood still, and her eyes slowly turned.
"Void Origin Realm, Silent Eye Field."
The hollow world behind her expanded into the labyrinth itself, and a strange silence spread. The false roads began disappearing on their own, not all at once, but steadily.

One by one, the corridors that held no true force faded under the pressure of origin emptiness, while the real routes grew clearer because they carried Kaiden’s intent. For the first time, the endless complexity of the Grand Void Labyrinth began to thin.
Kaiden’s face turned pale.
"She is adapting," Morgana Starveil murmured from her pillar.
Damian Voss nodded slightly. "That is what makes her dangerous."
Ervin’s gaze deepened. "Kaiden pushed her to the edge, but now she has begun reading the labyrinth."
Max watched with clear focus. Revona had not won because Kaiden was weaker. She was learning the battlefield while wounded, and that was terrifying in its own way.

Kaiden raised his hands again, knowing he could not delay any further. The Grand Void Labyrinth condensed. Every remaining corridor, mirror, wall, and exile point began gathering into one enormous silver-gray passage behind Revona. Its edges were dark, unstable, and frighteningly deep.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Final Corridor."
The passage opened completely.
"Void Beyond Return."

The deepest exile path Kaiden could currently create appeared beneath Revona’s feet. The moment it opened, the space around her body vanished downward, and Revona began to sink. Her Void Origin Realm pressed against it, but the Final Corridor was no ordinary attack.
It was an exile route built from the deepest layers of Kaiden’s Pseudo Cosmic Path, and it did not try to cut, crush, or pierce her. It tried to remove her from the battlefield entirely.
The spectators held their breath. Revona’s lower body sank into the corridor, then her waist, and then her chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 1894: Last few battles!
paragraphs: Kaiden pressed both hands downward as blood appeared at the corner of his mouth from the strain. "Go."
The Final Corridor pulled harder, and for a moment it looked as though Revona would truly be exiled. Then her eyes shone with a terrifying emptiness.
"Void Origin Realm."
Her voice was calm.
"Return To Nothing."
The hollow world behind her condensed into a single point, and that point appeared inside the Final Corridor itself.

Kaiden’s eyes widened. The Final Corridor did not shatter immediately. Instead, it began losing meaning. Its direction faded, its destination vanished, and its exile authority hollowed out from within. The path that was supposed to lead beyond return no longer had a place to return from, nor a place to send her to.
The corridor trembled violently. Revona stopped sinking. Then she stepped out. Her face was pale and blood flowed down her arm, but her gaze remained steady.
Kaiden tried to shift away. Revona looked at him.
"Trace To Nothing."

The corridor beneath Kaiden’s feet vanished, and his escape route disappeared. He tried to open another, but Revona’s eyes followed the intent and erased the new route before it could form. Kaiden’s pupils contracted. For the first time in the battle, he had nowhere to move.
Revona raised her hand, and a hollow ripple spread from her palm.
"Void Origin Realm, Hollow Return."

The ripple crossed the remaining distance and struck Kaiden’s chest. It did not explode, and it did not blast him away with force. It erased the spatial support around his body, hollowed the foundation of the Grand Void Labyrinth, and returned the last stable route beneath him to nothingness.
Kaiden’s Pseudo Cosmic Path trembled once, and then it collapsed.
The silver-gray labyrinth shattered. Corridors broke apart, mirrors faded, and exile points vanished. The stage returned to normal.

Kaiden stood in front of Revona with his aura unstable and his silver-gray robes torn. He tried to raise his hand one more time, but no corridor answered him quickly enough. Revona’s hand stopped before his chest, and the emptiness around her palm made the air between them disappear.
The entire arena fell silent.
Kaiden looked at her hand, and then at her eyes. After several breaths, he smiled faintly.
"You learned the labyrinth faster than I hoped."
Revona’s voice was quiet. "You almost exiled me."
"Almost is not victory."
"No."
Kaiden lowered his hand. "I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Revona.]
[Kaiden Voidmere Defeated.]
The screen above the arena updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 21]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Kaiden Voidmere]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 19]

The Divine Realm erupted. Kaiden Voidmere had lost again, but no one dared call him weak. He had pushed Revona closer to danger than almost anyone besides Orion. His Grand Void Labyrinth had wounded her, disrupted her Void Origin Eyes, and nearly sealed her inside the Void Beyond Return.

For a long stretch of the battle, it had truly looked as though Kaiden might hand Revona her first defeat. But Revona had adapted. She had traced his hidden routes, hollowed his false paths, survived the deepest exile corridor, and finally erased the foundation of the Grand Void Labyrinth itself.
On the pillars, Orion Starfall laughed softly despite his exhaustion. "That woman is unreasonably strong."
Rakan Thorne snorted. "Both of them are unreasonable."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly. "The difference is that Revona becomes more dangerous the longer she watches you."
Ervin nodded slightly. "That is why she won."

Max watched Revona quietly. Her aura was clearly weaker than before, and the wounds across her body proved how close the fight had become, yet her eyes remained calm. Kaiden had almost pushed her to her limit, but he had not crossed it.

The transfer light descended and returned both fighters to their pillars. Revona sat down after arriving, her pale face showing the cost of victory. Kaiden also sat quietly, his expression calm despite the defeat.
The battle had ended. Revona remained undefeated, and the final competitive stage moved one step closer to its true climax.

After Revona defeated Kaiden Voidmere, the atmosphere of the final competitive stage grew even more complicated. Kaiden had lost, yet the way people looked at him had changed once again. Against Max, his spatial path had been suppressed before it could reveal its full danger.

Against Ervin, he had forced the Abyssal Origin Descent into the Gate of the Second Depth. Against Revona, he had pushed one of the strongest undefeated geniuses in the entire conference close to the edge, cutting through her defenses, forcing her to adapt, and nearly sending her into the Void Beyond Return.
He had lost in the end, but the Divine Realm now understood clearly that Kaiden Voidmere could not be judged by his record alone.
Revona returned to her pillar with her aura unstable and her face paler than before. The laws of the Eternal Hourglass began repairing her wounds, but everyone could see that the battle had cost her.

Her Void Origin Eyes remained calm, yet a faint exhaustion hid in their depths. She had defeated Orion, Rakan, and now Kaiden. Each victory had been real, and each one had proven her strength. But each had also drained her, and the final competitive stage still had not ended.
Angelina Valerius waited only until the stage restored itself before continuing, and the battles that followed moved faster.

Several lesser participants were matched against the top geniuses and were quickly defeated. Most of them no longer tried to force a miracle. By this point, everyone had seen enough to recognize when a gap was impossible to cross.

A spear genius from a hidden sect surrendered to Damian after three exchanges once his spear intent was cut apart before it could fully form. A beast-blooded warrior tried to challenge Max with raw strength, only to be stopped by one palm and pushed outside the fighting zone without Max using any special ability.

Morgana Starveil defeated a flame cultivator by placing a curse on his spiritual fire, and Rosaline Lunara used the Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary to suppress a poison-path genius and forced him to surrender before his poison mist could spread across the stage.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Winner: Morgana Starveil.]
[Winner: Rosaline Lunara.]
The screen kept updating. The battle counts were approaching the end, and the pressure at the top grew sharper with every result.
Then another important match appeared.
[Ervin vs Fin Arclight]

Fin entered the stage with his Pale Eclipse Burial already stirring around him. He had lost several important matches, yet his strength remained dangerous. The moment the battle began, he opened the Pale Eclipse Field and tried to bury Ervin’s senses beneath moonless darkness. The pale eclipse spread in silence, dimming the stage until even the light of the Eternal Hourglass seemed to lose its warmth.
But Ervin’s response was direct. He summoned the Abyssal Origin Descent before the eclipse could fully close, and the black sea rose beneath the moonless field.

Fin’s eclipse was built to bury perception, sever rhythm, and suppress an enemy inside pale darkness, but Ervin’s abyss did not need ordinary sight. The moment the broken gate appeared, the Pale Eclipse Field began sinking from below.

Fin used "Pale Eclipse Burial, Moonless Descent," trying to crush Ervin before the gate opened wider, but Ervin answered with "Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth," and the moonless blade sank into the black sea.

Fin fought fiercely and changed angles again and again, yet his strongest eclipse power could not escape the pull of the abyss. In the end, Ervin’s spear stopped before his chest, and Fin surrendered with a grim expression.

Fin fought fiercely and changed angles again and again, yet his strongest eclipse power could not escape the pull of the abyss.
In the end, Ervin’s spear stopped before his chest, and Fin surrendered with a grim expression.

After that came another matchup that drew attention.
[Rakan Thorne vs Morgana Starveil]
Morgana’s Star-Curse Labyrinth opened immediately, filling the arena with violet-black mirrors, starry curse threads, and witch symbols that tried to twist Rakan’s movement.

Against ordinary close-combat fighters, this would have been a nightmare, since every step forward would trigger another curse and every punch would be redirected or weakened by star-bound witchcraft.

But Rakan had already suffered too many losses against the top monsters, and his mood was clearly terrible. He opened the First Limit, then the Second Limit, and charged straight through the curse field.

Morgana tried to slow him with "Star-Curse Labyrinth, Witch Mirror Binding," then followed with "Nameless Star Misfortune," but Rakan’s War God Body burned so violently that he broke through the curse layers by brute force.
When Morgana finally tried to deepen the labyrinth, Rakan opened the Third Limit and crushed three curse mirrors with one punch.
Morgana clicked her tongue and surrendered before he could close the distance completely.
[Winner: Rakan Thorne.]
[Morgana Starveil Defeated.]
Rakan returned to his pillar with a grin, though the curse marks on his arms were still fading.
"You witches are annoying," he said.
Morgana smiled faintly despite her loss. "And you body cultivators are far too stubborn to be elegant."
Rakan laughed. "Good. Elegance does not break bones."
The next notable match came soon after.
[Revona vs Rosaline Lunara]

Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary unfolded with beautiful brilliance, filling the arena with rose-gold light, falling petals, radiant palaces, and sovereign seals. She did not hold back. She knew Revona’s Void Origin Eyes were dangerous, so she did not rely on one large attack.

Instead, she used layered suppression, spreading "Dawn Edict, First Seal," "Dawn Edict, Second Seal," and "Dawn Edict, Third Seal" across different points of the battlefield while using the sanctuary itself to rebuild whatever Revona erased.

For a short time, it worked. Revona erased one seal, and Rosaline created two more. Revona hollowed the petal chains, and the sanctuary formed new bindings from another direction. Rosaline had learned from her earlier defeats, and this time she did not try to overpower Revona with one decisive strike.
She tried to drown her in repeated sovereign control instead.
But Revona’s eyes stayed too calm. She allowed Rosaline to build the sanctuary wider, then opened the Void Origin Realm and erased the foundation of the sealing structure one layer at a time.

When Rosaline used "Final Dawn Edict, Sovereign Rose Spear," Revona did not clash with it directly. She used "Void Origin Realm, Return To Nothing" in a far smaller form than the one she had used against Orion, hollowing the spear’s authority before it could fully pierce her defense.
Rosaline’s face turned pale, but she smiled bitterly and lowered her hands. "I surrender."
[Winner: Revona.]
[Rosaline Lunara Defeated.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 21]

The undefeated records still belonged to only a few people. Max Morgan, Damian Voss, and Revona stood among them. Every time those names appeared on the ranking projection, the arena felt the same pressure.

Everyone knew the final stretch would eventually force some of them to collide. The round-robin stage allowed no hiding. There were no brackets to avoid a bad matchup, no luck to carry someone around an opponent, and no excuse once the names were called.
Then another powerful battle appeared.
[Orion Starfall vs Morgana Starveil]

Orion was still recovering from his battle with Aurelian, and Morgana tried to take advantage of that at once. She opened the Star-Curse Labyrinth and used curse threads to slow the circulation of Orion’s star power.
For several exchanges, Orion’s movement was restricted, and his Nine Star Sovereign Body flickered under the pressure of the curses.

But Orion had already fought too many strange paths to be caught so easily now. He smiled, opened the Second Star Step, shifted his star rhythm three times in a single breath, and broke the curse pattern by constantly changing which star powered which part of his body.

Morgana’s eyes narrowed when she realized he was using his own unstable condition as a weapon, making his star rhythm difficult to predict because even he was forcing it to move beyond its normal limit.

In the end, Orion used "Nine Star Sovereign Body, Seven-Star Revolving Impact" to break three layers of the labyrinth, then forced Morgana to surrender with "Ninth Star Crown Fist." He did not use Starfall Extinction, and everyone could tell he was preserving what little recovery he had left.
[Winner: Orion Starfall.]
[Morgana Starveil Defeated.]
The next battle moved quickly as well.
[Max Morgan vs Fin Arclight]

Fin’s expression turned extremely ugly the moment he saw Max’s name beside his own. Still, he entered the stage and opened Pale Eclipse Burial directly. Pale darkness swallowed the arena, and the Moonless Descent blade formed above Max’s head with enough force to threaten most top geniuses.
Max did not draw Dragonheart, and he did not use the Emotion Severing Path. He simply raised one hand, and a seven-colored lightning glow flickered faintly around his fingers.

The destructive pressure of Divine King Punishment did not fully descend, yet even that faint trace was enough to make Fin’s pale eclipse tremble. Max flicked his finger, and the Moonless Descent blade shattered before it could fall.
Fin stared at him for one breath. Then he surrendered.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Fin Arclight Defeated.]
No one mocked Fin for it. At this stage, surrendering before Max when the gap was so obvious was not cowardice. It was survival.
The records continued rising.

By now, the entire Divine Realm could feel that the final stage was approaching its climax. The easy battles had nearly disappeared. The ranking table had begun settling into a terrifying shape, though the top positions still depended on the remaining collisions among the strongest.

Max, Damian, Ervin and Revona remained undefeated. Kaiden had suffered more losses because his matchups were brutal, yet every battle he fought proved that his true strength still belonged among the highest tier.
Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand once again, and the giant screen above the arena began spinning. This time, the atmosphere grew tense even before the first name appeared.
The light slowed, and the first name stopped.
[Damian Voss]
The Sword God Palace disciples immediately went silent with expectation.
The second name continued rotating. It passed over Max Morgan, then over Revona, and then over Ervin. Then it slowed and stopped.
[Kaiden Voidmere]
For a breath, the Eternal Hourglass became completely still. Then the screen enlarged both names.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Damian Voss vs Kaiden Voidmere]

A wave of excitement spread through the Divine Realm. Damian Voss, the undefeated sword sovereign of the Sword God Palace, would face Kaiden Voidmere, the supreme genius of the Grand Void Sanctum whose Grand Void Labyrinth had pushed both Ervin and Revona to reveal deeper strength.
This was another clash of two terrifying paths, sword against space, with Sword Sovereign Heaven set against the Grand Void Labyrinth. One path could cut through force, law, rhythm, and authority.
The other could fold the battlefield, create endless corridors, exile positions, and make distance itself meaningless.
On his pillar, Kaiden slowly opened his eyes. Damian Voss looked toward him calmly. Neither spoke at first, and the entire Divine Realm leaned closer to the screens.
Angelina Valerius looked at both of them and announced the next battle.
"Damian Voss."
"Kaiden Voidmere."
"Enter the stage."
