chapters.title: Chapter 1896: Damian vs Kaiden!
paragraphs: Two beams of light descended from above the arena.

Damian Voss appeared on one side of the central stage with his sword resting quietly at his waist. His expression was still calm, almost too calm, as though the battle before him was not one of the most important matches left in the final competitive stage.

Yet everyone who had watched him fight already knew that Damian’s calmness was more frightening than most people’s rage. His sword did not need loud pressure to make others cautious. The moment he stood there, the air around the stage seemed to grow thinner and sharper.

Kaiden Voidmere appeared opposite him. Silver-gray ripples spread beneath his feet, folding and unfolding the space around him in quiet waves. He had already suffered defeats against Max, Ervin, and Revona, yet those losses had not damaged his reputation. Instead, they had revealed just how terrible his matchups had been.
Against Max, his space power had been countered by someone with deeper mastery and almost natural immunity to spatial attacks.
Against Ervin, he had forced the Abyssal Origin Descent into the Gate of the Second Depth.
Against Revona, he had almost exiled one of the strongest undefeated geniuses into the Void Beyond Return before she adapted and turned the battle around.
Now he stood before Damian Voss. It was sword against space, Sword Sovereign Heaven against the Grand Void Labyrinth.
The Divine Realm held its breath.
Kaiden looked at Damian and spoke first. "I have been waiting for this battle."
Damian replied calmly, "You can say the same for me."
Kaiden’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Then this battle will depend on whether your sword can cut through my space."
Damian’s hand rested on the hilt of his sword. "We will see."
Kaiden’s silver-gray aura deepened. "You look confident?"
Damian looked at him quietly. "I have participated in this conference with only one goal, and that is to win this conference."
The words were simple, but the moment they fell, the atmosphere on the stage tightened.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Kaiden moved first.
"Void Genesis Art, Empty Step."

His figure vanished without disturbing the air. In the same instant, dozens of folded spatial ripples appeared around Damian. Some hovered above him, some waited beneath his feet, some lurked behind his shoulders, and some sat beside his sword arm. They did not attack immediately. They merely opened like hidden mouths, waiting for the exact moment to release their killing force.
Damian drew his sword.
"Silent Sword Art, First Cut, Parting Wind."

A single slash swept outward. The slash looked simple, yet every ripple it touched was cut apart before it could fully unfold. Seven spatial folds broke at the same time, and the lines hiding within them vanished as though they had been severed from their source.
Kaiden appeared far to the left with one palm raised.
"Void Genesis Art, Sevenfold Severing Line."

Seven invisible spatial cuts shot toward Damian from seven different layers. Unlike an ordinary blade attack, these lines did not travel through normal distance. They arrived by folding space around Damian and appearing directly beside his body.
Damian’s sword moved.
"Silent Sword Art, Returning Thread."

His blade flashed in a narrow arc. Three severing lines were cut apart, two were redirected into the ground, and one passed by his shoulder without touching him. The final line reached his chest, but Damian’s sword tip struck it directly and shattered it into silver-gray fragments.
Kaiden’s eyes sharpened. He had expected Damian to defend, but he had not expected him to cut the spatial lines with such accuracy from the very first exchange.
Damian looked at him calmly. "Again."
Kaiden did not answer. His hands rose, and the entire stage split into overlapping planes.
"Void Genesis Art, Thousand-Layer Spatial Cage."

The space around Damian folded again and again, forming a transparent prison without walls. Each layer shifted at a different angle, and each angle changed the direction of movement inside the cage. If Damian stepped forward, the distance would stretch. If he stepped back, the ground would fold under him. If he slashed, the sword light would be redirected into an empty plane. This technique had trapped many opponents before they could understand what had happened.
Damian lifted his sword with both hands.
"Sword God Palace, Falling Peak Sword."
The sword descended.
Boom!

A mountain-like sword force struck the Thousand-Layer Spatial Cage from within. The first dozens of layers trembled but did not break. The remaining layers turned the sword force sideways, trying to disperse it through folded planes, but Damian’s eyes remained still. His sword pressed deeper.
"Falling Peak Sword, Second Descent."
Another wave of sword force fell, and then a third.
"Falling Peak Sword, Third Descent."
Crack!
The spatial cage shattered layer by layer.
Kaiden’s expression grew more serious. "You are not only cutting the surface."
Damian stepped out of the collapsing cage. "The surface is meaningless."

The two vanished at the same time. Kaiden stepped through folded corridors while Damian advanced through straight sword movement. One moved by twisting space, and the other moved by cutting the shortest line through it. Their figures crossed the stage again and again, and the silver-gray spatial ripples and pale sword lights flashed so quickly that ordinary spectators could no longer follow their positions.
"Void Genesis Art, Hollow Displacement."
Kaiden’s body shifted away from reality, and Damian’s sword passed through his afterimage.
"Grand Void Sanctum, Reverse Corridor Palm."
A palm strike emerged from behind Damian instead of from Kaiden’s visible position. Damian’s eyes shifted slightly.
"Crosswind Return."
His sword turned backward without his body turning, and the blade met the palm strike behind him.
Boom!
The impact spread in a ring of folded space and broken sword light.
Kaiden appeared above Damian next.
"Void Genesis Art, Space Burial Palm."
The space around Damian sank like a tomb. Damian raised his sword upward.
"Heaven-Cutting Ascension."

A straight sword light pierced through the burial field and split the sinking space from bottom to top. Kaiden retreated through a folded path, but Damian’s sword light followed the path for a short distance and cut open his sleeve. A thin line of blood appeared on Kaiden’s arm.
The Grand Void Sanctum disciples grew tense.
"He wounded Senior Brother Kaiden."
"Damian’s sword is following the folds."
"That should not be easy."
At the Sword God Palace, the disciples watched with burning eyes.
"Senior Brother Damian can cut space."
"No, he is cutting the path hidden inside space."
"That is even more terrifying."
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the top geniuses grew serious.
Rakan Thorne crossed his arms and frowned. "I hate this one too. I cannot even tell where Kaiden is standing."
Orion Starfall smiled weakly. "That is the point. If you could tell, he would not be Kaiden."
Revona watched quietly, her Void Origin Eyes faintly glowing. "Damian is not trying to understand every corridor. He is cutting the route that carries Kaiden’s intent."
Ervin nodded. "That is why the sword is dangerous."

paragraphs: Max stood on his pillar with focused eyes. He had defeated Kaiden with the Void Genesis Art, but Damian was approaching the battle from a completely different direction. Max’s advantage had been mastery and immunity. Damian had neither.

He was not immune to spatial attacks, and he did not understand the Void Genesis Art as Kaiden did. Yet his sword path was so pure and precise that it could cut through the meaningful line behind Kaiden’s movements. That made him frightening in another way entirely.

On the stage, Kaiden’s aura finally changed. Silver-gray light expanded behind him, and the entire battlefield began twisting into a vast spatial maze. Corridors rose from the ground, mirrors opened in the air, and walls of folded distance appeared and vanished. Exile points flickered at the edge of sight while hidden blades of space moved between planes.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path."
Kaiden’s voice rang across the arena.
"Grand Void Labyrinth."
Boom!

The stage became a labyrinth of folded space. Damian stood within it, surrounded by countless corridors and mirror routes. Every direction looked real, and every path looked false. Even the sky above him had been divided into layers, and every layer could become an attack route, an escape route, or an exile route at any moment.
Kaiden’s figure appeared in a distant corridor. "Damian Voss," he said calmly, "if your sword can cut through this, then cut."
The Grand Void Labyrinth activated.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Corridor of Ten Thousand Cuts."
Countless invisible cuts emerged from all directions. Damian’s sword moved instantly.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, First Edict, All Blades Refuse Submission."

The sword world appeared behind him. An ancient sword altar rose within a vast sword heaven, and countless sword lights answered Damian’s blade. The first wave of spatial cuts was shattered before reaching him, but Kaiden’s attack did not end there.

The cuts arrived from delayed corridors, hidden mirrors, and folded paths that had not existed a breath earlier. One cut grazed Damian’s sleeve, another tore across his shoulder, and a third left a faint wound on his cheek.
Damian’s expression did not change.
Kaiden’s voice echoed again.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Mirror Burial."

Dozens of mirrored spaces appeared around Damian, each reflecting him from a different angle. Then the mirrors collapsed inward, trying to bury him inside false spatial layers. At the same time, Kaiden used the collapsing mirrors to hide his true attack.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Backflow Severance."
A silver-gray blade emerged from behind Damian’s reflection and struck toward his back. Damian’s eyes sharpened.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Second Edict, One Sword Divides Heaven."

One sword light swept outward. The mirrors split, the false layers split, and the Backflow Severance blade split as well. The sword light continued through the labyrinth and cut open three corridors at once, forcing Kaiden to step out from a distant fold.
Kaiden looked down at the torn edge of his robe, and then he smiled faintly. "As expected."
Damian lowered his sword slightly. "Your labyrinth is impressive."
Kaiden’s eyes grew deeper. "It is not finished yet."
The Grand Void Labyrinth began to rotate.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Infinite Corridor Rotation."

Every path around Damian changed position. The corridor behind him became the sky, and the mirror above him became the ground. The wall on his right became a blade, and the blade on his left became an exile gate. The entire labyrinth moved like a living spatial beast, constantly reshaping its own organs to confuse its prey.
Damian’s sword lights began missing, and for the first time, Kaiden started gaining a visible advantage. A spatial cut struck Damian’s arm. A folded palm force hit his shoulder.

An exile ripple brushed past his leg and nearly dragged him into a side corridor. Kaiden moved faster and faster within the Grand Void Labyrinth, no longer standing in one route long enough to be caught.
His attacks came from present space, delayed space, mirrored space, and reversed space. No single attack was enough to defeat Damian on its own, but together they began to pressure him heavily.
The Sword God Palace disciples grew tense.
"Senior Brother Damian is being pushed."
"Kaiden’s labyrinth changes too quickly."
"Can even Sword Sovereign Heaven keep cutting if the path keeps moving?"

Damian stopped in place. A silver-gray blade shot toward his throat, and he cut it apart. Another emerged from beneath his feet, and he stepped aside and severed it. A third appeared behind him, and he cut backward without turning.
Then ten more came, and then a hundred. Damian’s robe was cut in several places, and blood appeared on his arm and shoulder, yet his grip on the sword did not loosen at all.
Kaiden’s figure appeared above him through a folded corridor.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, World Exile Coffin."

Six massive spatial walls appeared around Damian, closing in from above, from below, and from all four sides. Each wall contained countless folded planes leading away from the battlefield. If the coffin sealed completely, Damian would be exiled into a space where even his sword would have to cut through countless layers before returning.
Damian looked up as the walls closed.
Kaiden pressed both hands downward. "Seal."

The World Exile Coffin descended. Damian finally raised his sword vertically before him, and the Sword Sovereign Heaven behind him changed. The ancient sword altar grew brighter. The sword palace above it appeared, and the empty throne within the palace released a faint glow.
Damian’s voice remained calm.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Third Edict."
The sword in his hand hummed.
"The sword does not follow distance."

He slashed, and a single straight line appeared within the World Exile Coffin. That line cut through the first spatial wall, then the second, and then the third. The fourth wall tried to fold the sword light away, but the sword light cut through the fold itself. The fifth wall opened an exile path, but the sword line severed the path’s destination. The sixth wall compressed inward, only to be split from its center.
Crack!
The World Exile Coffin shattered. Kaiden’s eyes widened slightly.
Damian stepped out with his aura sharper than before. "Your space changes many paths," Damian said. "But every path has a point where it begins."
Kaiden’s face turned solemn.
Damian raised his sword. "I only need to cut that."

The pressure of Sword Sovereign Heaven rose. Kaiden realized that Damian had adapted. At the beginning, Damian had cut attacks. Then he had cut routes. Now he was starting to cut the origin points of the spatial changes themselves. If this continued, the Grand Void Labyrinth would lose its advantage entirely.

Kaiden drew a deep breath, and the entire labyrinth condensed. Every corridor, mirror, folded path, and exile point began gathering toward one final silver-gray passage. The space behind Damian darkened into a terrifying tunnel that seemed to lead beyond the battlefield, beyond the Eternal Hourglass, and beyond return.
The spectators grew silent, because they had seen this move before. It was the technique that had almost defeated Revona.
"Grand Void Labyrinth, Final Corridor."
Kaiden’s hands trembled slightly as he formed the deepest route of his Pseudo Cosmic Path.
"Void Beyond Return."
The final corridor opened beneath Damian’s feet, and the space around him vanished downward. Damian’s body began to sink.
The Sword God Palace disciples shouted in alarm.
"Senior Brother Damian!"
The Grand Void Sanctum disciples clenched their fists.
"Seal him!"
"Void Beyond Return!"
Even the top geniuses grew focused.

chapters.title: Chapter 1898: Max vs Orion!
paragraphs: Damian sank to his knees, and then to his waist. The corridor tried to remove him from the battlefield entirely. It did not attack his body. It attacked his position, his presence, and the route connecting him to the stage. If it succeeded, even his Sword Sovereign Heaven would be forced to cut through endless folded exits to return.
Kaiden pressed harder. "Go."

Damian looked down at the darkness below him, and then he closed his eyes. For a breath, the sword in his hand became silent, and the Sword Sovereign Heaven behind him fell silent as well. Then the single sword hanging before the empty throne descended, and the entire sword world seemed to hold its breath.
Damian opened his eyes.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven."
The sword before the throne dissolved into light and entered his blade.
"Final Edict."
The labyrinth trembled.
"Throne Of The Only Sword."

In that instant, every sword light vanished. The sword altar vanished, the sword mountains vanished, and the sword rivers vanished. Even the palace behind Damian dimmed. Only one sword remained, the sword in Damian’s hand, and because only one sword remained, every other direction lost its meaning before it.
Damian slashed downward. The slash entered the Void Beyond Return.
For a moment, nothing happened. Then the final corridor cracked.
Kaiden’s face changed. "No."

The crack spread through the corridor. It did not spread along the surface. It spread along the hidden route of exile, cutting through the very connection that made the path lead away from the battlefield. The Void Beyond Return tried to deepen itself, but Damian’s sword had already found the line that mattered. The destination was cut, the returnless nature was cut, and the exile authority was cut. The corridor shattered.
Boom!

Damian stepped out of the collapsing void with his sword still lowered. The Grand Void Labyrinth shook violently. Kaiden tried to move, but Damian was already gone. A straight sword line crossed the labyrinth. No corridor delayed it, no mirror diverted it, and no folded plane swallowed it. The sword line cut through the center of the Grand Void Labyrinth and arrived before Kaiden.

Kaiden opened three emergency folds, and Damian cut through them. Kaiden formed a Hollow Displacement, and Damian severed the displaced position. Kaiden raised a World-Folding Barrier, and Damian’s blade pierced through it. Then the sword stopped at Kaiden’s throat.

The entire arena went silent. Kaiden stood still. His silver-gray robes were torn, his aura was unstable, and the Grand Void Labyrinth behind him cracked layer by layer before finally collapsing into countless fading fragments of space.

He had given everything. He had shown the full depth of his spatial path. He had trapped Damian, wounded him, nearly exiled him, and forced him to use the Final Edict of Sword Sovereign Heaven. But in the end, Damian’s sword had cut through space itself.
Kaiden looked at the blade before his throat, and then he looked at Damian. After a few breaths, he smiled faintly. "You cut the Void Beyond Return."
Damian’s expression remained calm. "Barely."
Kaiden shook his head lightly. "Barely is still enough."
He lowered his hands. "I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Kaiden Voidmere Defeated.]
The screen above the arena updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Damian Voss]
[Total Battles Fought: 20]
[Total Wins: 20]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Kaiden Voidmere]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 18]
The Divine Realm erupted. Damian Voss had completed all twenty-four battles with twenty-four victories.

The Sword God Palace fell into thunderous celebration. Countless swords rose from their sheaths, and their cries echoed through mountains, halls, and floating sword platforms. Their strongest genius had not merely won another battle. He had ended the full round-robin stage undefeated, cutting down divine light, body power, curses, and now the Grand Void Labyrinth of the Grand Void Sanctum.

At the Grand Void Sanctum, the disciples were silent, yet none of them lowered their heads in shame. Kaiden had fought beautifully. His space power had pushed Damian further than most opponents, and even in defeat he had proven once again that his place among the top monsters was unquestionable.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Damian lowered his sword and stepped back. Kaiden gave him a slight nod.
"The Sword God Palace deserves its name."
Damian sheathed his blade. "So does the Grand Void Sanctum."
The transfer light descended and returned both of them to their pillars.
Max watched Damian quietly. Twenty-four battles and twenty-four wins. Damian Voss had finished his round, and his sword still felt as though it had more to show.

After Damian defeated Kaiden and returned to his pillar with twenty-four victories to his name, the pressure inside the Eternal Hourglass rose to an even more frightening level. Everyone understood that the final competitive stage had entered its final stretch, and from this point onward, almost every battle that appeared on the screen would carry the weight to shake the entire Divine Realm.

Angelina Valerius gave the arena only a brief moment to settle. The broken traces of Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth disappeared, the stage restored itself under the laws of the Eternal Hourglass, and then the great screen of light above the battlefield began to spin once more.

This time, even before the first name appeared, many spectators had already begun holding their breath. The top monsters remaining had grown too few, and any pairing among them was enough to make the blood of the crowd heat up.
The first name slowed and stopped.
[Max Morgan]
A wave of noise rose instantly. The second name continued rotating through the light, passing several surviving participants before finally slowing as well.
[Orion Starfall]
The moment both names appeared together, the Eternal Hourglass erupted.
[Final Competitive Stage]
[Max Morgan vs Orion Starfall]

All across the Divine Realm, countless viewing grounds, sect halls, clan plazas, floating platforms, mountain palaces, and inheritance chambers burst into excitement. The Black Dragon Clan disciples straightened immediately. The Nine Star Court fell unusually quiet for a moment before its disciples began watching with burning eyes.
Even many elders from the seven strongest first-rate forces leaned forward slightly, because everyone knew this was no ordinary battle.

Max Morgan, who had risen from the mortal world and continued shocking the Divine Realm without pause, was now facing Orion Starfall, the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court, a man who had proven again and again that even when injured or cornered, his will to fight only grew more terrifying.

On his pillar, Orion stood up immediately, and his bright smile returned at once. That smile carried no fear, no hesitation, and no trace of gloom from his previous battles. If anything, he looked more alive than before.
"So it is finally my turn," Orion said with a laugh as he looked toward Max. "I have been waiting for this battle for a long time."
Max met his gaze from across the arena and smiled faintly. "I know," he said calmly. "You have been looking at me with battle intent for quite a while now."

Orion jumped down from his pillar as the beam of transfer light descended around him. "You are right," he replied, still smiling. "Because among everyone here, you are one of the few who truly make me feel excited."
Max stepped into his own beam of light and appeared on the central stage opposite him. "You should be excited," Max said. "I am not easy to fight."
Orion laughed loudly. "Good. If you were easy, I would be disappointed."

The crowd’s excitement only rose further at that exchange. Max stood with Dragonheart still sheathed, his white hair drifting lightly in the wind generated by the arena’s formations. Orion stood opposite him in dark-gold battle armor marked with stars, and even before the battle began, the air between them already felt heavy enough to crack.

chapters.title: Chapter 1899: Orion Going All Out!
paragraphs: Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]

The instant the battle started, Orion did not waste even a breath. He did not test Max, he did not throw a basic star attack, and he did not try to read the battlefield first. He went straight to his strongest state from the very beginning, because he knew better than most people here that anything less would be meaningless in front of Max Morgan.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body."

The sky above the stage changed. Nine stars appeared at once, each shining in a different color and carrying a different pressure. Silver, gold, crimson, azure, white, violet, black, green, and deep blood-red all lit up together, and before the crowd could fully appreciate the scene, all nine stars descended into Orion’s body one after another.
Boom!

His aura exploded, and the ground beneath his feet cracked. The muscles in his body tightened, the star marks on his armor lit up violently, and his eyes shone with a dazzling stellar brilliance, as if miniature galaxies had been lit inside them.

But Orion still did not stop there. He raised both hands, and the phantom of an ancient star palace appeared behind him, majestic and endless, while all nine stars within his body began revolving at terrifying speed.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path," Orion said, and for the first time since the battle was announced, even his smile gained a solemn edge. "Full Star Convergence."

The arena trembled. This was no simple technique, and it was not a single attack. The moment Full Star Convergence descended, the power of the nine stars no longer remained separate within Orion’s body.

It began fusing into his blood, his flesh, his bones, his veins, and his spirit, turning his already terrifying Nine Star Sovereign Body into something far more monstrous. In that moment, Orion no longer looked like a genius who specialized in long-range star techniques. He looked like a supreme close-combat tyrant carrying the power of an entire star court inside his body.
Rakan Thorne grinned from his pillar. "Good. That idiot did not hold back."
Morgana Starveil narrowed her eyes slightly. "Straight to the peak state from the start. He really has no intention of saving anything."
Revona watched in silence. Damian Voss also studied the stage carefully.
Max, however, only smiled. "That is more like it."
The next moment, Orion vanished. He did not move like an ordinary body cultivator. He exploded.
"First Star Impact!"

His fist arrived before Max’s chest almost instantly, carrying the crushing weight of a falling star. Max’s right hand rose and blocked. He also directly opened the first Divine Vein - Vein of Origin.
Boom!
A heavy shockwave spread across the stage, and the arena barrier rippled. Before the force from the first impact had fully dispersed, Orion was already gone again.
"Third Star Split!"

This time his elbow descended from above with enough force to split a mountain range. Max took half a step back and let the elbow brush past his shoulder, but before he could counter, Orion’s knee had already risen from below.
"Fifth Star Ascending Break!"
Max blocked again, and another violent shockwave burst outward.

The crowd shouted in excitement. Orion allowed no breathing room. Fully aware that letting Max settle into rhythm would make the battle harder, he pressed on without pause and attacked from every angle with the power of converged stars.

His fists, elbows, knees, and shoulders all became terrifying weapons, and each movement carried the pressure of a different star. One was crushing, one was piercing, one was explosive, one was twisting, and one was suppressive. Together they formed a close-combat storm powerful enough to overwhelm most geniuses in only a few breaths.

Max blocked several strikes barehanded at first. He even matched Orion in close combat for a short stretch, and that alone shocked countless people, because after seeing Orion enter Full Star Convergence, most had expected him to force even Max onto the defensive immediately.
But then Max smiled a little more deeply. "Not bad," he said.
Then Dragonheart came out. The sword cried once as it left its sheath, and in the next instant it met Orion’s descending fist.
Clang!
The metallic impact shook the stage.
Orion grinned brightly. "Now it begins."
He pressed forward again.
"Seventh Star Crushing Descent!"

Max answered with a horizontal slash. The sword and fist collided, and sparks of sword light and star light exploded between them. Orion slid back a short distance before charging again, and this time his attacks no longer came as isolated moves. They came as a complete martial sequence empowered by all nine stars within him.

His left fist carried the First Star. His right knee shifted into the Fourth. His shoulder impact changed to the Eighth. His palm strike fused the Third and Seventh. The speed at which he changed star attributes throughout his body made him look like a celestial war machine.

Max’s sword began moving faster. He did not release any major external power yet. He simply used Dragonheart and pure swordsmanship to answer Orion’s storm of close-combat attacks, but even that made the crowd uneasy, because Max was doing far more than barely keeping up.
He was already reading Orion’s changes, blocking some, redirecting others, cutting through the force of several, and even counterattacking whenever he found a gap.
Still, Orion was too powerful to suppress with ordinary swordsmanship alone.
"Starfall Spiral Fist!"
He spun and drove a rotating star fist toward Max with enough force to blow apart the ground beneath them. Max blocked with Dragonheart, but the impact still pushed him a short distance backward.
Orion’s smile widened at once. "Good!" he shouted. "You really can take it!"

Max steadied his footing. Then the expression on his face slowly changed. The smile remained, but the atmosphere around him became deathly calm. Dragonheart lowered slightly, and a silent, eerie sword aura spread out from him.

The lively pressure created by Orion’s stars suddenly felt as though it had entered a much colder world, one where the air itself carried a severing edge that aimed not merely at flesh or force, but at the invisible connections behind them.
Max raised Dragonheart.
"Emotion Severing Path."
The moment those words left his mouth, the noise around the arena seemed to dim for a breath.
Orion’s eyes sharpened immediately. He had seen this power before, and he had heard enough about it from others. But seeing it from the stage itself was different.

The Full Star Convergence inside his body was still raging, yet when Max’s Emotion Severing Path spread across the battlefield, Orion could feel a strange pressure touching not his flesh but the rhythm behind his power, as though that cold and silent sword aura wanted to cut the emotional force, intent, and momentum that allowed his star convergence to shine so fiercely.
Max stepped forward. One slash came, and it was silent. It was too silent.
Orion answered with "Ninth Star Crown Fist," condensing all his gathered momentum into one direct collision.
Boom!

Sword and fist met. The stage beneath their feet shattered into a wide crater, and the arena shook violently. But while Orion’s fist remained terrifyingly strong, the star intent supporting the strike was clearly shaken. Max’s severing aura had not merely clashed with the outer power. It had bitten into the rhythm of the star force itself.
Orion retreated three steps, then laughed. "So this is what it feels like directly."
He took another breath, then exploded forward again. This time he used everything.
"First Star Impact!"
"Third Star Split!"
"Sixth Star Heaven Drive!"
"Eighth Star Ruin Break!"

Each attack came stronger than the last, and Max answered each one with Dragonheart, sometimes blocking, sometimes cutting, sometimes redirecting, and sometimes meeting them with direct sword strikes that split even the air around them.

The battle grew fierce. Orion’s Full Star Convergence made him terrifying in close combat. He attacked like a man wearing the sky itself as armor and wielding the collapse of stars in every movement. Yet Max’s Emotion Severing Path made every collision dangerous for him in a different way.

chapters.title: Chapter 1900: Ervin vs Morgana!
paragraphs: The more they clashed, the more Orion could feel that Max’s sword was not only attacking his body but also trying to cut apart the battle intent, momentum, and converged star rhythm that allowed him to chain one brutal attack into another.

Still, Orion refused to yield. His injuries from earlier battles, the strain of Full Star Convergence, and the pressure of the Emotion Severing Path all gathered together, but instead of weakening his spirit, they seemed to force him into an even more desperate brilliance.
He leapt back once and raised both hands.
"Nine Star Sovereign Body, Starfall Extinction!"

The ancient star palace behind him trembled, and all nine stars within his body burned to their peak. A massive stellar force gathered around his right arm, layer after layer and star after star, until his whole arm looked as though it carried the collapse of a miniature cosmos.
The crowd was stunned. He was using that technique again, and from the beginning state of Full Star Convergence.
Orion appeared before Max like a falling comet. "Take this, Max!"

The fist came down. Max looked at the incoming attack calmly, and then his eyes grew colder. The Emotion Severing Path around Dragonheart deepened. He gripped the sword with both hands and brought it down in a single decisive slash.
"Sever."

The two attacks collided. For one breath, the arena went white with star light and dark-gray severing force. Then a crack appeared. It was not in the stage, and it was not in the barrier. It was in the star force itself.

Max’s Emotion Severing Path had cut into the converged will behind Orion’s Starfall Extinction, severing the furious upward battle spirit that held its star layers together. The moment that invisible support cracked, the immense stellar force began collapsing unevenly.

Orion’s eyes widened. Max’s slash continued. The star fist broke apart, the star layers shattered, and the stellar pressure split in two. Then Max’s figure passed through the broken light and appeared before Orion. Dragonheart stopped before his throat.

The entire arena fell silent. Orion stood frozen. The glow of Full Star Convergence around his body flickered once, then again, and then finally dimmed. He tried to steady himself, but the overuse of his Pseudo Cosmic Path and the destruction of Starfall Extinction had already drained too much of his strength.
For a few breaths, he simply stared at the sword before his throat. Then he laughed. It was not a bitter laugh. It was bright, honest, and filled with excitement even in defeat.
"You really are ridiculous," Orion said, breathing heavily. "I used my Full Star Convergence from the beginning, and you still cut through everything."
Max lowered Dragonheart slightly. "You forced me to take out my sword and use the Emotion Severing Path seriously from the start," Max replied. "That is enough to show your strength."
Orion shook his head and smiled helplessly. "That sounds like comfort."
"It is not."
Orion looked at him for a moment, then laughed again and finally raised both hands in surrender. "I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Orion Starfall Defeated.]
The great screen above the arena changed immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 21]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Orion Starfall]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 18]

The Divine Realm erupted once more. At the Black Dragon Clan, disciples shouted with excitement, some in pure joy, some in disbelief, and some with a pride that had long since surpassed their earlier expectations. Lady Virelia looked at the screen with bright eyes and a faint smile, while several elders exchanged astonished glances. Across the seven great families tied to the Black Dragon Clan, many leaders who had once only hoped Max would perform well in the Cosmic Ascension Conference now had no choice but to admit that he had become one of the most terrifying young geniuses in the entire Divine Realm.

At the Nine Star Court, the disciples were disappointed but not ashamed. Orion had gone all out from the beginning, and no one who watched that battle could say he had performed poorly. He had attacked with the courage and brilliance worthy of the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court.
On the stage, Orion let out a long breath. "I lost," he said simply, though his smile never faded. "But that was fun."
Max sheathed Dragonheart. "You are one of the best opponents here."
Orion grinned. "Good. Then next time, I will force even more from you."
Max smiled faintly. "I will wait."

The transfer light descended and returned both of them to their pillars. The battle had ended. Max Morgan remained undefeated, and with each battle, the final competitive stage moved closer to its true deciding point.

After Max defeated Orion, the atmosphere inside the Eternal Hourglass remained heated for a long time. Orion returned to his pillar with a tired but satisfied smile, his star armor cracked, his aura unstable, and his body still trembling from the backlash of using Full Star Convergence and Starfall Extinction against Max.

Yet no one looked down on him. He had known from the beginning that anything below his Pseudo Cosmic Path would be useless, so he had burned everything from the first breath. He had forced Max to draw Dragonheart and use the Emotion Severing Path seriously, and for someone who had already suffered through battles against Revona, Ervin, and Aurelian, that result alone was enough to make the Nine Star Court proud.
Max returned to his own pillar calmly. His record now stood at twenty-four battles and twenty-four victories, the same as Damian Voss. But the final competitive stage had not truly ended.

The battle count and record projection above the arena began shifting, and several names continued rotating through the final remaining matchups. Some participants had already finished all their battles, while a few important names still had several pairings left. The Eternal Hourglass gave no one special treatment.
Those who had not yet crossed paths would still be matched, and only after every necessary result had been recorded would the final ranking become complete.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand again.
"The final competitive stage will continue."
The next few battles came quickly.
[Revona vs Fin Arclight]

Fin Arclight stepped into the arena with a grim expression. He knew Revona was one of the worst possible opponents for him, but surrendering without trying would be too shameful for someone who had already reached this stage.

The moment the battle began, he opened Pale Eclipse Burial and tried to cover the entire stage in moonless darkness. Pale eclipse light spread outward, suppressing sight, sound, rhythm, and direction, while the Moonless Descent blade formed silently above Revona’s head.

Revona looked up once. The Void Origin Eyes opened fully, and the Moonless Descent blade faded before it could fall. Fin immediately shifted positions and used "Pale Eclipse Burial, Eclipse Shadow Division," creating several pale afterimages that attacked from different angles, but Revona’s gaze followed the true source of each strike.

One by one, the pale shadows vanished. When Fin tried to compress the eclipse field and launch one final attack, Revona opened a small portion of the Void Origin Realm and hollowed the center of the field before it could collapse around her.
Fin lowered his blade and surrendered.
[Winner: Revona.]
[Fin Arclight Defeated.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 21]
[Total Wins: 21]

The result caused little surprise. Revona’s strength had already been proven repeatedly, and after defeating Orion, Rakan, and Kaiden, no one expected Fin to be the one to break her undefeated record.
The next important match came after several faster results among the lower-ranked participants.
[Ervin vs Morgana Starveil]

Morgana entered the stage with a faint smile, but her eyes were extremely serious. Her Star-Curse Labyrinth was one of the most troublesome Pseudo Cosmic Paths among the top twenty-five, yet Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent had already swallowed too many different types of authority. She did not waste time with small curses.
The moment the battle began, the Star-Curse Labyrinth opened, and violet-black mirrors filled the stage, each one carrying a different misfortune, binding, or distortion curse.
